request.text:
{"body":" 「意味を壊すSVG」= semantic data自体は正しいのに、projectionが人間へ違う意味を伝えるSVG です。

例	semantic data	壊れたSVGが伝える誤解

edge接続先ズレ	A→B	A→Cに見える
矢印反転	A→B	B→Aに見える
containment崩れ	package ∋ model	modelがpackage外に見える
sequence順序逆転	A→B→C	C→B→Aに見える
node重なり	AとBは別物	1つのentityに見える
label切れ/消失	approved	状態不明・別状態に見える
set重なり崩れ	A∩Bあり	排他的に見える
map位置ズレ	点Pは領域A	領域B所属に見える
大小/位置の誤投影	value A > B	B > Aに見える


現在のrepoには graph / seq / set / map のprojectionがあるため、これは今後かなり現実的な故障です。既存semantic diffでは 「元データは変わっていない」 としか分かりません。

なのでShift-Leftとして欲しいのは単なる「SVGが変わった」ではなく、

semantic invariants
      +
SVG visual regression
      ↓
「意味を壊す可能性のある描画変更」を早期検出

です。

特に強いのは semanticが同一なのにSVG diffが出た場合。renderer変更による意味破壊候補として即redにできます。

ただしpixel diffだけでは「意味を壊した」と断定できません。候補検出＝SVG diff、意味保証＝semantic invariant の二段構えが一番合っています。"}

{"body":"## Purpose
Persist every worker decision and adapter output as append-only JSONL so answers, failures, and sessions remain readable after the terminal is gone.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Establishes `worker -> events.jsonl` as evidence. |
| product | Makes worker runs durable and testable. |
| system/org | Solves the “agent answer not visible later” problem. |
| business/meta | Creates artifacts suitable for review and handoff. |

## Scope
- Write `started`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `completed`, `failed`, and `blocked` events.
- Include run id, instruction id, target, timestamp, and source refs.

## Non-scope
- UI rendering.
- Adapter-specific output parsing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every worker branch emits a structured event.
- [ ] Failures are represented as JSONL rows, not only stderr.
- [ ] Event rows can be replayed to explain one run.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Agent final answer exists only in terminal scrollback.
- [ ] Worker crash leaves no event explaining the last decision.

## Evidence
- Event fixture and tests.

## Merge condition
Merge only when worker behavior is durable by default."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Let a selected node or edge in localhost UI become the current Vim/hq modeling target.

## Completion state

This is complete when UI selection can be written as a local `ui.targetRef.v1`-compatible file and Vim/hq completion can read it to narrow commands.

## Scope

- Define `.local/current-target.json`.
- Add targetRef read/write helpers.
- Include digest/version to detect stale targetRefs.
- Let hq completion read the current target.
- Keep UI selection as non-authority projection state.

## Local files

| path | Role |
|---|---|
| `.local/current-target.json` | Current selected targetRef |
| `.local/current-context.json` | Optional surrounding context |
| `.local/current-target.receipt.jsonl` | Optional target bridge receipts |

## Done checklist

- [ ] UI selection can be represented as targetRef.
- [ ] TargetRef can be written locally.
- [ ] Vim/hq can read the targetRef.
- [ ] TargetRef changes command suggestions.
- [ ] Stale projection digest/version is detected.
- [ ] Commands still work without targetRef where valid.
- [ ] UI selection is explicitly not authority.
- [ ] Browser cannot directly write accepted ledger.

## Non-scope

- Full UI hot reload.
- Queue worker.
- Admission."}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose
Read recent Herdr agent/pane output from JSONL instructions and persist the observed output as worker events.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Solves “I did not watch the TUI” for Herdr sessions. |
| product | Makes Herdr observable from the worker ledger. |
| system/org | Separates operation from readback. |
| business/meta | Preserves agent output as review evidence. |

## Scope
- Implement read operation for Herdr agent/pane recent output.
- Store read output in result events linked to run/session ids.

## Non-scope
- Interactive attach.
- Long-running observe stream.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Read instruction produces structured output event.
- [ ] Read can target stored Herdr session refs.
- [ ] Empty/missing session is reported as structured failure.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Output can only be seen by opening Herdr UI.
- [ ] Read output is not linked to a run/session id.

## Evidence
- Read fixture/proof.
- Event log sample.

## Merge condition
Merge only when Herdr output is recoverable without watching the TUI."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Improve the repo map semantic LOD so zooming in increases detail while preserving map-like global context.

Current implementation is focus-only:

```text
z < 24:
  all repos

24 <= z < 66:
  focus repo + packages only

z >= 66:
  focus package neighborhood + models only
```

This proves containment, but it loses map context. A map should not make the rest of the world disappear when zooming into one area.

## Current behavior

| z | current visible nodes | issue |
|---:|---|---|
| far | all repos | OK |
| middle | focus repo + its packages | other repos disappear |
| near | focus package neighborhood + models | other repos and most packages disappear |

## Desired behavior

Zoom should increase semantic detail without deleting the world context.

Expected behavior:

```text
far:
  all repos visible

middle:
  all repos remain as context
  focus repo shows packages as detail

near:
  all repos remain as context
  focus repo remains visible
  packages remain as context/detail
  focus package shows models as detail
```

## Invariant

This invariant remains unchanged:

```text
repo = packages[]
package = models[]
```

The visual map must preserve containment:

```text
repo rect
  package rect[]
    model rect[]
```

## Required architecture boundary

Keep the existing boundary:

```text
JSONL data
  -> CRUD event contract
  -> model graph reducer
  -> projection / LOD reducer
  -> coordinate-preserving SVG renderer
  -> svg-pan-zoom camera adapter
```

`svg-pan-zoom` remains camera-only.

## Required projection policy

Projection should distinguish:

```text
detail
context
hidden
```

Suggested node projection fields:

```text
visibilityRole:
  detail | context

interactionRole:
  active | passive

labelRole:
  full | short | hidden
```

These are projection/view fields, not source model fields.

## Required visual behavior

### z=far

- all repo rectangles are visible.
- package/model nodes are hidden.
- map is not empty.
- global layout is visible.

### z=middle

- all repo rectangles remain visible as context.
- focus repo remains visually stronger.
- focus repo packages are visible as detail.
- non-focus repo packages may remain hidden.
- non-focus repos must not disappear.
- package rectangles are inside focus repo rect.

### z=near

- all repo rectangles remain visible as context.
- focus repo remains visible.
- focus package and nearby packages are visible.
- models inside focus package are visible as detail.
- model rectangles are inside package rect.
- labels are screen-stable.
- focus detail is readable.
- context nodes do not overpower detail nodes.

## Edge policy

- Do not show all edges at all z levels.
- Far view may show no edges or only aggregate repo edges.
- Middle view may show focus repo/package edges.
- Near view may show selected-neighborhood model edges.
- Context nodes may remain visible without their edges.
- Avoid misleading long edge spaghetti.

## Product UI policy

No new product controls.

Allowed:

```text
-
+
fit
```

Forbidden:

```text
repo button row
z debug text
HUD
debug switches
count-only proof UI
```

## E2E requirements

E2E must prove context preservation, not only detail containment.

Required checks:

### z=far

- repo count >= total repo count.
- package count = 0.
- model count = 0.

### z=middle

- visible repo count >= total repo count.
- focus repo package count >= expected package count.
- non-focus repo context count >= total repo count - 1.
- package rects are inside focus repo rect.
- model count = 0.

### z=near

- visible repo count >= total repo count.
- focus package visible.
- focus package model count >= expected model count.
- model rects are inside focus package rect.
- focus repo remains visible.
- context repo rectangles remain visible.
- labels are not huge or clipped.

### mobile

- no horizontal overflow.
- context remains visible.
- focus detail is visible.
- labels do not explode.
- screenshot is not blank.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `repo = packages[]` and `package = models[]` remain documented.
- [ ] JSONL data format does not become renderer-specific.
- [ ] `svg-pan-zoom` remains camera-only.
- [ ] LOD reducer supports context/detail projection.
- [ ] z=middle keeps non-focus repos visible.
- [ ] z=near keeps repo context visible.
- [ ] package/model containment still passes.
- [ ] edge visibility remains bounded.
- [ ] product UI remains only `-`, `+`, `fit`.
- [ ] desktop screenshots pass z=far/middle/near.
- [ ] mobile screenshots pass z=far/middle/near.
- [ ] generated standalone HTML exists.
- [ ] CI uploads artifact and runtime report.
- [ ] generated HTML remains evidence, not authority.

## Non-scope

- No G6 retry.
- No MSAGL retry.
- No tldraw spike.
- No Canvas/WebGL migration.
- No map tile library.
- No new state store.
- No broad A2UI rewrite.
- No source model rewrite.
- No edge bundling implementation unless required by test failure.

## Merge condition

Merge only if zooming in increases detail while preserving map context.

Count-only pass is not enough.

## Merge-blocking conditions

- focus outside repos disappear at middle/near zoom.
- model/package containment breaks.
- labels explode under semantic focus.
- context nodes overpower detail nodes.
- all edges are shown at once.
- mobile view becomes blank or horizontally overflowing.
- `svg-pan-zoom` starts owning semantics.

## Implementation plan

| step | commit candidate | content |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `docs: define repo map context preserving lod` | record this issue contract in docs |
| 2 | `test: add context preserving lod core expectations` | lock z-level context/detail counts first |
| 3 | `feat: project repo context outside focus` | keep all repos visible at middle/near |
| 4 | `feat: distinguish detail and context nodes` | add projection-only detail/context roles |
| 5 | `feat: render context nodes with lower visual weight` | make context passive and visually quieter |
| 6 | `fix: bound context labels by semantic focus scale` | prevent context labels from dominating |
| 7 | `feat: keep focus edges only under context lod` | bound edges to focus neighborhood |
| 8 | `test: add desktop mobile context visual gates` | screenshot + DOM gates for context preservation |
| 9 | `ci: publish context preserving repo map artifact` | upload artifact/report evidence |

## Suggested reducer policy

| z | detail | context | hidden |
|---:|---|---|---|
| far | all repos | none | packages/models |
| middle | focus repo packages | all repos | non-focus packages/models |
| near | focus package models | all repos + focus repo packages + sibling packages | non-focus models |
"}

{"body":"## Purpose

Improve the repo map semantic LOD so zooming in increases detail while preserving map-like global context.

Current implementation is focus-only:

```text
z < 24:
  all repos

24 <= z < 66:
  focus repo + packages only

z >= 66:
  focus package neighborhood + models only
```

This proves containment, but it loses map context. A map should not make the rest of the world disappear when zooming into one area.

## Current behavior

| z | current visible nodes | issue |
|---:|---|---|
| far | all repos | OK |
| middle | focus repo + its packages | other repos disappear |
| near | focus package neighborhood + models | other repos and most packages disappear |

## Desired behavior

Zoom should increase semantic detail without deleting the world context.

Expected behavior:

```text
far:
  all repos visible

middle:
  all repos remain as context
  focus repo shows packages as detail

near:
  all repos remain as context
  focus repo remains visible
  packages remain as context/detail
  focus package shows models as detail
```

## Invariant

This invariant remains unchanged:

```text
repo = packages[]
package = models[]
```

The visual map must preserve containment:

```text
repo rect
  package rect[]
    model rect[]
```

## Required architecture boundary

Keep the existing boundary:

```text
JSONL data
  -> CRUD event contract
  -> model graph reducer
  -> projection / LOD reducer
  -> coordinate-preserving SVG renderer
  -> svg-pan-zoom camera adapter
```

`svg-pan-zoom` remains camera-only.

## Required projection policy

Projection should distinguish:

```text
detail
context
hidden
```

Suggested node projection fields:

```text
visibilityRole:
  detail | context

interactionRole:
  active | passive

labelRole:
  full | short | hidden
```

These are projection/view fields, not source model fields.

## Required visual behavior

### z=far

- all repo rectangles are visible.
- package/model nodes are hidden.
- map is not empty.
- global layout is visible.

### z=middle

- all repo rectangles remain visible as context.
- focus repo remains visually stronger.
- focus repo packages are visible as detail.
- non-focus repo packages may remain hidden.
- non-focus repos must not disappear.
- package rectangles are inside focus repo rect.

### z=near

- all repo rectangles remain visible as context.
- focus repo remains visible.
- focus package and nearby packages are visible.
- models inside focus package are visible as detail.
- model rectangles are inside package rect.
- labels are screen-stable.
- focus detail is readable.
- context nodes do not overpower detail nodes.

## Edge policy

- Do not show all edges at all z levels.
- Far view may show no edges or only aggregate repo edges.
- Middle view may show focus repo/package edges.
- Near view may show selected-neighborhood model edges.
- Context nodes may remain visible without their edges.
- Avoid misleading long edge spaghetti.

## Product UI policy

No new product controls.

Allowed:

```text
-
+
fit
```

Forbidden:

```text
repo button row
z debug text
HUD
debug switches
count-only proof UI
```

## E2E requirements

E2E must prove context preservation, not only detail containment.

Required checks:

### z=far

- repo count >= total repo count.
- package count = 0.
- model count = 0.

### z=middle

- visible repo count >= total repo count.
- focus repo package count >= expected package count.
- non-focus repo context count >= total repo count - 1.
- package rects are inside focus repo rect.
- model count = 0.

### z=near

- visible repo count >= total repo count.
- focus package visible.
- focus package model count >= expected model count.
- model rects are inside focus package rect.
- focus repo remains visible.
- context repo rectangles remain visible.
- labels are not huge or clipped.

### mobile

- no horizontal overflow.
- context remains visible.
- focus detail is visible.
- labels do not explode.
- screenshot is not blank.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `repo = packages[]` and `package = models[]` remain documented.
- [ ] JSONL data format does not become renderer-specific.
- [ ] `svg-pan-zoom` remains camera-only.
- [ ] LOD reducer supports context/detail projection.
- [ ] z=middle keeps non-focus repos visible.
- [ ] z=near keeps repo context visible.
- [ ] package/model containment still passes.
- [ ] edge visibility remains bounded.
- [ ] product UI remains only `-`, `+`, `fit`.
- [ ] desktop screenshots pass z=far/middle/near.
- [ ] mobile screenshots pass z=far/middle/near.
- [ ] generated standalone HTML exists.
- [ ] CI uploads artifact and runtime report.
- [ ] generated HTML remains evidence, not authority.

## Non-scope

- No G6 retry.
- No MSAGL retry.
- No tldraw spike.
- No Canvas/WebGL migration.
- No map tile library.
- No new state store.
- No broad A2UI rewrite.
- No source model rewrite.
- No edge bundling implementation unless required by test failure.

## Merge condition

Merge only if zooming in increases detail while preserving map context.

Count-only pass is not enough.

## Merge-blocking conditions

- focus outside repos disappear at middle/near zoom.
- model/package containment breaks.
- labels explode under semantic focus.
- context nodes overpower detail nodes.
- all edges are shown at once.
- mobile view becomes blank or horizontally overflowing.
- `svg-pan-zoom` starts owning semantics.

## Implementation plan

| step | commit candidate | content |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `docs: define repo map context preserving lod` | record this issue contract in docs |
| 2 | `test: add context preserving lod core expectations` | lock z-level context/detail counts first |
| 3 | `feat: project repo context outside focus` | keep all repos visible at middle/near |
| 4 | `feat: distinguish detail and context nodes` | add projection-only detail/context roles |
| 5 | `feat: render context nodes with lower visual weight` | make context passive and visually quieter |
| 6 | `fix: bound context labels by semantic focus scale` | prevent context labels from dominating |
| 7 | `feat: keep focus edges only under context lod` | bound edges to focus neighborhood |
| 8 | `test: add desktop mobile context visual gates` | screenshot + DOM gates for context preservation |
| 9 | `ci: publish context preserving repo map artifact` | upload artifact/report evidence |

## Suggested reducer policy

| z | detail | context | hidden |
|---:|---|---|---|
| far | all repos | none | packages/models |
| middle | focus repo packages | all repos | non-focus packages/models |
| near | focus package models | all repos + focus repo packages + sibling packages | non-focus models |
"}

{"body":"## Purpose
Define a small adapter contract so Herdr, shell, Codex, and Claude can be added without leaking target-specific logic into worker core.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Stabilizes `worker -> adapter` boundary. |
| product | Enables new targets without rewiring core. |
| system/org | Keeps adapter ownership clear. |
| business/meta | Makes the agent factory extensible and reviewable. |

## Scope
- Define adapter input, output, error, and event mapping expectations.
- Keep worker core dispatch target-agnostic.

## Non-scope
- Implementing individual adapters.
- Dynamic plugin loading.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Adapter contract exists in docs and code/types.
- [ ] Contract returns structured events, not free-form strings only.
- [ ] Worker core can call adapters without knowing CLI details.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Worker core has Herdr/Codex/Claude-specific branches beyond registry lookup.
- [ ] Adapter output cannot be logged as result rows.

## Evidence
- Interface/type tests or compile proof.
- Docs.

## Merge condition
Merge only when adapters are a replaceable boundary, not core branches."}

body: Prevent two local worker processes from claiming and executing the same project-local queue concurrently. Existing per-instruction idempotency protects re-read, but it does not by itself prove safe concurrent ownership.
| scope | Closes the concurrent-worker duplicate execution gap. |
| product | Makes local worker operation predictable. |
| system | Adds one explicit claim boundary before queue consumption. |
| organization | Prevents multiple agents/operators from unknowingly owning the same worker root. |
| business/meta | Reduces duplicate side effects, incident cost, and handoff ambiguity. |
- concurrent workers cannot both claim the same project-local queue.
Use the smallest cross-platform local solution consistent with the `.hq/` workspace contract:
-> record claim identity and start time
A second worker must fail closed before reading for execution or dispatching. Stale-claim recovery must be explicit and auditable rather than silently stealing ownership.
- define claim location under the canonical `.hq/` root;
- acquire/release claim atomically on Linux and Windows;
- include worker id, process id where useful, start time, and workspace identity;
- define stale claim inspection and explicit recovery behavior;
- persist structured claim/rejection evidence without treating it as run authority;
- test interaction with instruction idempotency and restart.
- [ ] First worker acquires the project-local claim before executable queue processing.
- [ ] Second concurrent worker fails closed before adapter dispatch.
- [ ] Rejection is machine-readable and names the workspace/claim identity without exposing secrets.
- [ ] A normal shutdown releases the claim.
- [ ] A crash/stale claim is detected and requires an explicit documented recovery action.
- [ ] Recovery cannot erase existing result/validation evidence.
- [ ] After valid recovery, normal idempotency still prevents already-started or terminal instructions from re-executing.
- [ ] Different project-local roots can run independently.
The issue is not complete if any succeeds:
1. two workers dispatch the same instruction concurrently;
2. second worker reads and mutates execution state before claim rejection;
3. stale claim is silently ignored or stolen;
5. process id alone is trusted without workspace/claim validation;
6. crash recovery causes terminal work to execute again;
7. platform-specific implementation weakens the claim on Windows or Linux.
- first/second worker transcripts and structured claim evidence;
Merge only when one project-local worker root has one fail-closed execution owner at a time on both supported operating systems.

body: ## 正式継承：未完了・保留のまま受入
既存Pi認証入口を対象別に引数化する未merge候補の採否を引き継ぐ。現在のresources実装との重複/差分、元の認証・対象・保持境界は再開時に現物で確認する。

[元windows PR83](https://github.com/roccho-dev/windows/pull/83)の未merge差分・全文契約・review/コメント・不合格/未完・予算/停止条件を継承する。[phase3 User GO](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/25#issuecomment-6249332372)は保全とrepo退役の許可であり、この候補の機能採択・実装/実機成功・旧GOの自動再開ではない。

原Git object/refsと差分は[resourcesの履歴保全Release](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/releases/tag/windows-retirement-20261018)の `windows-history.bundle`、原PR本文/全review/コメント/未merge file patchは `windows-discussions.json` の当該numberに保持する。保全物の公開・取得/独立復元と継承readbackが揃うまで、旧PRの処遇を完了としない。移行の現在値と最終証拠は[resources25](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/25)へ帰着する。

元担当・モデル/actor・scope・許可/拒否・期限・未完条件は原記録を保持し、この移管で新しいactorやruntime GOを作らない。現在の保留物の保全・再開調整はUser/P（既存Codex root）が受ける。再開時はこのIssueと固定原記録、現在のresources source/consumer/他writerを読み、必要な採否/作用許可と実在担当を確定してから、その担当が最小の実変更と元試験でfix/checkする。新認証/秘密/state/Host作用・元拒否の等価再送は許可しない。
旧PRを閉じる場合も「正式継承のため未mergeでclose」と記録し、元ref/head/全文/履歴を保持する。元機能の完成や元FAILの解消とは扱わない。

body: After a successful explicit `hq.submit` of a parsed `@command` object, return an optional version-tied standard text-edit plan that consumes exactly that accepted draft object.
The accepted row is appended and synced before the plan is returned. hq does not apply editor text, own Vim lifecycle, or make local edit success part of accepted authority.
Keep the existing outer `hq.submitResult.v1` and add optional:
1. hq parser owns the exact target object boundary.
2. URI/version equal the accepted submit argument.
3. positions use the negotiated LSP encoding already owned by hqlsp.
4. the edit contains no command or accepted semantics.
5. stale/rejected submit returns no plan and appends zero rows.
6. legacy one-line canonical-JSON submit retains its existing result without a plan.
7. repeated explicit submits remain fresh human intents.
- expose an hq-owned parsed `@command` object byte range without changing lowering;
- map that range to one standard LSP text edit;
- attach the versioned nested record only after append-and-sync succeeds;
- preserve unrelated objects and separator text through exact range selection;
- add protocol/unit tests for first/middle/last object, LF/CRLF/Unicode, stale/failure, legacy JSON, and repeated identity.
- applying a WorkspaceEdit or Vim edit;
- popup, key mapping, cursor, or native undo;
- duplicate guard, submitted state, confirmation, or force-submit;
- whole-buffer clear for a cursor-selected object;
- plan emission for a stale/rejected/unsynced acceptance;
- hq#114 sole normative body includes adrs#219 behavior;
- all required hq tests pass on Linux and Windows;
- one PR based on live `proposals` closes this issue;
- edits#70 can consume the plan mechanically without parsing hq syntax.

request.text:
{"body":"## Practical scope
Make **ChecklistUI = ext(SheetUI #347)**, not a second table renderer. Reuse the merged JSONL parser, editing, checkdate toggle, row add/delete, answer ownership, and standalone HTML packaging. Add only a thin checklist adapter that derives completion count from the saved check-date answer; no new persisted status.

## Direct purpose
Show a small completed/total counter above SheetUI, updated when items are checked/unchecked, added or removed. Leave comments, date and editing to SheetUI.

## Upper purpose
Turn reusable sheet rows into practical checklists for customer inspection/acceptance/release without cloning a business-specific HTML app.

## Meta purpose
One core renderer and one state format reduce repeat development, regression and handoff cost.

## Highest objective
Reusable high-margin UI assets for high-value company construction and eventual sale.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] A small `capabilities/checklist/` adapter imports SheetUI rather than copying rendering/serialization.
- [ ] `completed = count(valid checkdate answers)`; `total = definition row count`; completed is **derived**, not stored.
- [ ] The same definition JSONL / answers JSONL used by SheetUI remain valid; no second schema or stored boolean status.
- [ ] Date unchecked clears the date and decreases completion.
- [ ] Only synthetic fixtures/tests enter Git. Supplied STG/PRD business HTML, links and customer data stay out.
- [ ] Test initial count, checked/unchecked changes, add/delete, malformed dates/schema, lossless SheetUI snapshot and HTML packaging reuse.
- [ ] Read back exact HEAD, CI and source-layout compatibility before merge.

## Non-scope
No roles/tabs/filtering, rearranging/column widths, next-item navigator, history/localStorage, server/database, acceptance authority, CI release flow, customer data, or a new standalone HTML renderer. Deferred/future checklists are separate input views, not artificially included in current progress.

## Equations
- `ChecklistUI = SheetUI + DerivedProgress`
- `Completed = Σ 1(valid(answer[row.id][checkKey]))`
- `Persisted = DefinitionJSONL + AnswerJSONL`; never persist progress
- `OfflineHTML = SheetUI.Portable(Definition, Answers)` (same interactive checkdate controls; the extra progress counter is an embedded UI enhancement, not a new portable renderer)
- `ΔServer = ΔDB = ΔNewRenderer = 0`

## Proposed tree
```text
capabilities/
  editable-sheet/src/index.mjs          ~ small onChange port
  checklist/
    package.json
    README.md
    src/index.mjs
    tests/run.mjs
tests/run-all.mjs                        ~ register checklist test
```

## Merge-blocking conditions
Any UI or JSONL serialization duplication, fabricated stored status/progress, non-synthetic customer data, missing exact-head regression tests, broken direct `file://` HTML from SheetUI, unresolved source-layout collision, or missing explicit human merge approval.

## Tests to keep
Pure progress checks + DOM interaction regression tied to SheetUI notification + existing suite and offline browser proof.

## Tests not to keep
A second renderer, HTML golden snapshot with real STG/PRD data, optional role/navigation/layout UI, redundant workflows."}

Turn reusable sheet rows into practical checklists for customer inspection/acceptance/release without cloning a business-specific HTML app.

## Meta purpose
One core renderer and one state format reduce repeat development, regression and handoff cost.

## Highest objective
Reusable high-margin UI assets for high-value company construction and eventual sale.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] A small `capabilities/checklist/` adapter imports SheetUI rather than copying rendering/serialization.
- [ ] `completed = count(valid checkdate answers)`; `total = definition row count`; completed is **derived**, not stored.
- [ ] The same definition JSONL / answers JSONL used by SheetUI remain valid; no second schema or stored boolean status.
- [ ] Date unchecked clears the date and decreases completion.
- [ ] Only synthetic fixtures/tests enter Git. Supplied STG/PRD business HTML, links and customer data stay out.
- [ ] Test initial count, checked/unchecked changes, add/delete, malformed dates/schema, lossless SheetUI snapshot and HTML packaging reuse.
- [ ] Read back exact HEAD, CI and source-layout compatibility before merge.

## Non-scope
No roles/tabs/filtering, rearranging/column widths, next-item navigator, history/localStorage, server/database, acceptance authority, CI release flow, customer data, or a new standalone HTML renderer. Deferred/future checklists are separate input views, not artificially included in current progress.

## Equations
- `ChecklistUI = SheetUI + DerivedProgress`
- `Completed = Σ 1(valid(answer[row.id][checkKey]))`
- `Persisted = DefinitionJSONL + AnswerJSONL`; never persist progress
- `OfflineHTML = SheetUI.Portable(Definition, Answers)` (same interactive checkdate controls; the extra progress counter is an embedded UI enhancement, not a new portable renderer)
- `ΔServer = ΔDB = ΔNewRenderer = 0`

## Proposed tree
```text
capabilities/
  editable-sheet/src/index.mjs          ~ small onChange port
  checklist/
    package.json
    README.md
    src/index.mjs
    tests/run.mjs
tests/run-all.mjs                        ~ register checklist test
```

## Merge-blocking conditions
Any UI or JSONL serialization duplication, fabricated stored status/progress, non-synthetic customer data, missing exact-head regression tests, broken direct `file://` HTML from SheetUI, unresolved source-layout collision, or missing explicit human merge approval.

## Tests to keep
Pure progress checks + DOM interaction regression tied to SheetUI notification + existing suite and offline browser proof.

## Tests not to keep
A second renderer, HTML golden snapshot with real STG/PRD data, optional role/navigation/layout UI, redundant workflows."}

目的：Userが実装完了を指示した[ADRS #633の合意済みv6](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/pull/633)（head `6cac47d5572bfe609f4fc7c893e2701250d7420c`、tree `38a5af95fd3685375f709e08e2ac5ba53245ccc8`、[独立設計合意](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/pull/633#pullrequestreview-5512693855)）を、既存の所有先と更新入口へ実装し、実装成果の独立検証まで完了する。候補保存や図の合意を製品実装・実機合格と混同しない。
1. **基盤BとTool Tを分離**：ownの既存分離を維持し、rentにも互換な独立Tool世代を接続する。固定入力と必要な互換性・起動・状態条件が一致するTool-only更新で、OCI全体の再構築/交換を要求しない。Bの変更は別に扱う。NixOS NativeもOS基盤とTool世代を別に扱い、OCIを必須にしない。

2. **既存責務へ接続**：Producerの候補C、envsの承認済み対象選択D、Target実観測O、既存証拠から導く最後の成立Eを区別する。own/rent/Nativeが別の時点・版を選択でき、source不変だけでTarget NOOP/成功としない。Dの具体形式・既存入口へ接続する。新しい意味/形式が必要なら、既存ADRSの必要な採択経路を経てからproduction入力にし、既存#215/#220を無言で上書きしない。
3. **必要状態を保持**：認証・session・作業・repository・volumeの既存所有と保持を維持する。固定版/closure/起動条件/GC・初回/旧profile互換/単一writer・静止・条件付き復旧を対象scopeで検証する。Tool rollbackは作業データのrollbackではない。
4. **中断から完成へ接続**：UNKNOWNは許可された読取で照合し、読取開始に不明解消や製品開発GOを先に要求しない。変更は工程別の許可と必要条件で判定する。原因是正・独立検証・現版/現D/新O照合・残作用だけの再開、実開始と受理の区別、担当/経路停止時の帰着を実装・検証へ対応させる。無関係なTargetのUNKNOWNで安全なsource是正を止めない。
5. **対象間の整合**：Host relationの意味・表現はADRS/resources、source/buildはProducer、採用/Bindingはenvs、実現・観測はTargetのまま。既存admission・秘密供給・実行主体の境界を維持し、Host IDをrepo/OS/image/pathから生成しない。

6. **証拠と完成**：公開exact head/treeと検証入力の同一性、必要checkのrun/job/head/結論、要求への対応、実装済み/実証済み/未確認を区別する。v6のV01-V14、S1-A3、L01-L28を適用範囲へ対応させ、抽象条件確認を実装/実機試験へ昇格しない。系列の合成exact tree setと一つのcross-PR gateで全要求を独立評価し、未割当の必要修正を残さない。
対象repository：roccho-dev/windows、roccho-dev/envs、roccho-dev/resources、および必要な採択/契約接続だけのroccho-dev/adrs。製品source・必要なcheck/tests・直接対応するdocsを対象とする。詳細な実装方法・最小のPR系列は実変更PRで定める。

最初の実変更はwindowsのrent基盤/Tool分離を担う固定入力の実構成とその検証。開始base：`d3c7c02de70c680c5790f030ef6b128d5a002b54`（proposals）。最初の変更対象は `flake.nix` と `hosts/profile/nix.nix`。既存own/default/legacyの責務と既存保持・認証契約を維持し、計画だけ/能力probeだけのPRにしない。
共通daemon・汎用更新engine・新しい第二のmanifest/runtime台帳、認証情報の複製や平文出力、actor増員/黙示置換、repository退役、無関係な改修は非目標。失敗・UNKNOWN・旧証拠を消さず、別head/別treeの検証を流用しない。
この対象定義は実装sourceと候補環境/CIでの検証を要求する。現用Host/volume/秘密への変更、全Windows再起動、既存認証の変更、deploy/merge/Issue closeはこのIssueだけから許可しない。必要な実機検証作用は、対象・preimage・保持/復帰・担当・独立検証を具体化した境界判断へ返す。
到達点は全要求に対応する実装成果・公開PR・合成検証・独立受入が揃ったmerge-ready状態。実機未実証の項目は明示し、実機成功やIssue closedと主張しない。このIssueは対象定義だけで、R/Wの計画・進捗・反証・証拠交換は系列PR上で行う。

{"body":"## Purpose
Prove that `hq --accept --queue` has exactly one durable side effect: append an accepted JSONL row.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Prevents hidden execution in the `vim -> hq` step. |
| product | Keeps acceptance deterministic and testable. |
| system/org | Moves execution and observation to worker/event logs. |
| business/meta | Prevents false claims during handoff and due diligence. |

## Scope
- Add a fixture or test that accepts a row and checks queue append behavior.
- Assert no shell/Herdr/agent process is launched by `hq`.

## Non-scope
- Worker execution.
- Adapter integration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One accepted input creates exactly one queue row.
- [ ] Draft/complete/context never append.
- [ ] Accept never invokes external execution.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Unaccepted candidates are written.
- [ ] Accept triggers shell/Herdr/agent execution.
- [ ] Draft preview appends anything.

## Evidence
- Test fixture.
- CI output.

## Merge condition
Merge only when accept-only append semantics are proven and protected."}

- [ ] Observe/read target is represented as event data.
- [ ] Missing target produces structured failure.

- [ ] Attach command is only printed without being stored.

## Evidence
- Event fixture.
- Session projection sample.

This is complete when node and edge selections can produce `ui.targetRef.v1`-compatible records and expose them to local/dev tooling without granting authority.

- Add target metadata to SVG nodes and edges.

- Keep UI action as proposal, not approval.

| UI target | targetKind |
|---|---|

Ensure malformed or unsafe instruction rows are rejected before any adapter can execute them.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Protects `instruction.jsonl -> worker` from invalid rows. |

- Add invalid fixtures for missing required keys, unknown version, unknown target, malformed payload, duplicate ids, and unsafe policy.
- Add expected error reasons.

- Adapter execution.
- Full security sandbox.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every invalid fixture is rejected with a reason.
- [ ] Rejection emits or can produce a `blocked`/validation result row.
- [ ] Valid fixtures still pass.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Unknown target falls back to shell.
- [ ] Missing id/version/target is accepted.
- [ ] Malformed JSON silently drops later lines without report.

## Evidence
- Fixture files.
- Validator test output.

## Merge condition
Merge only when broken instruction rows fail closed."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Emit package inventory findings for missing, orphan, duplicate, or dead package surfaces so package-list removal cannot bypass ADRS/package enforcement.

## Post-merge state

After attached PRs merge:
- missing required package rows become blocking-capable findings.
- observed-but-unclaimed packages are surfaced as orphan/diagnostic findings.
- duplicate or dead package rows cannot silently pass.

## Completion audit impact

Contributes to:
- `packageAudit`: inventory closure result.
- `finalReport.inventory` section.
- `completionCertificate.blockingFindingCount` when inventory is not closed.

## Merge blockers

Do not merge child PRs when:
- missing package rows are warnings only with no strict path.
- orphan/duplicate/dead rows are not classified.
- findings omit packageId, expected, actual, delta, likelyOwner, or nextAction.
- fixture coverage is happy-path only.

## Required evidence

- finding emitter or compiler path.
- clean inventory fixture with no findings.
- dirty fixtures for missing, orphan, duplicate, and dead package surfaces.
- CI/check proving strict mode fails when required inventory is not closed.

## Boundary

This issue closes inventory findings only. It does not close assertion/receipt admission or branch protection."}

{"body":"## Goal

Prove that expected governance fixtures are not implicit repo-local files.

A required fixture must be:

1. produced as a Nix output;
2. referenced by `gov-package-output` with manifest and digest;
3. consumed by selected destination repos through a Nix-declared `governance` input;
4. run at the destination repo;
5. represented as a canonical receipt row;
6. read by the governance final join.

This issue is complete only when the fixture path proves destination behavior, not only producer behavior.

## Parent / refs

Parent:

- Refs #131

Existing completed or active foundations that this issue must reuse, not reimplement:

- Refs #79 / #89 — reusable `gov-package-output` producer and provenance verifier.
- Refs #93 / #96 — required repo packet org join.
- Refs #102 — canonical package receipts.
- Refs #125 — selected real package closure pass.
- Refs #126 — `gov-final-scope-purpose-join / gate` adapter surface.
- Refs roccho-dev/adrs#132 — ADRS package inventory, assertions, and receipts.
- Refs roccho-dev/ops#33 — ops local governance cutover evidence path.
- Refs roccho-dev/ui#103 — UI local governance cutover evidence path.

## Boundary

ADRS accepted decisions own fixture expectations and destination receipt requirements.
Governance provides projection, producer, verifier, report, and join logic.
`gov-package-output` is a joinable evidence packet, not meaning authority.
Fixture output alone is not final compliance.
Fixture check green alone is not final compliance.
Only `gov-final-scope-purpose-join / gate` may become merge authority after explicit cutover.

## Required closure model

```text
ADRS accepted fixture expectation
  -> governance Nix-produced fixture output
  -> gov-package-output fixture reference with manifest/digest
  -> selected destination repo Nix-declared consumption
  -> destination run
  -> canonical destination receipt
  -> governance final join input
  -> final report finding when missing, stale, mismatched, unconsumed, or not runnable
```

## Child work

| Child | Repo | Purpose | Blocks close? |
|---|---|---|---:|
| C1 | `roccho-dev/adrs` | Define or link accepted fixture output and destination receipt contract | yes |
| C2 | `roccho-dev/governance` | Extend `gov-package-output` with fixture bundle refs, manifest, and digest | yes |
| C3 | `roccho-dev/adrs` | Consume governance fixture output and emit destination receipt | yes |
| C4 | `roccho-dev/ops` | Consume governance fixture output and emit destination receipt | yes |
| C5 | `roccho-dev/ui` | Consume governance fixture output and emit destination receipt | yes |
| C6 | `roccho-dev/governance` | Join destination fixture receipts into final report / gate input | yes |
| C7 | `roccho-dev/governance` | Audit that fixture surfaces do not look like a separate governance route | yes |

## Done

- `gov-package-output` includes fixture bundle reference, fixture manifest, and fixture digest.
- Fixture bundle is produced through Nix output, not by an implicit fixed path read.
- Producer provenance, input closure, and output digest are verified by the existing producer/verifier path or accepted extension.
- Selected destination repos consume the fixture through Nix-declared `governance` input.
- Selected destination repos run the fixture.
- Destination run emits canonical receipt rows with at least:
  - `repoId`
  - `packageId`
  - `contractId`
  - `decisionDigest`
  - `assertionDigest`
  - `checkId`
  - `status`
  - `evidenceDigest`
  - fixture reference or fixture digest
- Governance final join consumes destination fixture receipts.
- Final report records actionable findings for missing, stale, mismatched, unconsumed, or not-runnable fixture evidence.
- Fixture producer checks remain evidence producers, not final-looking required checks.
- Completion evidence records destination fixture proof.
- Governance remains non-authority over accepted meaning.

## Not done when

- Fixture only exists inside governance selftest.
- Downstream example exists but selected destination repos do not consume it.
- Destination repo imports fixture but does not run it.
- Destination repo runs fixture but emits no canonical receipt.
- Receipt rows are not bound to decision, assertion, and fixture digests.
- Raw `nix flake check` green is described as final compliance.
- Fixture artifact/check/doc surface appears to be another governance route.
- Final join does not read destination fixture receipts.

## Required regression cases

The checker or final report must cover:

1. expected fixture output absent;
2. malformed fixture manifest;
3. manually authored fixture bundle;
4. missing producer provenance;
5. unexpected producer repo;
6. stale producer revision;
7. fixture digest mismatch;
8. fixture input closure gap;
9. destination repo does not consume fixture;
10. destination repo consumes but does not run fixture;
11. destination run emits no receipt;
12. destination receipt uses mismatched `decisionDigest`;
13. destination receipt uses mismatched `assertionDigest`;
14. destination receipt uses mismatched fixture digest;
15. fixture cannot run at destination;
16. fixture CI, artifact, or doc surface appears to be final pass.

## Expected finding classes

| Finding | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `missingExpectedFixtureOutput` | expected fixture output is absent |
| `invalidFixtureProducerProvenance` | fixture provenance cannot be verified |
| `staleFixtureOutput` | fixture producer, source, or digest is stale |
| `fixtureInputClosureGap` | fixture source input is outside the input closure |
| `missingDestinationFixtureConsumption` | destination repo does not consume the fixture |
| `fixtureNotRunnableAtDestination` | destination repo cannot run the fixture |
| `missingDestinationFixtureReceipt` | destination run produced no canonical receipt |
| `fixtureReceiptDigestMismatch` | receipt digest does not match fixture / decision / assertion |
| `apparentAlternativeFixtureRoute` | CI, artifact, docs, or README make fixture path look like another governance route |

Each final-report finding must include `expected`, `actual`, `delta`, `likelyOwner`, `nextAction`, and relevant digests.

## Acceptance criteria

Close only when all are true:

1. Accepted ADRS contract or accepted equivalent defines required fixture output and destination receipt expectations.
2. `gov-package-output` carries fixture bundle reference, manifest, and digest.
3. Fixture output is Nix-produced and provenance-verified.
4. Selected destination repos consume fixture outputs through Nix-declared inputs.
5. Selected destination repos run the fixtures.
6. Destination run emits canonical receipts.
7. Governance final join consumes those receipts.
8. Missing, stale, mismatched, unconsumed, or not-runnable fixture evidence becomes an actionable final-report finding.
9. Fixture producer/check/artifact surfaces are not final-looking required checks.
10. Completion evidence includes destination fixture proof.
11. Governance remains non-authority over accepted meaning.

## Merge blockers

Do not merge attached implementation PRs if:

- they introduce fixture output but no destination proof;
- they claim final active admission from fixture generation alone;
- they treat raw Nix green as final compliance;
- they require fixed repo-local fixture paths instead of Nix-declared outputs;
- they omit producer provenance or input closure verification;
- they omit destination receipt fields needed by final join;
- they add a final-looking CI, artifact, or check name outside `gov-final-scope-purpose-join / gate`;
- they change branch protection in a producer/evidence-only PR;
- they make governance semantic authority.

## Child PR comment template

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Parent | #143 |
| Related parent | #131 |
| Child scope |  |
| Delta removed |  |
| Destination proof |  |
| Receipt fields |  |
| Regression evidence |  |
| Final gate effect |  |
| Boundary | no meaning authority transfer; no final pass from fixture generation alone |
| Readback plan |  |"}

{"body":"## Status

V1 scope: **provider-detached, read-only live ADRS fixture integration**.

- authority: false
- production gate: false
- target-ref writes: forbidden
- all-repository enforcement: false
- causal support verified: false
- top purpose achieved: false

This body supersedes the previous body-based fixture design. The semantic source is now an append-only JSONL ledger carried by one ADRS fixture Issue's source comments. GitHub is only an adapter providing Issue UI/API, CI, and repository locators.

## Purpose

Close the smallest real path:

```text
ADRS fixture Issue append-only JSONL comments
  -> GitHub ledger adapter
  -> canonical provider-neutral ledger
  -> closed schema + explicit-supersession reducer
  -> purpose closure + Go architecture facts/checks
  -> provider-neutral semantic packet
  -> offline Nix materialization
  -> read-only CI receipt
```

The same engine must also accept a plain JSONL file adapter and sealed source trees obtained through interchangeable locators. Provider metadata must remain outside semantic inputs and outputs.

## Existing bounded proof

A local proof already passed 33 tests with these receipts:

| Artifact | SHA-256 / value |
|---|---|
| canonical ledger | `723ac930fbd5e1a85de8fc552e49d8477568c8da1c7acd58e0db34b29490338b` |
| canonical source tree | `fbae94090ad8ee0e08f64b268d2efa6b8b34121d099d978d3c94deed6654e361` |
| schema | `6d48c6cf59a84a7940fc8aac4b193f6e9d4f267727e61c50286ea3155f3862cb` |
| semantic packet / Nix output | `e7df1eceb56e00ab06f2e9d887aa74857b704adbd934f96c9408c1a37ca61b32` |
| Nix store path | `/nix/store/8szwzcsbh7czwpjxhdm1fhc4xd74aa5n-code-governance-semantic-v1.json` |
| test count | `33` |

This proof is evidence, not the production implementation or authority source.

## Authority and provider boundary

- `roccho-dev/adrs#202` remains the authority-boundary hub.
- The ADRS fixture Issue is non-authoritative test Data only.
- `governance` owns deterministic adapters, reduction, checks, findings, semantic packets, Nix materialization, and receipts.
- GitHub identity, repository, Issue number, comment/event IDs, actor, timestamps, pagination, Actions run IDs, artifact URLs, and SSH locators are transport provenance only.
- The engine must not import provider adapters or network clients and must contain no GitHub/Issue/comment/Actions/SSH semantic vocabulary.
- Nix reads only the provider-neutral semantic packet.

## Four-principle lock

| Principle | V1 application |
|---|---|
| YAGNI | one ADRS fixture Issue, one ledger contract, one engine, one read-only CI path, Go only |
| KISS | adapters emit files; engine consumes files; no provider framework, DB, queue, plugin system, or write gate |
| DRY | fixture meaning exists only as append-only ADRS JSONL rows; Git contains engine/schema/tests only |
| SOLID | provider adapters = Action, ledger/source files = Data, engine = Calculation, Nix = deterministic materializer |

The principle names are not diagnostics. Only observable lower-level rules may block.

## ADRS fixture source contract

One dedicated ADRS Issue must exist.

- Issue body is an index and contract only; it is not semantic rule input.
- Semantic input is JSONL-only source comments from the adapter-configured trusted fixture writer.
- V1 live fixture may use the authenticated repository owner as the designated writer because it is non-authoritative; production bot-only authority is out of scope.
- Source comments must never be edited or deleted.
- Human discussion comments are not source and must not affect the ledger digest.
- All pages must be fetched; missing pagination fails closed.
- Transport provenance is stored only in `transport-receipt.json`.
- Canonical ledger rows contain no provider identity or locator fields.
- Current state is computed only by the versioned reducer over the complete ledger.

## Closed ledger schema

Schema identity: `urn:roccho:code-governance-ledger:v1`.

Physical row kinds:

- `contract`
- `record`
- `edge`

Semantic kinds:

- `fixture-contract`
- `purpose`
- `code-rule`
- `test-case`
- `purpose-parent`
- `rule-purpose`

Required properties are closed; unknown properties and kinds fail. Updates use one explicit `supersedes` edge. Input order, timestamps, comment IDs, and provider IDs never select a winner. Every logical subject must reduce to exactly one active row.

## Code-governance V1 blocking rules

### Role classification

Every production Go file is classified exactly once as:

- `data`
- `calculation`
- `port`
- `action`
- `adapter`
- `composition`

Unclassified or multiply classified files fail.

### Dependency direction

Allowed edges:

```text
data        -> data
calculation -> data | calculation
port        -> data
action      -> data | calculation | port
adapter     -> data | calculation | port | adapter
composition -> any role
```

Core-to-adapter, action-to-concrete-adapter, data-to-action, and adapter-to-action dependencies fail.

### Effect boundary

`data`, `calculation`, `port`, and `action` cannot directly call configured filesystem, process, network, clock, randomness, environment, or mutable-global APIs. Actions reach effects through ports. Parse failures fail closed.

### KISS subset

- dot imports fail;
- blank imports outside adapter/composition fail;
- hidden ambient effect calls outside effect roles fail.

### YAGNI subset

For Go modules, `go mod tidy -diff` must be clean. Unused declared module dependencies fail.

### DRY subset

Duplicate event IDs, duplicate active logical subjects, duplicate rule identities, and conflicting contract identities fail.

### Purpose closure

- exactly one root purpose;
- no duplicate purpose IDs;
- all parents exist;
- no cycles;
- every blocking rule has one immediate purpose;
- every blocking rule reaches the root;
- every edge is direct or indirect;
- indirect edges require mechanism and falsification;
- structural closure never implies causal support or outcome achievement.

## Required adapters and file contracts

### Ledger adapters

A GitHub Issue adapter and a plain JSONL file adapter must each emit:

```text
ledger.jsonl
transport-receipt.json
```

Equivalent semantic rows with different repository, Issue, actor, comment IDs, timestamps, pagination, grouping, row order, whitespace, or CRLF must produce the same canonical ledger bytes.

### Source adapters

Local directory and Git locator adapters must emit:

```text
snapshot/
tree.json
transport-receipt.json
```

Equivalent sealed trees reached through different locators must produce the same tree and semantic packet.

## Provider-neutral engine outputs

The engine consumes only canonical ledger and sealed tree data and emits:

```text
projection.jsonl
facts.jsonl
findings.jsonl
semantic-packet.json
semantic-receipt.json
```

Provider provenance is not embedded in any semantic artifact. Changing transport metadata must not change semantic output. Changing one valid semantic row or source byte must change semantic output.

## Nix materialization

- Nix receives only `semantic-packet.json` as explicit input.
- Nix performs no live GitHub, network, clock, environment, or locator lookup.
- Offline materialization must preserve bytes and digest.
- Equivalent provider transports must resolve to identical output bytes and store path.

## Destructive proofs

The implementation must reject at least:

1. edited previously sealed source event;
2. deleted previously sealed source event;
3. missing page or incomplete pagination;
4. malformed JSONL;
5. unknown property, row kind, or semantic kind;
6. duplicate event ID;
7. invalid or conflicting supersession;
8. multiple active rows for one logical subject;
9. missing/multiple purpose root;
10. missing purpose parent;
11. purpose cycle;
12. rule without purpose;
13. rule unable to reach root;
14. indirect edge without mechanism or falsification;
15. unclassified Go file;
16. forbidden dependency edge;
17. forbidden direct effect;
18. unused Go module dependency;
19. dot import;
20. forbidden blank import;
21. Go parse failure;
22. provider metadata entering semantic artifacts;
23. engine importing provider adapters/network clients;
24. semantic output changing from transport-only mutation;
25. semantic output failing to change after semantic/source mutation.

## CI

Use one read-only orchestration path:

```text
fetch all ADRS fixture comments
  -> emit canonical ledger + transport receipt
  -> acquire sealed fixture source tree
  -> run provider-neutral engine
  -> materialize semantic packet with Nix offline
  -> verify expected digests and destructive tests
  -> publish read-only artifacts/receipt
```

CI provider behavior is limited to invoking the same CLI and translating exit code/artifacts. No target-repository write permission, merge/ref mutation, ruleset change, or candidate-code execution with secrets is allowed.

## Explicit non-goals

- accepted or production policy authority;
- exact-SHA merge/ref write gate;
- branch protection or required-check cutover;
- all-repository rollout;
- non-Go languages;
- transitive call/data-flow proof;
- generic clone similarity or arbitrary complexity limits;
- auto-fix;
- business outcome, causal support, buyer recognition, or corporate-sale achievement.

Required false claims remain:

```text
authority=false
production_authority=false
all_repositories_enforced=false
causal_support_verified=false
top_purpose_achieved=false
```

## Deliverables

1. Create one ADRS non-authority fixture Issue and append its 52 canonical JSONL rows as source comments.
2. Add provider adapters, closed schema, reducer, Go scanner, fixtures, engine, Nix materializer, and generic CI wrapper to `governance`.
3. Add live read-only ADRS Issue ingestion CI.
4. Reproduce the bounded local proof and produce a live transport receipt.
5. Read back the CI result and all digests.

No separate governance implementation Issue or target-repository Issue is required.

## Acceptance criteria

Close only when all are true:

- the ADRS fixture Issue exists and is explicitly non-authority;
- all 52 source rows are append-only comments from the declared fixture writer;
- the Issue body and discussion comments do not affect semantic digest;
- GitHub and file adapters produce identical canonical ledger bytes;
- provider metadata is isolated to transport receipts;
- engine has no provider-specific vocabulary/import dependency;
- reducer output is invariant to row order/chunking and has one active row per subject;
- purpose closure and all V1 code-rule fixtures pass;
- all destructive tests fail for their expected reason;
- local CLI and CI wrapper produce identical semantic output;
- local/Git locator variants produce the same sealed tree and semantic output;
- Nix offline materialization is byte-identical and provider-invariant;
- repeated live runs over the same Issue/source/checker produce identical semantic digests;
- CI is read-only and performs no repository/ref mutation;
- all required false authority/outcome claims remain false;
- no Git object contains a duplicate editable copy of ADRS fixture meaning.

## Closure receipt

The final comment must record:

- ADRS fixture Issue URL;
- declared source writer and comment count;
- canonical ledger digest;
- schema digest;
- sealed source-tree digest;
- governance checker commit/version;
- CI run/check identity;
- semantic packet and Nix output digest/store path;
- full test count and log digest;
- confirmation of provider/semantic separation;
- confirmation of read-only permissions;
- all false authority/outcome flags;
- residuals for live SSH, production write boundary, all-repository rollout, and non-Go languages.

Closing this Issue proves only provider-detached live ADRS ingestion and read-only code-governance validation. It does not activate production enforcement."}

- `adapter`
- `composition`

Unclassified or multiply classified files fail.

### Dependency direction

Allowed edges:

```text
data        -> data
calculation -> data | calculation
port        -> data
action      -> data | calculation | port
adapter     -> data | calculation | port | adapter
composition -> any role
```

Core-to-adapter, action-to-concrete-adapter, data-to-action, and adapter-to-action dependencies fail.

### Effect boundary

`data`, `calculation`, `port`, and `action` cannot directly call configured filesystem, process, network, clock, randomness, environment, or mutable-global APIs. Actions reach effects through ports. Parse failures fail closed.

### KISS subset

- dot imports fail;
- blank imports outside adapter/composition fail;
- hidden ambient effect calls outside effect roles fail.

### YAGNI subset

For Go modules, `go mod tidy -diff` must be clean. Unused declared module dependencies fail.

### DRY subset

Duplicate event IDs, duplicate active logical subjects, duplicate rule identities, and conflicting contract identities fail.

### Purpose closure

- exactly one root purpose;
- no duplicate purpose IDs;
- all parents exist;
- no cycles;
- every blocking rule has one immediate purpose;
- every blocking rule reaches the root;
- every edge is direct or indirect;
- indirect edges require mechanism and falsification;
- structural closure never implies causal support or outcome achievement.

## Required adapters and file contracts

### Ledger adapters

A GitHub Issue adapter and a plain JSONL file adapter must each emit:

```text
ledger.jsonl
transport-receipt.json
```

Equivalent semantic rows with different repository, Issue, actor, comment IDs, timestamps, pagination, grouping, row order, whitespace, or CRLF must produce the same canonical ledger bytes.

### Source adapters

Local directory and Git locator adapters must emit:

```text
snapshot/
tree.json
transport-receipt.json
```

Equivalent sealed trees reached through different locators must produce the same tree and semantic packet.

## Provider-neutral engine outputs

The engine consumes only canonical ledger and sealed tree data and emits:

```text
projection.jsonl
facts.jsonl
findings.jsonl
semantic-packet.json
semantic-receipt.json
```

Provider provenance is not embedded in any semantic artifact. Changing transport metadata must not change semantic output. Changing one valid semantic row or source byte must change semantic output.

## Nix materialization

- Nix receives only `semantic-packet.json` as explicit input.
- Nix performs no live GitHub, network, clock, environment, or locator lookup.
- Offline materialization must preserve bytes and digest.
- Equivalent provider transports must resolve to identical output bytes and store path.

## Destructive proofs

The implementation must reject at least:

1. edited previously sealed source event;
2. deleted previously sealed source event;
3. missing page or incomplete pagination;
4. malformed JSONL;
5. unknown property, row kind, or semantic kind;
6. duplicate event ID;
7. invalid or conflicting supersession;
8. multiple active rows for one logical subject;
9. missing/multiple purpose root;
10. missing purpose parent;
11. purpose cycle;
12. rule without purpose;
13. rule unable to reach root;
14. indirect edge without mechanism or falsification;
15. unclassified Go file;
16. forbidden dependency edge;
17. forbidden direct effect;
18. unused Go module dependency;
19. dot import;
20. forbidden blank import;
21. Go parse failure;
22. provider metadata entering semantic artifacts;
23. engine importing provider adapters/network clients;
24. semantic output changing from transport-only mutation;
25. semantic output failing to change after semantic/source mutation.

## CI

Use one read-only orchestration path:

```text
fetch all ADRS fixture comments
  -> emit canonical ledger + transport receipt
  -> acquire sealed fixture source tree
  -> run provider-neutral engine
  -> materialize semantic packet with Nix offline
  -> verify expected digests and destructive tests
  -> publish read-only artifacts/receipt
```

CI provider behavior is limited to invoking the same CLI and translating exit code/artifacts. No target-repository write permission, merge/ref mutation, ruleset change, or candidate-code execution with secrets is allowed.

## Explicit non-goals

- accepted or production policy authority;
- exact-SHA merge/ref write gate;
- branch protection or required-check cutover;
- all-repository rollout;
- non-Go languages;
- transitive call/data-flow proof;
- generic clone similarity or arbitrary complexity limits;
- auto-fix;
- business outcome, causal support, buyer recognition, or corporate-sale achievement.

Required false claims remain:

```text
authority=false
production_authority=false
all_repositories_enforced=false
causal_support_verified=false
top_purpose_achieved=false
```

## Deliverables

1. Create one ADRS non-authority fixture Issue and append its 52 canonical JSONL rows as source comments.
2. Add provider adapters, closed schema, reducer, Go scanner, fixtures, engine, Nix materializer, and generic CI wrapper to `governance`.
3. Add live read-only ADRS Issue ingestion CI.
4. Reproduce the bounded local proof and produce a live transport receipt.
5. Read back the CI result and all digests.

No separate governance implementation Issue or target-repository Issue is required.

## Acceptance criteria

Close only when all are true:

- the ADRS fixture Issue exists and is explicitly non-authority;
- all 52 source rows are append-only comments from the declared fixture writer;
- the Issue body and discussion comments do not affect semantic digest;
- GitHub and file adapters produce identical canonical ledger bytes;
- provider metadata is isolated to transport receipts;
- engine has no provider-specific vocabulary/import dependency;
- reducer output is invariant to row order/chunking and has one active row per subject;
- purpose closure and all V1 code-rule fixtures pass;
- all destructive tests fail for their expected reason;
- local CLI and CI wrapper produce identical semantic output;
- local/Git locator variants produce the same sealed tree and semantic output;
- Nix offline materialization is byte-identical and provider-invariant;
- repeated live runs over the same Issue/source/checker produce identical semantic digests;
- CI is read-only and performs no repository/ref mutation;
- all required false authority/outcome claims remain false;
- no Git object contains a duplicate editable copy of ADRS fixture meaning.

## Closure receipt

The final comment must record:

- ADRS fixture Issue URL;
- declared source writer and comment count;
- canonical ledger digest;
- schema digest;
- sealed source-tree digest;
- governance checker commit/version;
- CI run/check identity;
- semantic packet and Nix output digest/store path;
- full test count and log digest;
- confirmation of provider/semantic separation;
- confirmation of read-only permissions;
- all false authority/outcome flags;
- residuals for live SSH, production write boundary, all-repository rollout, and non-Go languages.

Closing this Issue proves only provider-detached live ADRS ingestion and read-only code-governance validation. It does not activate production enforcement."}

Establish a transferable, auditable and replaceable back-office operating model for CEO, COO, CFO and CMO teams in which:
- the only normal human UI is permitted OneDrive/SharePoint directories, Office files and Agent conversation;
- Agent participation is required for normal formal CRUD;
- Microsoft 365 provides identity, file UI, department ownership, versioning, approval, audit and retention;
- Agent, UI and provider remain replaceable without losing business files or permission ownership;
- custom software remains zero unless an observed repeated gap justifies one finite addition;
- the resulting operating capability lowers dependency on individual employees, diligence cost, integration ambiguity and transfer cost.
Technical completion alone does not prove increased company value or a completed corporate sale.

| G4 | Make management predictable, accountable, recoverable and auditable |

Any admitted implementation must close only that bounded gap. It must not create a generic platform unless two real consumers already require the same extracted boundary.
