{"body":"## Status

```text
architectureTarget=true
implementationAuthority=false
v0Child=roccho-dev/ism#1
finalStateProved=false
businessOutcomeProved=false
```

## Relationship to V0

- `roccho-dev/ism#1` is the smallest executable V0 proof.
- This Issue defines the complete target state, permanent boundaries, staged path, destructive conditions, and final acceptance gates.
- Closing V0 does not close this Issue.
- This Issue does not require future components to be implemented before an observed need exists.

## Purpose

Establish a transferable, auditable and replaceable back-office operating model for CEO, COO, CFO and CMO teams in which:

- the only normal human UI is permitted OneDrive/SharePoint directories, Office files and Agent conversation;
- Agent participation is required for normal formal CRUD;
- Microsoft 365 provides identity, file UI, department ownership, versioning, approval, audit and retention;
- Agent, UI and provider remain replaceable without losing business files or permission ownership;
- custom software remains zero unless an observed repeated gap justifies one finite addition;
- the resulting operating capability lowers dependency on individual employees, diligence cost, integration ambiguity and transfer cost.

Technical completion alone does not prove increased company value or a completed corporate sale.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Purpose |
|---:|---|
| G0 | Complete a high-value corporate sale on acceptable terms |
| G1 | Increase realizable value and probability of completion |
| G2 | Reduce buyer uncertainty, residual liability and integration cost |
| G3 | Build transferable and independently verifiable operating capability |
| G4 | Make management predictable, accountable, recoverable and auditable |
| G5 | Unify file work, Agent-assisted CRUD, permissions, approval and readback |
| G6 | Define exact ownership, state, authority, evidence and closure contracts |

## One-line final state

```text
OneDrive / Office file UI
  → Agent conversation
  → current identity, ownership, permission, expected version and risk gate
  → human approval where required
  → Microsoft 365 effect
  → version, permission and audit readback
  → visible completion or residual
```

## Final responsibility split

| Concern | Final owner |
|---|---|
| Human file UI | OneDrive, SharePoint and Office |
| Department file ownership | SharePoint shared library |
| Personal draft | Business OneDrive |
| Human and group identity | Entra ID |
| File permission | SharePoint ACL constrained by Entra groups |
| Conversation and work planning | Replaceable Agent product |
| Business decision and accountability | Named human role |
| Normal CRUD entry | Agent conversation or Agent-mediated Office flow |
| High-risk approval | Correct accountable human |
| File version truth | Microsoft 365 version identity and stored bytes |
| Permission truth | Current Entra membership and SharePoint ACL |
| Effect evidence | Version history, approval record and audit readback |
| Retention and legal hold | Microsoft 365 retention and compliance controls |
| Infrastructure code | Only stable official provider surfaces where useful |
| Provider migration | Documented export, inventory and replacement procedure |

## Authority and source-of-truth boundaries

| Subject | Authoritative state | Non-authoritative surfaces |
|---|---|---|
| Business content | Approved exact file version in the owning department library | Agent summary, chat text, personal draft, copied report |
| Subject ownership | Exactly one owning department and responsible role | Last editor, file location alone |
| Permission | Current Entra group membership plus SharePoint ACL | Permission statement written inside a file or chat |
| Approval | Recorded approval for the exact target version and action | Agent statement that approval exists |
| Effect completion | Read-back version, location, permission and audit result | Agent statement that work succeeded |
| Retention/deletion | Current retention, legal hold and administrative state | A requested deletion date in a document |
| Agent conversation | Intent, explanation and recoverable draft | Formal business record unless explicitly materialized and approved |
| Generated summary | Replaceable projection linked to source versions | Original business source |

No single giant file, library, JSONL or chat thread is the universal SSOT. Each governed subject has one owning department and one authoritative current state for each concern.

## Role ownership

| Role | Owns | May consume | Must not do |
|---|---|---|---|
| CEO | Strategy, company policy, major decisions and risk acceptance | Approved summaries and decision material from all departments | Directly rewrite CFO, COO or CMO operational raw |
| COO | Operating procedures, delivery, incidents, capacity and work progress | CEO direction, CFO constraints and CMO demand evidence | Rewrite finance books or marketing-owned raw |
| CFO | Cash, budget, accounting, billing, payment and financial forecast | Approved requests and operational evidence from other teams | Rewrite other departments' claimed results to fit finance |
| CMO | Market, campaigns, customer segments, acquisition and pipeline creation | Approved finance limits, operating capacity and CEO direction | Rewrite finance or operations raw |
| Every role | Its own department subjects | Approved references, requests and results from others | Share direct write ownership of the same subject |

## File lifecycle

| State | Human action | Agent action | Authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Personal draft | Edit in personal OneDrive | Read, revise and organize | None |
| Department draft | Collaborate in department library | Create, update and prepare diff | None |
| Pending approval | Review exact delta and effect | Verify identity, version, permission and approval route | None |
| Approved current | Read and use | Publish or update the declared current version | Authoritative business content |
| Shared reference | Read permitted scope | Share original or create purpose-limited derivative | Reference to source authority |
| Archived/revoked | Normally not used | Move, revoke or mark inactive | Historical evidence |
| Legal hold | Restricted use | Read and organize only | Protected evidence |
| Physical deletion | Exceptional administrative action | Normally prohibited | Governed by retention and legal authority |

## CRUD contract

| Operation | Normal UX | Agent duty | Completion gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create | Ask Agent or create an Office draft | Select owner, permitted library, name and access | Valid destination, no forbidden duplicate and required approval |
| Read | Open file or ask Agent | Use only content visible to the requester | Current requester permission |
| Update | Edit draft or request change | Bind expected source version, produce delta and detect conflict | Expected version matches, permission and approval pass |
| Delete | Request archive, revoke, erasure or deletion | Distinguish lifecycle action and check retention/hold | Physical deletion requires separate authority |
| Move | Request destination | Check ownership, permission change and broken references | Source and destination permit the move |
| Share | Name recipient, purpose and duration | Apply minimum scope and expiry where needed | Sharing policy and required approval pass |
| Approve | Review exact target and effect | Fix version, approver and conditions | Correct accountable actor approves |
| Restore | Select prior version | Check conflicts and downstream impact | Post-restore readback succeeds |

## Formal update sequence

1. Human or Agent creates a draft.
2. Agent reads the exact source version, owning department, requester identity and current permission.
3. Agent shows the proposed delta, target, risk and expected effect.
4. Low-risk reversible work may proceed under accepted rules.
5. Medium/high-risk work waits for the correct human approval.
6. Agent or bounded service performs the Microsoft 365 effect.
7. The system reads back exact version, location, permission and audit state.
8. Completion is reported only when expected and observed states match.
9. Partial failure remains visible and is recovered or escalated.

## Risk levels

| Level | Examples | Agent limit | Human requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | Search, summarize, compare | May complete | None |
| R1 | Naming, folder organization, internal tagging, template creation | May complete if reversible | Normally none |
| R2 | Operational state or material content change | Prepare and execute within accepted rules | Owning department confirmation |
| R3 | Money, permissions, external sending, publication | Prepare exact effect only | Explicit accountable approval |
| R4 | Legal commitment, irreversible deletion, exceptional payment | Explain and prepare only | Named final authority |

Agent may execute; Agent never becomes the final accountable authority.

## Agent security boundary

- Use requester-delegated permission by default.
- A service identity is allowed only for a proven unattended operation.
- Service identity permission must be restricted by operation, department, library, target and duration.
- Agent must not read or answer from files the requester cannot access.
- Agent must not store credentials in file content or conversation.
- File content is untrusted data and must not override user instruction, role policy or administrative rules.
- Agent natural-language output is never sufficient effect evidence.
- Agent-specific memory or runtime state must not become business-content authority.

## Department handoff

| Handoff | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Question | Receiving team answers from information it owns and may disclose |
| Information delivery | Owning team shares an approved source or purpose-limited derivative |
| Change request | Receiving owner changes its own subject; requester never edits it directly |
| Approval request | Approver sees exact source, proposed delta, effect and accountable owner |
| Budget request | Requesting team supplies evidence; CFO owns the financial decision/result |
| Executive direction | CEO issues direction; each owning department records its own implementation result |
| Copy avoidance | Prefer permissioned source sharing over uncontrolled copies |
| Derived document | Record source versions, purpose, creator and time |

## Direct Office editing and continuity

- Human direct editing is allowed for drafts.
- Normal formal publication passes through Agent verification.
- Agent outage must not block reading or drafting.
- A bounded break-glass process may allow exceptional formal action.
- Every break-glass action must be reconciled after Agent recovery.
- Unreconciled break-glass work must remain visibly incomplete.

## Failure and recovery

| Failure | Required recovery |
|---|---|
| Agent unavailable | Continue Office reading and drafting; use bounded break-glass if necessary |
| Wrong content update | Restore through version history and read back the result |
| Wrong sharing | Revoke access, inspect audit and notify correct owner |
| Employee departure | Remove group membership, transfer owned content and inspect residual sharing |
| Agent vendor removal | Keep files, ACLs, versions and audit; connect a replacement Agent |
| Microsoft 365 outage | Use documented business-continuity copies and procedure for critical material |
| Acquisition transfer | Export department, group, library, owner, retention and exception inventories |

## Dependency policy

Depend heavily on Microsoft 365 while the dependency creates more value than it destroys. Do not build abstractions merely to appear vendor-neutral.

Maintain peelability through:

- exportable file formats or tested conversion;
- inventory of sites, libraries, files, groups, permissions, retention and exceptions;
- documented operation without the Agent;
- documented replacement of the Agent product;
- measured provider-exit scope, lost functions, duration and cost;
- no business authority stored only in Agent-specific memory, prompt or proprietary runtime;
- provider-specific code isolated at the smallest actual boundary.

## Infrastructure policy

- Terraform is optional, not a completion objective.
- Use official stable providers where they reduce risk, primarily for Entra group/application/role surfaces.
- Microsoft Admin Center, SharePoint administration and supported scripts are acceptable where no stable official Terraform surface exists.
- Do not add unstable community providers, `local-exec`, wrapper frameworks or generic control planes solely to claim IaC completeness.

## YAGNI lock

Do not build before a proven repeated gap:

- custom Web UI;
- custom Office editor;
- independent JSONL SSOT or deployment ledger;
- custom database or search platform;
- generic workflow engine;
- custom RBAC/ReBAC;
- generic provider plugin system;
- department-specific CRUD applications;
- universal business-object platform;
- always-on provider abstraction layer.

## Custom implementation admission

A custom component may be proposed only when at least one condition is observed with evidence:

1. The same finite unsupported operation repeats in at least two departments.
2. The same required relationship permission cannot be represented by native ACL in at least two departments.
3. A legal or business requirement cannot be met by native retention, audit or approval.
4. Agent cost, latency or failure exceeds an accepted threshold for a repeated operation.
5. A provider-exit exercise reveals an unacceptable non-exportable dependency.
6. Required external-system write access has no acceptable existing connector.

Any admitted implementation must close only that bounded gap. It must not create a generic platform unless two real consumers already require the same extracted boundary.

## Staged path

| Stage | Required result | Forbidden overbuild |
|---|---|---|
| V0 | `ism#1`: four roles, one real workflow each, permissions, Agent CRUD, approval, version recovery, cost and outage proof | All custom application code |
| V1 | Major internal workflows use the same role/ownership/effect pattern | General-purpose SaaS replacement |
| V2 | Cross-department request, approval, sharing and result return are repeatable | Independent cross-department ledger |
| V3 | Audit, retention, departure, incident and break-glass tests run regularly | Custom audit platform |
| V4 | Agent replacement, export and provider-exit inventory are physically tested | Permanent abstraction layer |
| Final | Every material subject has owner, authoritative version, permission, Agent path, evidence, recovery and transfer procedure | Unproved future functionality |

## Final acceptance gates

- [ ] Material subjects with unknown owning department: `0`.
- [ ] Material subjects with multiple direct-write owning departments: `0`.
- [ ] Unauthorized reads or updates in destructive tests: `0`.
- [ ] Normal formal CRUD paths bypassing Agent verification: `0`.
- [ ] High-risk effects completed without the correct human approval: `0`.
- [ ] Completed external effects without version/permission/audit readback: `0`.
- [ ] Updates without an exact expected source version: `0`.
- [ ] Updates without a tested recovery path: `0`.
- [ ] Unreconciled break-glass effects: `0`.
- [ ] Department-authoritative raw owned only by a departed user: `0`.
- [ ] Agent-only business authority or credentials: `0`.
- [ ] Each role has proved Agent-outage continuity.
- [ ] At least one Agent-product replacement has succeeded without moving business authority.
- [ ] File and permission export has been physically tested.
- [ ] Provider-exit inventory and estimated migration cost are current.
- [ ] New department onboarding requires no custom application change unless it introduces a proved new bounded capability.
- [ ] Agent cost is measurable per successful workflow.
- [ ] Work duration, failure, approval delay, audit collection time, recovery time and transfer time are measured.

## Destructive proofs

The final system must demonstrate rejection or containment of at least:

1. Cross-department unauthorized read.
2. Cross-department unauthorized write.
3. Stale-version overwrite.
4. Agent claim of success without effect.
5. Wrong destination library.
6. Permission expansion caused by move.
7. External share without approval.
8. Payment or financial commitment without approval.
9. Physical deletion under retention or legal hold.
10. Prompt injection inside an Office file.
11. Service identity exceeding its bounded target.
12. Employee departure leaving authoritative personal ownership.
13. Agent outage during a formal operation.
14. Partial external effect.
15. Provider export missing permissions, versions or retention state.

## Value measurements

- Workflow completion time.
- Human handling time.
- Agent cost per successful workflow.
- Permission violation and near-miss count.
- Wrong-version and recovery count.
- Approval waiting time.
- Audit-evidence collection time.
- New role and department onboarding time.
- Agent outage continuity time.
- Agent replacement duration.
- Provider-exit inventory time and estimated migration cost.

These measurements support, but do not by themselves prove, company-value improvement.

## Non-goals

- Making JSONL mandatory.
- Making Terraform the only control surface.
- Giving Agent final decision authority.
- Replacing Microsoft 365 with a custom SaaS.
- Creating a generic framework in anticipation of future providers.
- Claiming corporate-sale achievement from architecture or test completion.

## Closure rule

Do not close for a design document, a V0-only proof, a successful Agent demo, or zero custom code alone.

Close only when all material workflows in the accepted final scope satisfy ownership, permission, Agent verification, approval, exact-version effect, readback, recovery, outage continuity, Agent replacement, export and transfer gates, and all residuals are explicitly recorded.
"}

{"body":"## Status

```text
architectureTarget=true
implementationAuthority=false
v0Child=roccho-dev/ism#1
finalStateProved=false
businessOutcomeProved=false
```

## Relationship to V0

- `roccho-dev/ism#1` is the smallest executable V0 proof.
- This Issue defines the complete target state, permanent boundaries, staged path, destructive conditions, and final acceptance gates.
- Closing V0 does not close this Issue.
- This Issue does not require future components to be implemented before an observed need exists.

## Purpose

Establish a transferable, auditable and replaceable back-office operating model for CEO, COO, CFO and CMO teams in which:

- the only normal human UI is permitted OneDrive/SharePoint directories, Office files and Agent conversation;
- Agent participation is required for normal formal CRUD;
- Microsoft 365 provides identity, file UI, department ownership, versioning, approval, audit and retention;
- Agent, UI and provider remain replaceable without losing business files or permission ownership;
- custom software remains zero unless an observed repeated gap justifies one finite addition;
- the resulting operating capability lowers dependency on individual employees, diligence cost, integration ambiguity and transfer cost.

Technical completion alone does not prove increased company value or a completed corporate sale.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Purpose |
|---:|---|
| G0 | Complete a high-value corporate sale on acceptable terms |
| G1 | Increase realizable value and probability of completion |
| G2 | Reduce buyer uncertainty, residual liability and integration cost |
| G3 | Build transferable and independently verifiable operating capability |
| G4 | Make management predictable, accountable, recoverable and auditable |
| G5 | Unify file work, Agent-assisted CRUD, permissions, approval and readback |
| G6 | Define exact ownership, state, authority, evidence and closure contracts |

## One-line final state

```text
OneDrive / Office file UI
  → Agent conversation
  → current identity, ownership, permission, expected version and risk gate
  → human approval where required
  → Microsoft 365 effect
  → version, permission and audit readback
  → visible completion or residual
```

## Final responsibility split

| Concern | Final owner |
|---|---|
| Human file UI | OneDrive, SharePoint and Office |
| Department file ownership | SharePoint shared library |
| Personal draft | Business OneDrive |
| Human and group identity | Entra ID |
| File permission | SharePoint ACL constrained by Entra groups |
| Conversation and work planning | Replaceable Agent product |
| Business decision and accountability | Named human role |
| Normal CRUD entry | Agent conversation or Agent-mediated Office flow |
| High-risk approval | Correct accountable human |
| File version truth | Microsoft 365 version identity and stored bytes |
| Permission truth | Current Entra membership and SharePoint ACL |
| Effect evidence | Version history, approval record and audit readback |
| Retention and legal hold | Microsoft 365 retention and compliance controls |
| Infrastructure code | Only stable official provider surfaces where useful |
| Provider migration | Documented export, inventory and replacement procedure |

## Authority and source-of-truth boundaries

| Subject | Authoritative state | Non-authoritative surfaces |
|---|---|---|
| Business content | Approved exact file version in the owning department library | Agent summary, chat text, personal draft, copied report |
| Subject ownership | Exactly one owning department and responsible role | Last editor, file location alone |
| Permission | Current Entra group membership plus SharePoint ACL | Permission statement written inside a file or chat |
| Approval | Recorded approval for the exact target version and action | Agent statement that approval exists |
| Effect completion | Read-back version, location, permission and audit result | Agent statement that work succeeded |
| Retention/deletion | Current retention, legal hold and administrative state | A requested deletion date in a document |
| Agent conversation | Intent, explanation and recoverable draft | Formal business record unless explicitly materialized and approved |
| Generated summary | Replaceable projection linked to source versions | Original business source |

No single giant file, library, JSONL or chat thread is the universal SSOT. Each governed subject has one owning department and one authoritative current state for each concern.

## Role ownership

| Role | Owns | May consume | Must not do |
|---|---|---|---|
| CEO | Strategy, company policy, major decisions and risk acceptance | Approved summaries and decision material from all departments | Directly rewrite CFO, COO or CMO operational raw |
| COO | Operating procedures, delivery, incidents, capacity and work progress | CEO direction, CFO constraints and CMO demand evidence | Rewrite finance books or marketing-owned raw |
| CFO | Cash, budget, accounting, billing, payment and financial forecast | Approved requests and operational evidence from other teams | Rewrite other departments' claimed results to fit finance |
| CMO | Market, campaigns, customer segments, acquisition and pipeline creation | Approved finance limits, operating capacity and CEO direction | Rewrite finance or operations raw |
| Every role | Its own department subjects | Approved references, requests and results from others | Share direct write ownership of the same subject |

## File lifecycle

| State | Human action | Agent action | Authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| Personal draft | Edit in personal OneDrive | Read, revise and organize | None |
| Department draft | Collaborate in department library | Create, update and prepare diff | None |
| Pending approval | Review exact delta and effect | Verify identity, version, permission and approval route | None |
| Approved current | Read and use | Publish or update the declared current version | Authoritative business content |
| Shared reference | Read permitted scope | Share original or create purpose-limited derivative | Reference to source authority |
| Archived/revoked | Normally not used | Move, revoke or mark inactive | Historical evidence |
| Legal hold | Restricted use | Read and organize only | Protected evidence |
| Physical deletion | Exceptional administrative action | Normally prohibited | Governed by retention and legal authority |

## CRUD contract

| Operation | Normal UX | Agent duty | Completion gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create | Ask Agent or create an Office draft | Select owner, permitted library, name and access | Valid destination, no forbidden duplicate and required approval |
| Read | Open file or ask Agent | Use only content visible to the requester | Current requester permission |
| Update | Edit draft or request change | Bind expected source version, produce delta and detect conflict | Expected version matches, permission and approval pass |
| Delete | Request archive, revoke, erasure or deletion | Distinguish lifecycle action and check retention/hold | Physical deletion requires separate authority |
| Move | Request destination | Check ownership, permission change and broken references | Source and destination permit the move |
| Share | Name recipient, purpose and duration | Apply minimum scope and expiry where needed | Sharing policy and required approval pass |
| Approve | Review exact target and effect | Fix version, approver and conditions | Correct accountable actor approves |
| Restore | Select prior version | Check conflicts and downstream impact | Post-restore readback succeeds |

## Formal update sequence

1. Human or Agent creates a draft.
2. Agent reads the exact source version, owning department, requester identity and current permission.
3. Agent shows the proposed delta, target, risk and expected effect.
4. Low-risk reversible work may proceed under accepted rules.
5. Medium/high-risk work waits for the correct human approval.
6. Agent or bounded service performs the Microsoft 365 effect.
7. The system reads back exact version, location, permission and audit state.
8. Completion is reported only when expected and observed states match.
9. Partial failure remains visible and is recovered or escalated.

## Risk levels

| Level | Examples | Agent limit | Human requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | Search, summarize, compare | May complete | None |
| R1 | Naming, folder organization, internal tagging, template creation | May complete if reversible | Normally none |
| R2 | Operational state or material content change | Prepare and execute within accepted rules | Owning department confirmation |
| R3 | Money, permissions, external sending, publication | Prepare exact effect only | Explicit accountable approval |
| R4 | Legal commitment, irreversible deletion, exceptional payment | Explain and prepare only | Named final authority |

Agent may execute; Agent never becomes the final accountable authority.

## Agent security boundary

- Use requester-delegated permission by default.
- A service identity is allowed only for a proven unattended operation.
- Service identity permission must be restricted by operation, department, library, target and duration.
- Agent must not read or answer from files the requester cannot access.
- Agent must not store credentials in file content or conversation.
- File content is untrusted data and must not override user instruction, role policy or administrative rules.
- Agent natural-language output is never sufficient effect evidence.
- Agent-specific memory or runtime state must not become business-content authority.

## Department handoff

| Handoff | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Question | Receiving team answers from information it owns and may disclose |
| Information delivery | Owning team shares an approved source or purpose-limited derivative |
| Change request | Receiving owner changes its own subject; requester never edits it directly |
| Approval request | Approver sees exact source, proposed delta, effect and accountable owner |
| Budget request | Requesting team supplies evidence; CFO owns the financial decision/result |
| Executive direction | CEO issues direction; each owning department records its own implementation result |
| Copy avoidance | Prefer permissioned source sharing over uncontrolled copies |
| Derived document | Record source versions, purpose, creator and time |

## Direct Office editing and continuity

- Human direct editing is allowed for drafts.
- Normal formal publication passes through Agent verification.
- Agent outage must not block reading or drafting.
- A bounded break-glass process may allow exceptional formal action.
- Every break-glass action must be reconciled after Agent recovery.
- Unreconciled break-glass work must remain visibly incomplete.

## Failure and recovery

| Failure | Required recovery |
|---|---|
| Agent unavailable | Continue Office reading and drafting; use bounded break-glass if necessary |
| Wrong content update | Restore through version history and read back the result |
| Wrong sharing | Revoke access, inspect audit and notify correct owner |
| Employee departure | Remove group membership, transfer owned content and inspect residual sharing |
| Agent vendor removal | Keep files, ACLs, versions and audit; connect a replacement Agent |
| Microsoft 365 outage | Use documented business-continuity copies and procedure for critical material |
| Acquisition transfer | Export department, group, library, owner, retention and exception inventories |

## Dependency policy

Depend heavily on Microsoft 365 while the dependency creates more value than it destroys. Do not build abstractions merely to appear vendor-neutral.

Maintain peelability through:

- exportable file formats or tested conversion;
- inventory of sites, libraries, files, groups, permissions, retention and exceptions;
- documented operation without the Agent;
- documented replacement of the Agent product;
- measured provider-exit scope, lost functions, duration and cost;
- no business authority stored only in Agent-specific memory, prompt or proprietary runtime;
- provider-specific code isolated at the smallest actual boundary.

## Infrastructure policy

- Terraform is optional, not a completion objective.
- Use official stable providers where they reduce risk, primarily for Entra group/application/role surfaces.
- Microsoft Admin Center, SharePoint administration and supported scripts are acceptable where no stable official Terraform surface exists.
- Do not add unstable community providers, `local-exec`, wrapper frameworks or generic control planes solely to claim IaC completeness.

## YAGNI lock

Do not build before a proven repeated gap:

- custom Web UI;
- custom Office editor;
- independent JSONL SSOT or deployment ledger;
- custom database or search platform;
- generic workflow engine;
- custom RBAC/ReBAC;
- generic provider plugin system;
- department-specific CRUD applications;
- universal business-object platform;
- always-on provider abstraction layer.

## Custom implementation admission

A custom component may be proposed only when at least one condition is observed with evidence:

1. The same finite unsupported operation repeats in at least two departments.
2. The same required relationship permission cannot be represented by native ACL in at least two departments.
3. A legal or business requirement cannot be met by native retention, audit or approval.
4. Agent cost, latency or failure exceeds an accepted threshold for a repeated operation.
5. A provider-exit exercise reveals an unacceptable non-exportable dependency.
6. Required external-system write access has no acceptable existing connector.

Any admitted implementation must close only that bounded gap. It must not create a generic platform unless two real consumers already require the same extracted boundary.

## Staged path

| Stage | Required result | Forbidden overbuild |
|---|---|---|
| V0 | `ism#1`: four roles, one real workflow each, permissions, Agent CRUD, approval, version recovery, cost and outage proof | All custom application code |
| V1 | Major internal workflows use the same role/ownership/effect pattern | General-purpose SaaS replacement |
| V2 | Cross-department request, approval, sharing and result return are repeatable | Independent cross-department ledger |
| V3 | Audit, retention, departure, incident and break-glass tests run regularly | Custom audit platform |
| V4 | Agent replacement, export and provider-exit inventory are physically tested | Permanent abstraction layer |
| Final | Every material subject has owner, authoritative version, permission, Agent path, evidence, recovery and transfer procedure | Unproved future functionality |

## Final acceptance gates

- [ ] Material subjects with unknown owning department: `0`.
- [ ] Material subjects with multiple direct-write owning departments: `0`.
- [ ] Unauthorized reads or updates in destructive tests: `0`.
- [ ] Normal formal CRUD paths bypassing Agent verification: `0`.
- [ ] High-risk effects completed without the correct human approval: `0`.
- [ ] Completed external effects without version/permission/audit readback: `0`.
- [ ] Updates without an exact expected source version: `0`.
- [ ] Updates without a tested recovery path: `0`.
- [ ] Unreconciled break-glass effects: `0`.
- [ ] Department-authoritative raw owned only by a departed user: `0`.
- [ ] Agent-only business authority or credentials: `0`.
- [ ] Each role has proved Agent-outage continuity.
- [ ] At least one Agent-product replacement has succeeded without moving business authority.
- [ ] File and permission export has been physically tested.
- [ ] Provider-exit inventory and estimated migration cost are current.
- [ ] New department onboarding requires no custom application change unless it introduces a proved new bounded capability.
- [ ] Agent cost is measurable per successful workflow.
- [ ] Work duration, failure, approval delay, audit collection time, recovery time and transfer time are measured.

## Destructive proofs

The final system must demonstrate rejection or containment of at least:

1. Cross-department unauthorized read.
2. Cross-department unauthorized write.
3. Stale-version overwrite.
4. Agent claim of success without effect.
5. Wrong destination library.
6. Permission expansion caused by move.
7. External share without approval.
8. Payment or financial commitment without approval.
9. Physical deletion under retention or legal hold.
10. Prompt injection inside an Office file.
11. Service identity exceeding its bounded target.
12. Employee departure leaving authoritative personal ownership.
13. Agent outage during a formal operation.
14. Partial external effect.
15. Provider export missing permissions, versions or retention state.

## Value measurements

- Workflow completion time.
- Human handling time.
- Agent cost per successful workflow.
- Permission violation and near-miss count.
- Wrong-version and recovery count.
- Approval waiting time.
- Audit-evidence collection time.
- New role and department onboarding time.
- Agent outage continuity time.
- Agent replacement duration.
- Provider-exit inventory time and estimated migration cost.

These measurements support, but do not by themselves prove, company-value improvement.

## Non-goals

- Making JSONL mandatory.
- Making Terraform the only control surface.
- Giving Agent final decision authority.
- Replacing Microsoft 365 with a custom SaaS.
- Creating a generic framework in anticipation of future providers.
- Claiming corporate-sale achievement from architecture or test completion.

## Closure rule

Do not close for a design document, a V0-only proof, a successful Agent demo, or zero custom code alone.

Close only when all material workflows in the accepted final scope satisfy ownership, permission, Agent verification, approval, exact-version effect, readback, recovery, outage continuity, Agent replacement, export and transfer gates, and all residuals are explicitly recorded.

- Do not move projection building into UI.

## Checks

- Boundary doc/static check passes.
- Existing repo-map tests still pass.

## Why this matters

Fix `ui` as the read-only visualization side of the editor-to-queue-to-ui flow.

## Scope

- Document that `ui` emits `ui.targetRef.v1` metadata for local/dev tooling.
- Document that `ui` reads external `repoMap.projection.v1` artifacts.
- Document that `ui` does not write queue rows, accepted ledger rows, admission receipts, or model authority.
- Preserve localhost preview as non-authority evidence.

## Done

- README/docs clearly state: `ui = targetRef emitter + projection reader + preview`.
- Boundary check rejects state-store/admission/ledger ownership in UI packages.
- Existing repo-map external input, targetRef, and localhost preview docs remain consistent.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly supports the visible `ui` end of editor-to-queue-to-ui while preserving repo boundaries.
- Core/port/adapter: view core consumes projection and emits targetRef metadata; projection input and targetRef are ports; renderer/localhost/browser are adapters.
- Pure/effect split: view model normalization is pure; DOM, browser, server, file artifact, and hot reload behavior are adapter-only.
- False-positive exclusion: checks allow ui to emit targetRef and read projection artifacts as non-authority view behavior.
- False-negative exclusion: checks fail if ui writes queue, admission, accepted ledger, model authority, or runtime worker state.
- Authority boundary: ui artifacts, previews, targetRefs, and manifests are evidence/view only.
- Repo cleanliness: ui owns rendering and preview adapters only, not queue runtime or accepted model state.

- Do not add accepted ledger or admission code.

{"body":"recordId: `HQ-VERIFIED-RESOURCE-INVOCATION-V1`

## Authority

- Parent latest-writer decision: roccho-dev/adrs#211 comment `4978001609`.
- Accepted gap and closure authority: roccho-dev/adrs#222.
- roccho-dev/adrs#220 remains unchanged and independently closable.

## Scope

Add one second operation form under the existing `local-tool` target:

```text
selected hq.local-tool.v1 resource
  + ordered non-secret argv[]
  -> existing instruction.v1 and accepted ledger
  -> approval_required/held until exact digest-bound approval
  -> existing managed worker
  -> existing verified binding and direct executor
  -> existing result.v1
```

Finite named actions remain unchanged and remain the promotion target for repeated typed operations.

## Required implementation

1. Extend one selected local-tool resource with a bounded invocation policy; allow a resource to expose invocation without declaring a per-subcommand action.
2. Accept a strict resource invocation payload containing only tool ID, tool version, and ordered argv.
3. Reject empty argv, empty args, excessive arg count/bytes, and resource-policy authority-escape options before provider preparation.
4. Treat missing approval as held: append policy evidence and accepted evidence, start zero process, emit no terminal blocked result, and permit the same queued run to become runnable after a later exact approval.
5. Keep stale/mismatched approval, invalid payload, policy rejection, unknown resource, stale binding, and executable tampering terminally non-green with zero process start.
6. Reuse the existing local-tool preparer, verified binding registry, direct executor, empty environment, timeout/output bounds, provider evidence, recovery, redaction, cancellation, and result vocabulary.
7. Add deterministic AWS-shaped multi-subcommand proof data and destructive tests. Physical restricted-AWS evidence remains required before adrs#222 closure.

## Fixed exclusions

No shell or command string; executable path; PATH/cwd/shim/plugin/filesystem discovery; queue-owned environment/credential/profile/account/config selection; stdin; PTY/TUI; interactive authentication; generic SSH/OCI; workflow graph; second queue/worker/executor/result; automatic agent submit; automatic finite-action promotion.

## Merge gates

- one resource registration supports at least three distinct argv vectors with zero per-subcommand action/command definitions;
- missing approval is durable held work and starts zero process;
- exact approval resumes the same queued run and executes once;
- denied option, stale approval, unknown resource, binding mismatch, digest tamper, and shell punctuation destructive cases pass;
- existing finite local-tool tests remain green;
- repository Linux and Windows CI pass at the exact final head;
- PR is mergeable, non-draft, has no unresolved review thread, and its final diff creates no parallel runtime.

## Closure relation

Closing this issue and merging its implementation PR are necessary but not sufficient to close adrs#222. adrs#222 additionally requires the restricted AWS physical multi-subcommand evidence and final authority readback."}

{"body":"recordId: `HQ-VERIFIED-RESOURCE-INVOCATION-V1`

## Authority

- Parent latest-writer decision: roccho-dev/adrs#211 comment `4978001609`.
- Accepted gap and closure authority: roccho-dev/adrs#222.
- roccho-dev/adrs#220 remains unchanged and independently closable.

## Scope

Add one second operation form under the existing `local-tool` target:

```text
selected hq.local-tool.v1 resource
  + ordered non-secret argv[]
  -> existing instruction.v1 and accepted ledger
  -> approval_required/held until exact digest-bound approval
  -> existing managed worker
  -> existing verified binding and direct executor
  -> existing result.v1
```

Finite named actions remain unchanged and remain the promotion target for repeated typed operations.

## Required implementation

1. Extend one selected local-tool resource with a bounded invocation policy; allow a resource to expose invocation without declaring a per-subcommand action.
2. Accept a strict resource invocation payload containing only tool ID, tool version, and ordered argv.
3. Reject empty argv, empty args, excessive arg count/bytes, and resource-policy authority-escape options before provider preparation.
4. Treat missing approval as held: append policy evidence and accepted evidence, start zero process, emit no terminal blocked result, and permit the same queued run to become runnable after a later exact approval.
5. Keep stale/mismatched approval, invalid payload, policy rejection, unknown resource, stale binding, and executable tampering terminally non-green with zero process start.
6. Reuse the existing local-tool preparer, verified binding registry, direct executor, empty environment, timeout/output bounds, provider evidence, recovery, redaction, cancellation, and result vocabulary.
7. Add deterministic AWS-shaped multi-subcommand proof data and destructive tests. Physical restricted-AWS evidence remains required before adrs#222 closure.

## Fixed exclusions

No shell or command string; executable path; PATH/cwd/shim/plugin/filesystem discovery; queue-owned environment/credential/profile/account/config selection; stdin; PTY/TUI; interactive authentication; generic SSH/OCI; workflow graph; second queue/worker/executor/result; automatic agent submit; automatic finite-action promotion.

## Merge gates

- one resource registration supports at least three distinct argv vectors with zero per-subcommand action/command definitions;
- missing approval is durable held work and starts zero process;
- exact approval resumes the same queued run and executes once;
- denied option, stale approval, unknown resource, binding mismatch, digest tamper, and shell punctuation destructive cases pass;
- existing finite local-tool tests remain green;
- repository Linux and Windows CI pass at the exact final head;
- PR is mergeable, non-draft, has no unresolved review thread, and its final diff creates no parallel runtime.

## Closure relation

Closing this issue and merging its implementation PR are necessary but not sufficient to close adrs#222. adrs#222 additionally requires the restricted AWS physical multi-subcommand evidence and final authority readback."}

{"body":"## 背景・目的

既存の coding 主力は Codex / Claude Code、安価な coding-model pool 候補は OpenCode Go（[ADRS #530](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/530)）。
そこへ、役割が異なる二つの既存FOSSを**必要な時だけ使える**ようにしておきたい。

| 道具 | 使いたい能力 | 非目的 |
|---|---|---|
| Ollama | local / cloud LLM inference。Goの補助・代替候補 | 新model router、daemon常駐、契約代行 |
| Ollaya | local System One決定（分類・選択・点数、TypeSafe互換） | Jev退役、独自判断core、学習・蒸留 |

Ollayaは [ops PR #441](https://github.com/roccho-org/ops/pull/441) にCPU artifact replay PASS、[ops PR #443](https://github.com/roccho-org/ops/pull/443) にWinnow CPU評価（35/36、p50 33.748s）という先行証拠がある。速いモデルを無条件で保証しない。

参照: [ADRS #530](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/530) / [ADRS #520](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/520) / [ADRS #465](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/465) / [ADRS #443](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/443)。

## repo責務と最小構成

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph WIN["windows / oci/dev"]
    N["pinned Nix profile"]
    OL["ollama CLI + local runtime"]
    AY["ollaya CLI + local System One runtime"]
    N --> OL
    N --> AY
  end
  subgraph External["任意の外部入力"]
    EN["envs: Ollama Cloud key（別Issue）"]
    M["Ollaya model registry（初回pull）"]
  end
  EN -. "認証済み時のみ" .-> OL
  M -. "使用時のみ" .-> AY
```

**windowsは実行可能なbinとOCI境界だけ所有**する。API key、契約・請求、provider固有判断契約、model選択の意味を所有しない。

## 完成条件（現地配置とsourceを区別）

1. 既存の固定Nixpkgs / exact release pinで、oci/devのprofileから `ollama` と `ollaya` が呼べる。実行時latestを勝手に入れない。
2. CPU-only、起動時daemon 0、port公開 0、model自動download 0。現在のPi/Jev/gh-auth/envs設定の意味を変えない。
3. CLIの版・helpと、非秘密のlocal-only実行入口をCIで検査する。少なくとも配布物として呼べることを実証する。
4. Ollayaは既存`/v1/systemone`を使う。新しいSystem One adapter/評価基盤を作らない。local `127.0.0.1:11435`のみ、公開portなし。
5. Ollama localは `127.0.0.1:11434`のみ。Cloud keyはenvs経由の別境界で扱い、CLI製品に平文を入れない。
6. exact-head CI / protected PR review / normal merge / canonical CIでsourceを閉じ、実環境のimage更新・モデル初回pull・Cloud実通信は別のreadbackとして残す。

## 破壊条件

- ① Go用`pi_auth_command`を変更する ② keyをGit、log、argvに置く ③ 自動でservice/daemonを起動する
- ④ local APIを`0.0.0.0`へ出す ⑤ 自動model pullや巨大modelのimage同梱 ⑥ GPU依存をデフォルト化
- ⑦ Jevのaccepted判断をOllayaの結果で上書きする ⑧ CPUモデルの速度未確認を即時PASSとする
- ⑨ 同じ provider adapter をopsとwindowsで二重開発 ⑩ CIsのfixture PASSをlive利用PASSと呼ぶ
- ⑪ /nix store再作成時に鍵やモデルを不可逆消失させる ⑫ 偽のCloud key疎通を成功として記録する

## Source PR

[PR roccho-dev/windows#66](https://github.com/roccho-dev/windows/pull/66)（Draft）— 既存OCI profileへCLIを追加。model storeは既存work volume、実key・実provider応答は別gate。

## Scope

最小source PRは`oci/dev`のprofile/依存と必要なら同じ既存proofだけ。独立provider/router framework、envs secretの新authority、opsのJev代替判断は追加しない。

body: This Issue owns the shared renderer capability only. It does not own publication admission, routes, canonicals, sitemap topology, discovery policy, provider-neutral bundle meaning, deployment, or final product closure.

Extract and harden a framework-neutral A2UI/SDUI semantic document renderer that converts approved semantic component inputs into complete HTML documents and HTML fragments for `web-publication` and future consumers.
The renderer must be reusable beyond LLMO/SEO examples and must not import `webPublication.*` product semantics.
| Scope | Reuse and harden the existing A2UI JSONL-to-HTML capability as a stable library. |
| Product | Give `web-publication` one shared semantic renderer instead of a copied local renderer. |
| Architecture | Preserve `ui = semantic component/renderer owner`, not publication owner. |
| Quality | Enforce semantic elements, escaping, raw-HTML rejection, accessibility and document/fragment consistency. |
| Reuse | Support multiple external products through one versioned port. |
| Transfer | Make renderer compatibility and output provenance inspectable through receipts. |
| Meta | Reduce duplicated renderer cost and lock-in across sellable products. |
Provide `ui.semanticHtmlRenderer.v1` with separate document and fragment requests.
- approved semantic component tree or A2UI surface/data compatible with the shared catalog;
- title/head fields supplied by the caller;
- approved interaction attributes such as HTMX request/target/swap fields;
- caller-owned opaque identity/provenance fields that are returned unchanged.
Add only reusable document/Web components that have stable semantic meaning, for example:
Do not add publication-specific route admission, source graph resolution, sitemap, keyword, ranking, or customer-domain logic.
- refactor existing `a2ui-shell-builder`/document renderer capability rather than introduce a second renderer;
- define the versioned port and conformance fixtures;
- ensure full-document output includes doctype, language, head/body/main structure, title and caller-supplied canonical/head metadata without deciding those values;
- ensure fragments contain no accidental full-document shell;
- preserve HTML escaping and reject untrusted raw HTML;
- validate heading outline, link/button semantics, IDs/targets, and allowed interaction attributes;
- render documents and HTMX fragments through the same catalog and component mappings;
- emit deterministic renderer receipts and output digests;
- expose a library entrypoint usable from a pinned external consumer;
- [ ] One public renderer implementation serves documents and fragments.
- [ ] Existing renderer logic is reused/refactored; duplicate renderer paths are removed or explicitly retained as adapters.
- [ ] Same input produces identical HTML bytes/digest.
- [ ] Values are escaped and raw external HTML is rejected.
- [ ] Unsupported component or property fails closed.
- [ ] Exactly one primary H1 can be enforced when requested by the caller contract.
- [ ] Links produce real `a[href]`; actions that are not navigation produce buttons.
- [ ] Citation/fallback link semantics survive HTMX enhancement.
- [ ] Fragment target IDs and interaction attributes are validated without resolving publication routes.
- [ ] Renderer returns no route/admission/canonical authority fields.
- [ ] No Astro dependency or `.astro` template is required by the renderer.
- [ ] A conformance fixture from `web#3` renders a complete document and fragment.
- [ ] Renderer revision/digest and output digests are recorded in a non-authority receipt.
- [ ] Existing UI tests and artifacts remain green.
- navigation action emitted only as button;
- fragment unexpectedly contains full document shell;
- caller attempts to pass approval/authority fields;
- product/customer vocabulary enters shared component implementation;
- document and fragment use different semantic mappings;
- Astro becomes required for HTML output.

Merge only after the versioned contract, deterministic library entrypoint, semantic catalog, document/fragment conformance, destructive cases, dependency boundary, exact revision/digest receipt, and existing UI regression suite are green. The selected external consumer must be able to pin and call this renderer without copying source.

body: This Issue owns the shared renderer capability only. It does not own publication admission, routes, canonicals, sitemap topology, discovery policy, provider-neutral bundle meaning, deployment, or final product closure.

Extract and harden a framework-neutral A2UI/SDUI semantic document renderer that converts approved semantic component inputs into complete HTML documents and HTML fragments for `web-publication` and future consumers.
The renderer must be reusable beyond LLMO/SEO examples and must not import `webPublication.*` product semantics.
| Scope | Reuse and harden the existing A2UI JSONL-to-HTML capability as a stable library. |
| Product | Give `web-publication` one shared semantic renderer instead of a copied local renderer. |
| Architecture | Preserve `ui = semantic component/renderer owner`, not publication owner. |
| Quality | Enforce semantic elements, escaping, raw-HTML rejection, accessibility and document/fragment consistency. |
| Reuse | Support multiple external products through one versioned port. |
| Transfer | Make renderer compatibility and output provenance inspectable through receipts. |
| Meta | Reduce duplicated renderer cost and lock-in across sellable products. |
Provide `ui.semanticHtmlRenderer.v1` with separate document and fragment requests.
- approved semantic component tree or A2UI surface/data compatible with the shared catalog;
- title/head fields supplied by the caller;
- approved interaction attributes such as HTMX request/target/swap fields;
- caller-owned opaque identity/provenance fields that are returned unchanged.
Add only reusable document/Web components that have stable semantic meaning, for example:
Do not add publication-specific route admission, source graph resolution, sitemap, keyword, ranking, or customer-domain logic.
- refactor existing `a2ui-shell-builder`/document renderer capability rather than introduce a second renderer;
- define the versioned port and conformance fixtures;
- ensure full-document output includes doctype, language, head/body/main structure, title and caller-supplied canonical/head metadata without deciding those values;
- ensure fragments contain no accidental full-document shell;
- preserve HTML escaping and reject untrusted raw HTML;
- validate heading outline, link/button semantics, IDs/targets, and allowed interaction attributes;
- render documents and HTMX fragments through the same catalog and component mappings;
- emit deterministic renderer receipts and output digests;
- expose a library entrypoint usable from a pinned external consumer;
- [ ] One public renderer implementation serves documents and fragments.
- [ ] Existing renderer logic is reused/refactored; duplicate renderer paths are removed or explicitly retained as adapters.
- [ ] Same input produces identical HTML bytes/digest.
- [ ] Values are escaped and raw external HTML is rejected.
- [ ] Unsupported component or property fails closed.
- [ ] Exactly one primary H1 can be enforced when requested by the caller contract.
- [ ] Links produce real `a[href]`; actions that are not navigation produce buttons.
- [ ] Citation/fallback link semantics survive HTMX enhancement.
- [ ] Fragment target IDs and interaction attributes are validated without resolving publication routes.
- [ ] Renderer returns no route/admission/canonical authority fields.
- [ ] No Astro dependency or `.astro` template is required by the renderer.
- [ ] A conformance fixture from `web#3` renders a complete document and fragment.
- [ ] Renderer revision/digest and output digests are recorded in a non-authority receipt.
- [ ] Existing UI tests and artifacts remain green.
- navigation action emitted only as button;
- fragment unexpectedly contains full document shell;
- caller attempts to pass approval/authority fields;
- product/customer vocabulary enters shared component implementation;
- document and fragment use different semantic mappings;
- Astro becomes required for HTML output.

Merge only after the versioned contract, deterministic library entrypoint, semantic catalog, document/fragment conformance, destructive cases, dependency boundary, exact revision/digest receipt, and existing UI regression suite are green. The selected external consumer must be able to pin and call this renderer without copying source.

body: Turn the merged workspace, approval, and redaction contracts into one mandatory worker execution sequence. Safety must constrain the real path, not remain an independently tested package.
| scope | Integrates F-lane safety into C/D worker and adapter execution. |
| product | Gives every target one shared safety path. |
| system | Prevents dispatch or durable logging from bypassing approval and redaction. |
| organization | Removes adapter-owner discretion over common safety. |
| business/meta | Reduces incident, handoff, and technical-DD risk. |
- validation precedes approval, redaction, durable append, and dispatch;
- approval-required work never reaches an adapter without exact approval;
- secret fixtures do not survive in durable policy/result records.
No concrete adapter may reorder or bypass this sequence.
- compose `internal/workersafety` into the worker processing path;
- bind policy decision to exact canonical instruction digest;
- redact all durable policy, stdout, stderr, error, final metadata, and final text/path records where applicable;
- pass only approved validated requests to registry/adapter;
- fail closed when policy or redaction fails;
- preserve canonical `validation.v1` and `result.v1` as durable contracts.
- [ ] Worker invokes policy before registry lookup or adapter execution.
- [ ] `require_approval` without exact current instruction-digest approval produces durable blocked evidence and zero adapter calls.
- [ ] Stale or mismatched approval produces zero adapter calls.
- [ ] A safe approved fixture reaches a fake adapter exactly once.
- [ ] Policy evidence is redacted before durable append.
- [ ] Adapter stdout, stderr, final answer, error, and metadata are redacted before `result.v1` append.
- [ ] Known secret fixture plaintext is absent from every durable file and proof artifact.
- [ ] Redaction or policy internal failure fails closed and produces no dispatch.
- [ ] Adapter cannot override the worker-owned policy decision or canonical lifecycle fields.
- [ ] Restart/readback preserves the same blocked/completed projection.
The issue is not complete if any succeeds:
1. registry lookup or adapter call occurs before policy;
2. adapter runs when approval is missing, stale, or digest-mismatched;
3. secret plaintext reaches durable JSONL or final artifact;
4. redaction failure falls back to unredacted append;
5. adapter supplies its own approval or risk result;
6. policy result is stored only as terminal text;
7. blocked work creates a completed session;
8. one target bypasses the common path.
- allow, block, pending, stale, and digest-mismatch fixtures;
Merge only when safety is mandatory in the real common worker path and negative tests prove no adapter or durable append can bypass it.

{"body":"## Purpose

Emit actionable blocking findings for required repo packet problems before org join can mark a repo active.

Parent phase issue: #80

## Scope

This is an issue for a future governance implementation PR. Do not open or implement the PR from this issue alone.

## Requirements

- Consume D1 required repo universe output.
- Consume D2 packet registry/transport output.
- Emit finding for required repo missing packet.
- Emit finding for missing packet source.
- Emit finding for packet fetch/read failure.
- Emit finding for unpinned packet source.
- Emit finding for malformed packet.
- Emit finding for unsupported schema version.
- Emit finding for stale packet/sourceRev according to freshness rule.
- Emit finding for missing producer provenance.
- Emit finding for producerRepo mismatch.
- Emit finding for producerRev mismatch.
- Emit finding for packetDigest/outputDigest mismatch where available.
- Findings must include `repoId`, `expected`, `actual`, `delta`, `diagnosticClass`, `likelyOwner`, `nextAction`, and relevant digests/refs.
- Findings must be deterministic and stable sorted.
- Findings must not claim final admission by themselves.

## Done when

- Clean fixture emits no blocking packet findings.
- Missing packet fixture emits stable actionable finding.
- Stale packet fixture emits stable actionable finding.
- Malformed packet fixture emits stable actionable finding.
- Invalid producer metadata fixture emits stable actionable finding.
- CLI/check returns nonzero for blocking dirty fixtures when run in strict finding mode.

{"body":"## Purpose
Require explicit approval or blocking behavior for potentially destructive worker actions.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Keeps editor-selected rows from becoming unsafe auto-execution. |
| product | Makes execution policy explicit. |
| system/org | Supports safe human-in-the-loop boundaries. |
| business/meta | Reduces operational risk for agent factory use. |

## Scope
- Define `policy.allow_auto`, `policy.require_approval`, and blocked behavior.
- Add examples for safe auto-run and dangerous blocked rows.

## Non-scope
- Full permission server.
- UI approval workflow.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dangerous operations can be represented as blocked/pending approval.
- [ ] Worker does not execute approval-required rows automatically.
- [ ] Policy result is stored as JSONL event.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Destructive row executes because it came from Vim/hq.
- [ ] Approval state exists only in free text.

## Evidence
- Policy fixtures.
- Tests.

## Merge condition
Merge only when dangerous work cannot auto-run without explicit policy approval."}

{"body":"<!-- resource-landscape-topology-20261019-v1 -->

## 目的・位置付け

Own / Rent / 各Providerの実体、配置先、任せる仕事、依存を一枚で俯瞰するための**読取用全体図**。配置の重複、移行費用、運用負荷を減らし、低コストで継続改善できる開発工場と顧客向け基盤を作る。

**状態：現状調査＋設計案。実装・実機採用・Provider契約の採択を意味しない。**
確認基準：2026-10-19 JST。ここに配置・秘密・認証・契約・稼働の第二正本を作らない。

| 既存Issue | 所有する内容 | このIssueとの境界 |
|---|---|---|
| [resources #1](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/1) | Host識別、contains / manages、任意wrapの宣言と整合性 | Host relationの実装・検証は#1 |
| [ADRS #630](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/630) | Host relationの意味・admission | 意味の変更はしない |
| [resources #25](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/25) | Windows repoからresourcesへの移管・閉包 | 移行・archiveの証拠は#25 |
| [resources #10](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/10)、[#52](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/52) | NixOS上OCI、Windows own/rent OCIの個別受入 | 配備済み・稼働成功とは推定しない |
| 各repo / Provider / envs | 実装source、API、Binding、資格情報、実作用 | 本図はリンクするだけ |

## 表現規則

- **Resource / Host / Provider / Provider内サービス＝すべてsubgraphのみ。** Resource自体をnodeにしない。
- **実体node＝原則package・CLI・API endpoint・保存物。** 機能概念はノードの説明であり新たな実行エンジンではない。
- Own / Rentは所有区分。Windows / NixOSはOS。OCIは包含される実行環境。公式nixos/nix imageはNixOSではない。
- 実線は確認できた実装依存または供給経路。点線は採用・適用・実稼働が別途要確認の経路。いずれも権限や稼働成功を自動証明しない。
- 同じpackageを複数Hostに展開しても実装sourceを複製しない。Host IDはrepo名・OS・imageから導かない。

## Resource実体MMD

~~~mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph OWN["Own｜自己所有"]
    direction LR
    subgraph OW["Windows｜Own"]
      direction TB
      subgraph OOCI["OCI｜windows-own"]
        OC["Codex CLI"]
        OP["Pi CLI"]
        OA["Claude CLI"]
        OO["OpenCode CLI"]
      end
      subgraph NIXIMG["OCI｜公式 nixos/nix・bootstrap"]
        NX["Nix CLI"]
      end
    end
    subgraph ON["NixOS｜VersaPro"]
      direction TB
      BC["bcon｜Terminal"]
      subgraph VOCI["OCI｜versapro-own-oci・統合未証明"]
        VC["Codex CLI"]
        VP["Pi CLI"]
        VT["ops-typellm｜供給定義"]
      end
    end
  end
  subgraph RENT["Rent｜借用"]
    subgraph RW["Windows｜Rent"]
      subgraph ROCI["OCI｜windows-rent"]
        RC["Codex CLI"]
        RA["Claude CLI"]
        RN["Nix・Git・gh"]
      end
    end
  end
  subgraph GH["GitHub"]
    direction LR
    subgraph REPOS["Repositories"]
      RES["resources｜Host構成・OCI供給"]
      JP["ops/packages/jev"]
      TP["ops/packages/typellm"]
      APP["apps｜voice-ui"]
      EN["envs｜Binding"]
      ADR["adrs｜意思決定"]
    end
    subgraph ACT["Actions"]
      CI["CI・Build・Publish"]
    end
    subgraph REG["GHCR"]
      OIMG["windows-own image digest"]
      RIMG["windows-rent image digest"]
    end
  end
  subgraph CF["Cloudflare"]
    direction LR
    subgraph WK["Workers"]
      VOICE["voice-ui｜実配備未確認"]
      GOV["gov-release-proxy｜実装"]
    end

      SESSION["会話状態｜候補"]
    end

    end

  subgraph AWS["AWS"]
    subgraph LAMBDA["Lambda"]

        GEM["generateContent"]
      end

~~~

図中のCLIノードは**供給・構成候補の実体名**であり、すべてのHostで現在同時に稼働中という意味ではない。Providerに「外部サービス」の共通親を設けない。Jev / TypeLLMは独立API・package・credential。Gemini Developer APIとVertex AI、Gmailと有料GWS契約は同一視しない。

## 責務表・確認範囲

| Resource | 基本責務 | 確認結果 / 留保 |
|---|---|---|
| Own Windows | GUI・人の操作・own OCI | own imageは公開済み。現在のHost適用版は別途照合 |
| Own NixOS | TTY・Host管理・開発実行 | VersaPro導入歴あり。直近実機運用・再接続未完を保持 |
| Own Windows / 公式nixos/nix OCI | 一時Nix bootstrap | NixOS・own/rent製品imageと区別 |
| Own NixOS / OCI | Codex/Pi等の隔離実行 | [#10](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/10)の統合実証未完 |
| Rent Windows / OCI | 借用先Agent実行 | rent image公開済み。実機受入は別 |
| GitHub / resources | source・CI・GHCR・Release | [PR #31](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/pull/31)の公開取得実証。旧windows repoはarchive済み、Windows Hostは存続 |
| GitHub / ops | Jev・TypeLLMの独立実装 | endpointをsourceで確認。consumer採用と実疎通は独立 |
| Cloudflare | 公開Worker・状態・保存・メール経路 | PoC / source / 実配備を混同しない |
| AWS | 既存Lambda・Bedrock・S3 | slideの既存実行記録。今回現行repo/headは未照合 |
| Google | GCP/Google AIのGemini、GWS製品群のGmail/Drive/Calendar | API/課金/契約を別判定 |
| TypeSafe AI / TypeLLM | Noul/Choice/Score・型付き生成 | Providerと秘密情報を別々に所有 |
| その他モデルProvider | OpenAI・Anthropic・DeepSeek・OpenCode | CLI・仲介サービス・推論APIを混同しない |

## 破綻ケース（要反証）

1. NixOSと公式nixos/nix imageを同一視。
2. Windows own / rent / NixOS own-OCIを同じ稼働実体とする。
3. GHCRの配布成功＝実機適用成功と主張。
4. 一時bootstrap imageを全OCIの必須実装と主張。
5. Resource名をnode化してpackageと混同。
6. repo移管でHost IDを変えてしまう。
7. API endpointを呼出元と同じHostのpackageと誤認。
8. Gemini Developer API / Vertex AIの認証・料金を一本化。
9. GmailアカウントからGWS有料契約を推定。
10. JevとTypeLLMを同じProvider/secretとして扱う。
11. Cloudflare PoC/source/CIを本番稼働証拠へ昇格。
12. 宣言・実装・Binding・観測それぞれに第二正本を作る。
13. ソース不変をTargetのNOOP/成功とする。
14. Own Host停止が公開製品まで停止させる依存を見落とす。

## 次の改善・出口

配置の実状確認は、各利用先について「期待配置 / 実際の観測 / 固定成果版 / 観測日時 / 責任owner / 未証明」を分けて既存sourceへ参照する。配置差分を確認するまではResourceの共有daemon・共通broker・全Provider共通管理器を新設しない。

利益・売却価値への因果は、費用・復旧工数・改善速度・顧客向け停止時間の計測で判断する。**このIssueの完了は読み取り可能な配置図と根拠・境界の整合まで。製品実装や各実Hostの完了には昇格しない。**

根拠：[resources #1](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/1#issuecomment-6206774424) / [#25](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/25) / [#10](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/10) / [#52](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/52) / [PR #31](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/pull/31)、[ADRS #630](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/630)、[resources flake](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/blob/proposals/flake.nix)、[Jev transport](https://github.com/roccho-org/ops/blob/proposals/packages/jev/src/core.mjs)、[TypeLLM transport](https://github.com/roccho-org/ops/blob/proposals/packages/typellm/src/typellm.mjs)。
"}

body: Prove that editing SSG input or SSG compiler source updates generated UI data **without a page reload** and preserves the current pan/zoom viewport.
This is a `ui` development-proof slice, not a production runtime feature and not a generic organization-wide dev server.
Related: #114, #116. This issue does not block, close, or expand either issue.
-> publish revision only after complete output
-> living browser page fetches generated output
- viewport `x`, `y`, and `scale` remain equal within `1e-9` after both changes;
- viewer root DOM object remains identical;
- production-style output contains neither a revision marker nor the dev polling client.
| `packages/a2ui-adapter-artifacts/dev/ssg-output-refresh.js` | dev-only revision polling and one refresh callback |
| `packages/a2ui-adapter-artifacts/scripts/build-ssg-hot-refresh-proof.mjs` | deterministic fixture build; revision publication last |
Generated HTML, screenshot, revision file, and proof report are evidence only and must remain untracked under `packages/a2ui-adapter-artifacts/.generated/` or CI artifacts.
Do not change `packages/core-port/**` or `runtime/geo-map-port.js`; polling owns no UI meaning, camera meaning, LOD, SVG, or data-model semantics.
- Fully write generated output before revision changes.
- A failed build must not advance revision.
- Production-style build removes or omits revision and the dev polling client.
- Generated application data must not include a current timestamp merely to prove freshness.
- Initial revision establishes the baseline and does not trigger a duplicate refresh.
- At most one poll is in flight.
- Temporary fetch failure preserves the current screen and retries later.
- Polling knows only how to invoke `refresh(revision)`.
The viewer owns `getViewport`, `setViewport`, and `setData`; the poller owns none of them.

The test must copy the fixture into a unique temporary directory, start the dev server against the copy, mutate only the copied input/compiler, generate evidence, stop the server, remove the copy, and prove the tracked repository tree was not dirtied.
Do not edit tracked fixture files and restore them in `finally`.
Generate `proof/report.json` in the untracked artifact with:
- raw viewport values before and after each update;
Reuse an existing `ui` workflow. Do not create a new workflow.
The issue may be closed only after the PR-head CI itself:
2. executes the live SSG input and compiler edits;
4. uploads or retains the machine-readable report and screenshot as non-authoritative evidence;
6. passes the existing full `ui` check suite.
A historical local proof, source review, or count-only test is insufficient. Green CI must be read back from the exact final PR head before merge, and the merged commit must be read back afterward.
- hot replacement of viewer JavaScript, HTML, CSS, or camera implementation.

1. a second independent repo needs the same revision-publication and polling behavior;

3. both consumers prove the same contract in CI;

- [ ] existing complete `npm run check` remains green;

- [ ] issue closes only after those receipts exist.

{"body":"## Purpose

Add positive and destructive receipt fixtures so missing, stale, wrong-decision, wrong-assertion, and malformed receipts cannot pass as evidence.

## Post-merge state

After attached PRs merge:
- valid receipts pass fixture validation.
- missing/stale/wrong digest receipts fail in strict fixture mode.
- final join phases can rely on receipt fixtures as regression seeds.

## Completion audit impact

Contributes to:
- `receiptAudit`: destructive coverage for receipt validity.
- `toolSelftestAudit`: receipt verifier regression coverage.
- `completionCertificate.receiptFixtureDigest`.

## Merge blockers

Do not merge child PRs when:
- only happy path receipts are tested.
- stale decisionDigest or assertionDigest can still pass.
- missing receipt is downgraded to warning only.
- fixture output lacks expected exit code or finding class.

## Required evidence

- fixture paths for clean, missing, stale, wrong-decision, wrong-assertion, and malformed receipt cases.
- selftest/check command and expected exit codes.
- CI/check proving destructive cases fail as intended.
- PR comment linking this issue and listing covered negative cases.

## Boundary

This issue closes receipt fixture coverage only. It does not close final report compilation or branch protection."}

- PR comment linking this issue and listing covered negative cases.

Define `edits` as the local/dev control plane for Vim, hq, local queue, local worker, and repo adapters.

## Completion state

This is complete when future PRs can attach to `edits` without ambiguity about repo responsibility, local-only state, generated evidence, or dependency direction.

## Scope

- Document `edits` as the local/dev operation surface, not the canonical model authority.
- Define `.local/` for local queue, receipt, targetRef, projection, and preview state.
- Define boundaries between queue, receipt, projection, accepted ledger, and generated preview.
- Allow only one-way dependency from `edits` to `ui`, contracts, and source repos.
- Forbid `ui`, contracts, or source repos from depending on `edits`.
- Define how a temporary `contracts-poc` can later split into a contracts repo.

## Suggested PRs

1. Add README/docs boundary.
2. Add minimal directories and `.gitignore` for `.local/`.
3. Add PR/issue operation notes for attached work.

- [ ] README says `edits` is a local/dev control plane.

- [ ] Local queue is explicitly not state store or authority.

- [ ] Committed examples live under `examples/`, not `.local/`.
- [ ] Dependency direction is documented as `edits -> ui/contracts/source repos` only.
- [ ] Generated HTML, preview, and projection are evidence only.

## Non-scope

- hq implementation.
- UI renderer changes.
- cue validation implementation.
- accepted ledger operation."}

{"body":"Parent: #99

## Purpose

Build one mixed-target run ledger from canonical durable evidence so recent shell, Herdr, Codex, and Claude work can be inspected without target-specific hunting.

## Corrected evidence boundary

The ledger is rebuilt from valid durable `instruction.v1` and `result.v1` rows. `session.v1` and the ledger are projections only.

The former wording "event/session rows" was insufficient because `op` and `cwd` originate in the linked instruction, while a stored session row must never become authority.

## Purpose lineage

| generation | purpose | contribution | relation |
|---:|---|---|---|
| G0 scope | Produce one recent-run ledger. | Reduces canonical instruction/result evidence into mixed-target rows. | direct |
| G1 correctness | Never invent a healthy run from incomplete or invalid evidence. | Requires linked instruction identity and valid result lifecycle. | direct |
| G2 boundary | Keep read models non-authoritative. | No ledger or session row can overwrite source evidence. | direct |
| G3 product | Remove per-target session hunting. | One row shape covers sh, Herdr, Codex, and Claude. | direct |
| G4 system | Rebuild state after restart. | Ledger is a deterministic reduction of durable JSONL. | direct |
| G5 organization | Give humans and agents one reviewable operation view. | Handoff no longer depends on target UI knowledge. | direct |
| G6 business | Lower supervision cost for parallel agent execution. | Recent work is reviewable from one surface. | direct |
| G7 transfer | Let a new owner reconstruct run history. | Stable fields, fixtures, and tests expose the evidence chain. | indirect |
| G8 due diligence | Make execution claims reproducible. | Mixed-target and invalid-evidence cases are mechanically checked. | indirect |
| G9 asset value | Preserve a small extensible runtime without another database. | Existing append-only JSONL remains sufficient. | indirect |
| G10 meta | Increase company value and saleability. | Lower hidden-state and handoff risk improves transferability. | indirect |

## Scope

- Build a transient `worker.ledger.v1` read model from valid `instruction.v1` and `result.v1` rows.
- Reuse canonical `session.v1` lifecycle reduction.
- Include run id, instruction id, target, op, status, cwd, started time, last event time/kind, native session id, summary, final path, and structured error where available.
- Sort recent runs by `last_event_at`, newest first.
- Preserve one row per run/attempt; never collapse retry/replay history.
- Return non-green diagnostics for invalid or unlinked evidence.

## Non-scope

- Persisting the ledger as authority.
- Browser UI.
- Live target discovery.
- Adapter execution, approval, retry, claim, or endpoint placement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mixed sh/Herdr/Codex/Claude runs appear in one list.
- [ ] queued/running/completed/failed/blocked/timeout/cancelled are clear.
- [ ] Native session refs, final paths, and errors appear when present.
- [ ] `op` and `cwd` come from linked canonical instruction evidence, not defaults invented by observation.
- [ ] Newest run ordering is deterministic.
- [ ] Deleting stored projection data and rebuilding produces the same ledger.
- [ ] Invalid lifecycle or missing instruction evidence cannot produce a healthy ledger row.
- [ ] Ledger output performs zero durable writes and zero adapter calls.

## Destructive cases

The issue is not complete if any succeeds:

1. a stored session row overrides instruction/result evidence;
2. observation fills missing op/target/cwd with target-specific defaults;
3. invalid lifecycle appears green;
4. a target requires live CLI discovery for basic history;
5. retry/replay attempts are collapsed into one row;
6. ledger generation mutates durable state;
7. endpoint location changes ledger meaning.

## Dependencies

Foundation:

- #36-#48
- #75

Integrated validation:

- #100-#102
- #52-#66
- #81-#84
- #98 for managed lifecycle/crash states

## Evidence

- Mixed-target pure projection test.
- Newest-first ordering test.
- Missing/invalid instruction and lifecycle negatives.
- Binary-level JSON ledger artifact on Linux; Windows build and command test.
- Architecture readback proving the ledger is disposable.

## Merge condition

Merge only when one deterministic, non-authoritative ledger explains recent runs across targets from canonical durable evidence and cannot dispatch or mutate execution state."}
