body: Depends on: #116 candidate/index contract; #113 provenance and compatibility decisions
Implement the accepted-history half of #114 without creating another history authority.

Accepted history is a deterministic read-only projection from canonical accepted evidence. The editor buffer is disposable. Recall selection edits only the draft; explicit submit alone creates a new accepted intent.
| G0 | Restore prior human-facing commands after the draft is wiped. |
| G1 | Keep one durable log rather than a parallel history store. |
| G2 | Separate human recall from worker retry/replay. |
| G3 | Preserve provenance, policy, and current-world revalidation. |
| G4 | Exclude denied/sensitive values before indexing. |
| G5 | Degrade safely to world-only recall. |
| G6-G10 | Keep history auditable, rebuildable, transferable, and low-cost. |
disposable draft      = current editable projection only
No `history.jsonl`, persistent history database, Vim history, shell history, register history, terminal scrollback, buffer history, or ambient file becomes authority.
Worker retry/replay is a separate operation and identity model.
Every successful new `@command` acceptance writes normalized accepted-input evidence alongside the canonical instruction.
- typed safe fields in declared order;
If any supplied field was denied or sensitive, `recall_complete=false`.
Accepted input is never executed directly and is never sent to the worker as meaning. A recalled object is always reparsed, revalidated, and recompiled against the current selected world.
Legacy rows without accepted input are not recall candidates. Do not reverse canonical instructions and do not emit canonical-JSON fallback drafts.
| Policy | Persist safe value | Field-value recall | Free query | Complete preset |
| `deny` | no | no | no | no when supplied |
| `recall` | yes | yes | no | yes when all supplied fields are safe |
| `search` | yes | yes | yes | yes when all supplied fields are safe |
- sensitive plus recall/search rejects the world;
- key names are not used to guess sensitivity;
- permitted safe fields from an incomplete row may still contribute `field_value` recall.
An accepted row is eligible only when:
- world and command provenance are complete;
- current selected world contains the command;
- safe normalized fields validate against the current command;
- every indexed/displayed/materialized value is explicitly permitted.
Missing, ambiguous, incompatible, or unverifiable provenance excludes that row. Never infer provenance from command text.
No denied/sensitive value may enter recall terms, labels, detail, documentation, edits, recall diagnostics, or recall-component logs.
- canonical one-line empty draft -> recent complete presets only.
Recent recall is not enabled for arbitrary multi-line whitespace documents.
| retained source refs per grouped candidate | 5 |

Group identical complete objects by canonical materialization digest. Keep frequency, latest accepted ID/time, and at most five source refs. Never deduplicate or rewrite the canonical accepted ledger.
| digest mismatch | exclude row and emit non-green recall evidence |
| malformed/truncated log or authority-integrity failure | disable history projection |
| any history failure | world-only recall remains available |
Derived state must be rebuildable and non-authoritative. No second durable store.
Candidate ID remains query-independent. History source identity and grouping evidence are preserved without becoming authority.
5. assign fresh ID and acceptance time;
6. append exactly one canonical accepted row;
Repeated text is a new human intent, not retry/replay.
- no accepted input -> no history candidate;
- missing provenance -> row exclusion and world-only recall;
- denied/sensitive values appear on zero recall surfaces/logs;
- omitted sensitive/denied field names are not retained;
- safe fields from incomplete rows may produce permitted field values;
- structural corruption disables only history recall;
- recalled submit appends one row with fresh ID/time;
- buffer wipe and LSP restart do not lose recall evidence;
- accepted-input and policy contracts are versioned;
- acceptance writer emits safe normalized evidence;
- bounded projection and failure behavior are merged;
- no duplicate authority or wheel entered production code.

{"body":"Parent: #37

## Purpose

Freeze canonical candidate and LSP output snapshots so subtle rank, ordering, or `textEdit` regressions cannot pass unnoticed.

Why this contributes: it makes the completion contract reviewable as stable data, not only as pass/fail test output.

## Current gap

The CI proves expected labels and some ranges, but it does not store a canonical output snapshot for key prefixes.

## Required work

Add snapshots for at least:

- `houji`
- `houjin`
- `houjinb`
- `houjinScore`
- one hq-source prefix once hq fixture exists

Snapshots should include:

- candidate labels
- source
- rank/score
- `filterText`
- `sortText`
- `textEdit.range`
- `textEdit.newText`

## False-positive prevention

A candidate/rank/range change must produce a visible snapshot diff.

## False-negative prevention

Snapshots should omit volatile fields and use deterministic ordering.

## Done when

- CI compares current output to canonical snapshots.
- Snapshot updates require intentional PR diffs.
- Failure output shows expected vs actual for changed fields.

{"body":"## Summary
This issue records the current hq code state and the external proof already completed in the ChatGPT environment for the fzf-backed CLI/REPL UX direction. It is intended to become the issue anchor for merge-readiness work. It does not claim that the repo already contains the final CLI/REPL implementation.

## Current repo code state

As of the inspected `main` state and open PR #8:

- `README.md` defines hq as a small JSONL-aware autocomplete compiler.
- The first product boundary is: read the JSONL world, read the current cursor context, suggest only context-valid candidates, finalize only the human-chosen candidate, and append durable instructions as JSONL.
- `hq.terminal_surface.autocomplete_payload` builds suggestions from `JsonlWorld` and `CursorContext`.
- `hq.terminal_surface.choose_payload` finalizes a selected suggestion.
- `hq.core.JsonlWorld` and `CursorContext` exist.
- `hq.suggestion` supports key suggestions, enum value suggestions, duplicate-key diagnostics, unknown-key quick fixes, and `compileDraft` in suggestions.
- `hq.finalize` converts the selected suggestion into a `jsonl.instruction` row.
- The CLI entry on main is still `python -m hq demo-autocomplete` only.
- PR #8, `Finish hq terminal autocomplete proof`, is open and not merged.
- PR #8 close criteria include scripted REPL or acceptance E2E, input -> suggestion -> accept -> final JSONL row, permanent repo-backed evidence, practical business fixture, and governance-referenceable evidence.

## External proof completed outside repo

The following proof was completed in the ChatGPT runtime and should be treated as candidate evidence until moved into repo-backed scripts, snapshots, or tests:

- Existing-wheel proof showed hq self-owned JSON key/value completion can be reduced by using JSON Schema / vscode-json-languageservice style boundaries.
- fzf UX proof showed `queue.item JSONL -> fzf -> selected.jsonl -> dispatch.requests.jsonl -> ctx` as a viable UX path.
- Real terminal screenshots were generated with `fzf 0.73.1` from an uploaded Linux amd64 binary.
- Screenshots demonstrated:
  - small REPL picker with `fzf --height`, not full-screen takeover;
  - preview-pane picker for candidate reason/details;
  - full-screen fzf only for heavy selection.

External artifacts produced in the ChatGPT runtime:

- `hq-existing-wheels-proof.zip`
- `hq-fzf-ux-proof.zip`
- `hq-fzf-terminal-screens.zip`
- `00_contact_sheet.png`
- `01_repl_small_fzf.png`
- `02_repl_preview_fzf.png`
- `03_fullscreen_heavy_fzf.png`

These artifacts are not yet permanent repo-backed evidence and must not be used as final merge evidence unless reproduced by repo scripts or committed as stable snapshots.

## Product decision recorded here

The merge path should continue, but not as an immediate merge of the current state.

The correct direction is:

```text
hq core:
  context + JSONL IR + index/receipts
  -> ranked candidates / queue.item JSONL

projection:
  fzf for menu / preview / multi-select
  carapace for shell tab completion
  PSReadLine predictor for Windows inline suggestion later

ctx:
  resolver
  admission
  dispatch
  receipts
```

This means hq should not become an fzf-specific tool. fzf is one projection of the same candidate/queue protocol.

## Required merge-readiness work

- [ ] Add `hq suggest --protocol jsonl` or an equivalent stable candidate protocol.
- [ ] Add a real `hq repl` entrypoint, not only `demo-autocomplete`.
- [ ] Add an fzf projection that can run as a small REPL picker, preferably `--height` based.
- [ ] Add non-interactive E2E proof for `input buffer -> suggestion -> selection -> final JSONL instruction row`.
- [ ] Add a practical business-work-item fixture, not only toy schema rows.
- [ ] Add repo-backed proof snapshots or generated artifacts that survive GitHub Actions artifact expiry.
- [ ] Keep existing terminal autocomplete behavior from regressing.
- [ ] Keep fzf as optional projection; terminal autocomplete / tab completion path must remain possible without fzf.
- [ ] Add or preserve CI guards proving stdout / payload / screenshot drift where appropriate.
- [ ] Emit `dispatch.request.jsonl` or equivalent bridge output for future ctx integration, without implementing ctx inside hq.

## Non-goals

- Do not merge external ChatGPT sandbox artifacts as authority without repo reproduction.
- Do not turn hq into a general TUI framework.
- Do not implement ctx resolver/admission in hq.
- Do not replace future tab completion with fzf; fzf is a picker projection, not the whole completion UX.
- Do not claim governance gate completion from this issue alone.

## Close when

- hq repo contains stable proof for the fzf-backed REPL UX path.
- hq repo contains stable proof for input -> suggestion -> accept -> JSONL instruction.
- the proof is reproducible by CI or a documented repo command.
- the existing JSONL-aware autocomplete compiler boundary is preserved.
- the resulting PR can be reviewed as the merge-readiness closure for the current terminal/CLI/REPL proof lane."}

body: This issue records the current hq code state and the external proof already completed in the ChatGPT environment for the fzf-backed CLI/REPL UX direction. It is intended to become the issue anchor for merge-readiness work. It does not claim that the repo already contains the final CLI/REPL implementation.
As of the inspected `main` state and open PR #8:
- `README.md` defines hq as a small JSONL-aware autocomplete compiler.

- The first product boundary is: read the JSONL world, read the current cursor context, suggest only context-valid candidates, finalize only the human-chosen candidate, and append durable instructions as JSONL.
- `hq.suggestion` supports key suggestions, enum value suggestions, duplicate-key diagnostics, unknown-key quick fixes, and `compileDraft` in suggestions.
- `hq.finalize` converts the selected suggestion into a `jsonl.instruction` row.
- The CLI entry on main is still `python -m hq demo-autocomplete` only.
- PR #8, `Finish hq terminal autocomplete proof`, is open and not merged.

- PR #8 close criteria include scripted REPL or acceptance E2E, input -> suggestion -> accept -> final JSONL row, permanent repo-backed evidence, practical business fixture, and governance-referenceable evidence.
The following proof was completed in the ChatGPT runtime and should be treated as candidate evidence until moved into repo-backed scripts, snapshots, or tests:
- Existing-wheel proof showed hq self-owned JSON key/value completion can be reduced by using JSON Schema / vscode-json-languageservice style boundaries.
- fzf UX proof showed `queue.item JSONL -> fzf -> selected.jsonl -> dispatch.requests.jsonl -> ctx` as a viable UX path.
- Real terminal screenshots were generated with `fzf 0.73.1` from an uploaded Linux amd64 binary.
- small REPL picker with `fzf --height`, not full-screen takeover;
- full-screen fzf only for heavy selection.
External artifacts produced in the ChatGPT runtime:
These artifacts are not yet permanent repo-backed evidence and must not be used as final merge evidence unless reproduced by repo scripts or committed as stable snapshots.
The merge path should continue, but not as an immediate merge of the current state.
PSReadLine predictor for Windows inline suggestion later
This means hq should not become an fzf-specific tool. fzf is one projection of the same candidate/queue protocol.
- [ ] Add `hq suggest --protocol jsonl` or an equivalent stable candidate protocol.
- [ ] Add a real `hq repl` entrypoint, not only `demo-autocomplete`.
- [ ] Add an fzf projection that can run as a small REPL picker, preferably `--height` based.
- [ ] Add non-interactive E2E proof for `input buffer -> suggestion -> selection -> final JSONL instruction row`.
- [ ] Add a practical business-work-item fixture, not only toy schema rows.
- [ ] Add repo-backed proof snapshots or generated artifacts that survive GitHub Actions artifact expiry.
- [ ] Keep existing terminal autocomplete behavior from regressing.
- [ ] Keep fzf as optional projection; terminal autocomplete / tab completion path must remain possible without fzf.
- [ ] Add or preserve CI guards proving stdout / payload / screenshot drift where appropriate.
- [ ] Emit `dispatch.request.jsonl` or equivalent bridge output for future ctx integration, without implementing ctx inside hq.
- Do not merge external ChatGPT sandbox artifacts as authority without repo reproduction.
- Do not turn hq into a general TUI framework.
- Do not implement ctx resolver/admission in hq.
- Do not replace future tab completion with fzf; fzf is a picker projection, not the whole completion UX.
- Do not claim governance gate completion from this issue alone.
- hq repo contains stable proof for the fzf-backed REPL UX path.
- hq repo contains stable proof for input -> suggestion -> accept -> JSONL instruction.
- the proof is reproducible by CI or a documented repo command.
- the existing JSONL-aware autocomplete compiler boundary is preserved.
- the resulting PR can be reviewed as the merge-readiness closure for the current terminal/CLI/REPL proof lane.

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose
Define a session/run index row so recent Herdr, Codex, Claude, and shell executions can be listed from one durable source.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Makes recent agent/session list possible. |
| product | Standardizes run identity across targets. |
| system/org | Lets users recover answers and attach points after non-interactive execution. |
| business/meta | Creates transferable operational evidence. |

## Scope
- Define fields: `run_id`, `instruction_id`, `target`, `status`, `cwd`, `native_session_id`, `started_at`, `last_event_at`, `final_path`.
- Define relation to result rows.

## Non-scope
- Implementing list/show/tail commands.
- Adapter-specific discovery.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Session row contract exists.
- [ ] A run list can be projected from result/session rows.
- [ ] Native session ids are optional but typed when present.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Claude/Codex/Herdr require separate incompatible ledgers.
- [ ] `native_session_id` cannot be stored.

## Evidence
- Contract doc.
- Fixture session index.

## Merge condition
Merge only when target-crossing session projection is possible from JSONL alone."}

{"body":"## Purpose
Prove at least one coding agent can run through the worker without TUI driving and leave final answer/session evidence.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Proves non-interactive agent path. |
| product | Validates the worker adapter design beyond shell. |
| system/org | Solves “direct instruction hides answer” through logs/ledger. |
| business/meta | Demonstrates agent factory value. |

## Scope
- Use Codex or Claude adapter, whichever is available under CI/local proof constraints.
- Persist prompt, events, native session id when available, and final answer.

## Non-scope
- Proving every agent adapter.
- Long-running background orchestration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Non-interactive agent run produces completed/failed event rows.
- [ ] Final answer or failure reason is persisted outside terminal scrollback.
- [ ] Session/run is visible in ledger/list/show path.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Agent response is only visible in live terminal.
- [ ] Proof requires manually driving a TUI.

## Evidence
- Proof artifact or stubbed CI artifact with clear non-live limitation.
- Event log sample.

## Merge condition
Merge only when at least one agent lane proves non-TUI durable execution."}

{"body":"Parent: #37

## Purpose

Prove that `jp-jsonl`, `domain-jsonl`, and `hq-source-jsonl` all satisfy the same provider port contract.

Why this contributes: it prevents a source adapter from being only directory-shaped while failing to behave as a real completion provider.

## Current gap

The refactor created source adapter boundaries, but the existing checks do not strongly prove all source adapters satisfy one shared contract.

## Required work

- Add a provider contract test table covering all source adapters.
- Test the same request shape against each adapter.
- Assert normalized candidate fields: `word`, `reading`, `romaji` or filter key, `rank`, `source`, and optional detail.
- Assert deterministic ordering for equal inputs.
- Ensure the core only consumes the provider port, not concrete adapter types.

## False-positive prevention

A source adapter cannot pass by merely existing or returning arbitrary candidates. It must return candidates matching the shared normalized shape.

## False-negative prevention

Use small, stable fixtures per adapter so format-specific differences are normalized before assertions.

## Done when

- CI runs a provider contract test across `jp-jsonl`, `domain-jsonl`, and `hq-source-jsonl`.
- All adapters return the same normalized candidate shape.
- Failures identify which adapter and which field violated the contract.
"}

{"body":"## Purpose
Start Herdr agents from validated JSONL rows while preserving Herdr session/pane references in worker events.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Proves `JSONL -> worker -> Herdr agent start`. |
| product | Adds first non-shell orchestration adapter. |
| system/org | Lets commands run without manually driving the TUI. |
| business/meta | Supports multi-agent factory operation. |

## Scope
- Implement Herdr start operation only.
- Capture agent id, pane id, command argv, cwd, and status into event/session rows.

## Non-scope
- Reading output.
- Attach/observe.
- Agent-specific prompt semantics.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Valid Herdr start row creates a Herdr agent/pane or dry-run-equivalent proof in CI constraints.
- [ ] Session refs are written to event/session rows.
- [ ] `hq` has no Herdr dependency.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Herdr id is visible only in terminal scrollback.
- [ ] Worker core hard-codes Herdr CLI details outside adapter boundary.

## Evidence
- Adapter test or proof fixture.
- Event log sample.

## Merge condition
Merge only when Herdr start is adapter-owned and produces durable refs."}

| generation | purpose | contribution | relation |

- The durable target name remains exactly `sh` until a versioned instruction-contract migration says otherwise.
- `sh` v1 means direct `argv` execution only.
- The adapter must not invoke `/bin/sh`, `bash`, `cmd.exe`, PowerShell, `shell=true`, or any equivalent interpreter implicitly.
- Pipes, redirects, globbing, variable expansion, command substitution, quoting rules, and shell control operators have no special meaning.
- The worker supplies the policy-derived effective cwd, explicitly allowed environment, and context deadline/cancellation.
- Ambient environment or PATH must not become an undocumented authority. Cross-platform proof uses a built helper executable with an explicit path.
- Adapter types cannot set event id, sequence, time, canonical kind, status, run identity, or instruction identity.
- Non-zero process exit returns a stable transient failure and becomes canonical `failed` evidence through the worker mapper.
- Successful empty output must still produce a deterministic completion summary derived from the process exit, so success is readable without fabricating a target answer.

## Scope

- Add a concrete direct-executable adapter behind `internal/worker/adapter.Adapter`.
- Parse the already-validated `sh` payload as non-empty `argv` plus optional cwd.
- Execute one direct child process with exact argv boundaries.
- Use only worker-approved cwd, environment, and context.
- Capture stdout and stderr and emit them through the transient `Emit` port.
- Return a valid transient completion on exit code 0.
- Return a stable structured failure on non-zero exit or process-start failure.
- Register the adapter for exact target `sh`; add no aliases or default adapter.
- Exercise the adapter through the common worker path after #101 composes mandatory safety.
- Add Linux and Windows helper-binary proof.

- Shell-language evaluation or script parsing.
- PTY/TUI programs or interactive stdin.
- Full OS sandbox, container, or DLP.
- Distributed execution.
- Guaranteed descendant process-tree termination on every OS; #54 claims the direct child and states any wider guarantee explicitly.
- Arbitrary inherited environment or hidden PATH-based executable selection.
- A second durable adapter event schema.

- [ ] A real built helper executable is invoked through exact argv, without any shell process.
- [ ] Arguments containing `;`, `|`, `>`, `*`, `$`, `%`, quotes, and spaces arrive as literal argument bytes/strings and cannot start another command.
- [ ] The adapter is resolved only by exact registry key `sh`; unknown/case-shifted targets do not fall back.
- [ ] Validation and common policy complete before registry lookup or process start.
- [ ] One approved instruction starts the helper exactly once.
- [ ] stdout and stderr become canonical worker-owned `result.v1` rows.

- [ ] Windows proof passes with actual built `hq-worker.exe` and helper binaries.

1. a command string is evaluated by a shell;
2. an argument containing shell syntax starts a second process;
3. unknown target resolves to this adapter;
4. ambient PATH or environment silently changes the claimed executable/configuration;
5. adapter runs before common validation and approval;
6. adapter writes durable result rows itself;
7. adapter forges lifecycle identity or status;
8. non-zero exit is reported as completed;
9. output exists only in process/terminal scrollback;
10. duplicate normal consumption starts the executable twice;
11. proof uses only a fake adapter or handwritten result fixture;
12. Linux passes while the claimed Windows path is untested.

- Direct-executable package tests.
- Exact-argv/metacharacter fixture matrix.
- Built cross-platform helper executable.
- Fake/sentinel process-start count proof.
- Canonical `result.v1` readback for stdout, stderr, completion, and non-zero exit.
- Duplicate/idempotency proof.
- Linux and Windows worker artifacts and transcripts.

## Dependencies

Required foundations:

- #36-#40 and #78 — canonical contracts
- #41-#51 — worker core and adapter port
- #75-#77 — workspace and safety contracts
- #100-#102 — real handoff, mandatory safety composition, and single-writer ownership

Related lane issues:

- #53 — policy and negative fixture proof
- #54 — timeout and cancellation proof

Blocks:

- #55-#66 as the reference concrete adapter pattern
- #81-#84 integrated proof and architecture readback
- parent #99 closure

## Merge condition

Merge only when the direct-executable adapter runs through the final common worker path, all #53/#54 negative behavior required by this lane is green, no implicit shell or fallback path exists, and Linux/Windows evidence is produced from actual built binaries."}

- The adapter must not invoke `/bin/sh`, `bash`, `cmd.exe`, PowerShell, `shell=true`, or any equivalent interpreter implicitly.
- Pipes, redirects, globbing, variable expansion, command substitution, quoting rules, and shell control operators have no special meaning.
- The worker supplies the policy-derived effective cwd, explicitly allowed environment, and context deadline/cancellation.
- Ambient environment or PATH must not become an undocumented authority. Cross-platform proof uses a built helper executable with an explicit path.
- Adapter types cannot set event id, sequence, time, canonical kind, status, run identity, or instruction identity.
- Non-zero process exit returns a stable transient failure and becomes canonical `failed` evidence through the worker mapper.
- Successful empty output must still produce a deterministic completion summary derived from the process exit, so success is readable without fabricating a target answer.

## Scope

- Add a concrete direct-executable adapter behind `internal/worker/adapter.Adapter`.
- Parse the already-validated `sh` payload as non-empty `argv` plus optional cwd.
- Execute one direct child process with exact argv boundaries.
- Use only worker-approved cwd, environment, and context.
- Capture stdout and stderr and emit them through the transient `Emit` port.
- Return a valid transient completion on exit code 0.
- Return a stable structured failure on non-zero exit or process-start failure.
- Register the adapter for exact target `sh`; add no aliases or default adapter.
- Exercise the adapter through the common worker path after #101 composes mandatory safety.
- Add Linux and Windows helper-binary proof.

## Non-scope

- Shell-language evaluation or script parsing.
- PTY/TUI programs or interactive stdin.
- Full OS sandbox, container, or DLP.
- Distributed execution.
- Guaranteed descendant process-tree termination on every OS; #54 claims the direct child and states any wider guarantee explicitly.
- Arbitrary inherited environment or hidden PATH-based executable selection.
- A second durable adapter event schema.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A real built helper executable is invoked through exact argv, without any shell process.
- [ ] Arguments containing `;`, `|`, `>`, `*`, `$`, `%`, quotes, and spaces arrive as literal argument bytes/strings and cannot start another command.
- [ ] The adapter is resolved only by exact registry key `sh`; unknown/case-shifted targets do not fall back.
- [ ] Validation and common policy complete before registry lookup or process start.
- [ ] One approved instruction starts the helper exactly once.
- [ ] stdout and stderr become canonical worker-owned `result.v1` rows.
- [ ] Exit code 0 produces one terminal `completed` row with deterministic final readback.
- [ ] A non-zero exit produces terminal `failed` evidence with a stable error code and the observed numeric exit status; it never produces `completed`.
- [ ] Start failure produces terminal `failed` evidence and no false `started`/`completed` state beyond what the common lifecycle contract permits.
- [ ] Adapter output cannot forge durable identity, sequence, timestamp, kind, or status.
- [ ] Re-reading the same instruction does not execute the helper a second time under normal mode.
- [ ] Linux proof passes with actual built `hq-worker` and helper binaries.
- [ ] Windows proof passes with actual built `hq-worker.exe` and helper binaries.

## Destructive cases

The issue is not complete if any succeeds:

1. a command string is evaluated by a shell;
2. an argument containing shell syntax starts a second process;
3. unknown target resolves to this adapter;
4. ambient PATH or environment silently changes the claimed executable/configuration;
5. adapter runs before common validation and approval;
6. adapter writes durable result rows itself;
7. adapter forges lifecycle identity or status;
8. non-zero exit is reported as completed;
9. output exists only in process/terminal scrollback;
10. duplicate normal consumption starts the executable twice;
11. proof uses only a fake adapter or handwritten result fixture;
12. Linux passes while the claimed Windows path is untested.

- Direct-executable package tests.
- Exact-argv/metacharacter fixture matrix.
- Built cross-platform helper executable.
- Fake/sentinel process-start count proof.
- Canonical `result.v1` readback for stdout, stderr, completion, and non-zero exit.
- Duplicate/idempotency proof.

Merge only when the direct-executable adapter runs through the final common worker path, all #53/#54 negative behavior required by this lane is green, no implicit shell or fallback path exists, and Linux/Windows evidence is produced from actual built binaries."}

{"body":"

1. 目的

世代 | 期待 -- | -- G0 | Windowsでフォント・端末・OS設定を再現可能にする G1 | Windows / Linuxで同じ見た目・同じ選択を使う G2 | UI・日本語・terminal・Nerd・Emojiまで選定を終わらせる G3 | 手作業・個別PowerShell・巨大artifactを減らす G4 | GitHub Release + version/hash固定で宣言的に取得する G5 | Windows固有処理を交換可能なadapterへ閉じ込める G6 | 将来WindowsもLinuxもNixへ寄せられる形を保つ Meta | OS設定について二度と高コストな判断をせず、開発へ集中する

5. より美しい最終形

今は、

desired choice
├─ IBM Plex Sans JP
├─ PlemolJP Console NF
└─ Color Emoji

Windows
└─ DSC → WinGet → GitHub Release

Linux
└─ Nix → upstream/GitHub Release

将来Windows Nixが十分なら、

desired choice
        │
       Nix
    ┌───┴───┐
 Windows   Linux

へ縮退できます。

したがって、今DSCを採ることと、最終的にNixへ統一することは矛盾しません。

むしろ「DSCにWindows固有処理だけ閉じ込め、artifactと選択をOSから独立させる」のが、将来Nix一本へ最も安く移れる設計です。

整理すると、期待と結論はこれです。

区分 | 内容 -- | -- 最上位期待 | Windows / Linux を同じ宣言モデルで再現可能にしたい SSOT | 可能な限り Nix に寄せる Linux | Nixが build / package / system / activation までほぼ担当 Windows | Nixが 定義・依存・pin・artifact生成を担当 Windows固有変更 | DSC 3 が activation backend を担当 package | 将来はNix優先。足りない部分だけWinGet等をDSC resourceとして利用 imperative script | .ps1 を主役にしない。必要でも薄いbootstrap/adapterだけ artifact取得 | GitHub Release等もNix inputとして固定して取得 fonts / terminal等 | Windows固有設定も同じNix定義からDSC設定を生成 host | Linux/Windowsとも、手作業状態をできるだけ減らす 将来 | native nix.exe が成熟するほどWindows側もLinux側の構造へ近づける

つまり今の結論は、

Nixをcross-OSの上位IaC / compilerにする。

LinuxではNix自身が最後まで適用する。
Windowsでは当面、最後のOS変更だけDSCへ渡す。

です。

そして重要なのは、これは

Linux = Nix
Windows = DSC

という二重管理ではなく、

          Nix
           │
     OS-specific backend
       /           \
   Linux           DSC

という一つの設計です。

非目標

  • Windows専用の巨大IaC frameworkを新しく作らない
  • Ansible/Chefを中間層として常設しない
  • PowerShell script群をSSOTにしない
  • Nix derivation内からregistry/serviceを直接変更しない
  • LinuxとWindowsで別々の設定体系を育てない

最終的に狙っているのは、

「OS差分はactivation backendだけ」

まで圧縮することです。

これは将来 nix.exe が成熟したときにも、そのままWindows側のDSC依存をさらに薄くできる構造です。

"}

  • Ansible/Chefを中間層として常設しない
  • PowerShell script群をSSOTにしない
  • Nix derivation内からregistry/serviceを直接変更しない
  • LinuxとWindowsで別々の設定体系を育てない

最終的に狙っているのは、

「OS差分はactivation backendだけ」

まで圧縮することです。

これは将来 nix.exe が成熟したときにも、そのままWindows側のDSC依存をさらに薄くできる構造です。

{"body":"## Purpose
Create the worker as a separate runtime boundary so `hq` stays a meaning-free compiler and execution starts only after JSONL validation.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Establishes `instruction.jsonl -> worker` outside `hq`. |
| product | Preserves small core and makes execution optional. |
| system | Creates a place for adapter dispatch, event logging, and policy. |
| org/business/meta | Makes agent factory operation inspectable and transferable. |

## Scope
- Add worker package/command skeleton outside compiler/core packages.
- Read configuration paths but do not execute adapters yet.

## Non-scope
- Herdr/Codex/Claude/sh adapter implementation.
- UI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Worker command builds separately from `cmd/hq`.
- [ ] Worker does not require importing `cmd/hq` internals.
- [ ] Docs show `hq` produces queue rows and worker consumes them.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Worker logic is embedded in `cmd/hq`.
- [ ] `hq` must link execution adapters to build.

## Evidence
- Build/test output.
- Package boundary note.

## Merge condition
Merge only when worker ownership is visibly separate from `hq` compiler ownership."}

{"body":"## Status

```text
authority=false
effectful=false
blockedUntilAcceptedADRS=true
migrationComplete=false
```

## Purpose

Implement the accepted ADRS contract-modeling decision in `governance`, migrate
the historical behavior of `jsonl-datamodeling-duckdb-ci`, and close the migration
with deterministic proof rather than a documentation-only move.

## Baseline

Already demonstrated:

- provider-detached ADRS Issue/file JSONL adapters;
- pagination and transport receipt separation;
- canonical ledger sealing;
- closed schema validation;
- explicit-supersession reduction;
- provider-invariant semantic output;
- exact candidate SHA evidence;
- deterministic Nix materialization.

Not yet demonstrated:

- recursive contract-modeling envelope across package and data-model profiles;
- derived model-admission decisions;
- the legacy DuckDB gate set in the current authority boundary;
- promotion bound to accepted ADRS digest and explicit purpose path;
- production admission and effect readback;
- complete removal of active specs consumers.

## Dependency

This Issue may be implemented in shadow mode before acceptance, but it may not
claim production authority or cutover until the ADRS decision digest is accepted.

Required references:

```text
ADRS_ISSUE=roccho-dev/adrs#234
ACCEPTED_DECISION_ID=
ACCEPTED_DECISION_DIGEST=
ACCEPTED_RELEASE=
```

## Owned here

- provider-neutral claim-ledger reader;
- canonicalization and sealing;
- closed envelope schema and V1 profile schemas;
- explicit supersession and recursive containment reduction;
- data-model admission compiler;
- package-contract admission compiler;
- DuckDB projections and gates;
- purpose and responsibility closure;
- exact-SHA evidence join;
- deterministic generated artifacts;
- findings and receipts;
- shadow and final-gate adapters.

## Not owned here

- accepted meaning or waivers;
- package-owner intent;
- production database/registry/deployment effects;
- branch/ref/ruleset mutation;
- business outcome claims.

## Repository layout

```text
tools/contract-modeling/
  README.md
  schema/
    envelope.v1.schema.json
    package-contract.v1.schema.json
    data-model.v1.schema.json
    receipt.v1.schema.json
  engine/
    canonicalize
    reduce
    derive
    promote
    project
  duckdb/
    load.sql
    derive.sql
    gates.sql
    abi.sql
  adapters/
    issue
    file
    package-packet
  fixtures/
    legacy
    positive
    destructive
    real-packages
    model-only-package
  nix/
    materialize.nix
  tests/
```

Shared adapter/canonicalization code should be extracted from the prior bounded
code-governance implementation only where two real consumers now need it. Do not
create an abstract plugin framework.

## Deliverables

### D1. Common envelope and recursive graph

Implement stable opaque `subject_key`, typed edges, explicit supersession, and
derived display paths.

Required invariants:

- no fixed semantic depth;
- no containment cycle;
- exactly one active row per logical subject;
- deterministic result independent of input order/chunking;
- unknown kinds/properties fail closed.

### D2. Package-contract profile

Support and enforce:

- input;
- output;
- error/residual;
- effect;
- dependency/port;
- lifecycle;
- evidence/receipt;
- purpose linkage.

Join accepted organization policy with package assertions. A local assertion may
strengthen but may not weaken the accepted rule.

### D3. Data-model profile

Support:

- schema/field contracts;
- semantic terms;
- equivalence/distinctness;
- compatibility/migration;
- projection/query contracts;
- witnesses/counterexamples;
- destructive fixtures.

### D4. Derived admission

Inputs contain claims and evidence only.

Derive:

- duplicate/equivalent candidates;
- ambiguity;
- breaking classification;
- migration coverage/losslessness status;
- query impact;
- decision;
- promotion eligibility;
- responsibility closure level.

Emit one of the eight defined decisions. Quarantine conflicts and preserve the
previous current epoch.

### D5. DuckDB gate port

Port the stable legacy invariants, but separate proof-corpus constants from
production policy.

The production gate catalog must include:

- no raw direct SQL;
- no equivalent duplicate new model;
- no ambiguous approved model;
- no breaking promotion without destructive and migration proof;
- projection/query contract completeness;
- promotion-only current;
- old/new shared ABI where compatibility is claimed;
- replay equality;
- bounded active ABI and model growth from accepted policy;
- complete reasons, owners, purpose paths, and digests.

Legacy PoC counts such as exact source-file count or exact request count remain
fixture assertions, not organization policy.

### D6. Legacy migration ledger

Produce one row for every active legacy responsibility:

```text
legacy_id
legacy_source_digest
new_subject_key
new_semantic_kind
disposition = mapped | retired | quarantined
reason
owner
accepted_decision_digest
```

Block while any active legacy row is unexplained.

### D7. Responsibility closure projection

Emit `responsibility-closure.v1` with:

```text
responsibility_id
responsibility_kind
accepted_decision_id
accepted_decision_digest
purpose_root_id
purpose_path_digest
claim_digest
candidate_sha
receipt_set_digest
promotion_id
current_epoch
effect_receipt_digest
closure_level
residuals
```

Closure levels:

```text
unlinked
decision-linked
purpose-linked
evidence-closed
effect-closed
outcome-observed
```

Only the first five are in this implementation scope. `outcome-observed` remains
a separate business-evidence plane.

### D8. Bounded model-only package proof

Create one deterministic fixture with no handwritten application logic:

```text
JSONL input
→ validate
→ deterministic transform
→ output
→ receipt
```

The model compiles to an execution contract. A shell/Nix wrapper may be generated,
but shell text is not authority.

### D9. Real package proof

Connect two unrelated real packages from the accepted required-package universe.

Prove:

- package input/output contract completeness;
- internal subjects at multiple depths;
- package assertions cannot weaken organization constraints;
- exact candidate SHA receipts;
- findings identify expected, actual, delta, owner, and next action.

### D10. Cutover and anti-regression

After accepted cutover:

- final admission check is required for selected scope;
- active consumers of `specs/packages/jsonl-datamodeling-duckdb-ci` are zero;
- CI rejects legacy authority imports and editable generated current state;
- effectful consumers use accepted artifacts and return readback receipts.

## Work sequence

1. Freeze and digest legacy source/evidence.
2. Add envelope and two closed profiles.
3. Reuse/extract only proven adapter/reducer primitives.
4. Add migration ledger.
5. Implement recursive reduction.
6. Implement derived admission and DuckDB gates.
7. Emit current/ABI/query/responsibility projections.
8. Add destructive tests.
9. Run frozen legacy differential proof.
10. Connect two real packages.
11. Add bounded model-only package proof.
12. Run shadow mode and read back artifacts.
13. Accept cutover.
14. Remove active specs consumers and enable negative guard.
15. Publish closure receipt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Accepted ADRS decision ID/digest is pinned.
- [ ] Legacy source snapshot and digest are pinned.
- [ ] Every active legacy row has a disposition; unexplained count is zero.
- [ ] Envelope and both profile schemas are closed.
- [ ] No trusted self-reported decision fields exist.
- [ ] Recursive reduction has no fixed schema depth and rejects cycles/orphans.
- [ ] Eight-way admission is deterministic and explained.
- [ ] Conflicts quarantine without changing previous current state.
- [ ] Promotion rows bind decision, policy, input, purpose, proof, and candidate digests.
- [ ] Current state has no source other than promotion.
- [ ] Full replay equals incremental byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Old/new compatibility fixture uses the same versioned ABI.
- [ ] Approved query contracts do not read raw JSONL.
- [ ] Production policy is separated from PoC fixture counts.
- [ ] Two unrelated real packages pass exact-SHA admission.
- [ ] Model-only package fixture passes.
- [ ] At least 26 destructive cases fail for their expected reason.
- [ ] Governance performs no production mutation.
- [ ] Effect readback receipts are joined where effects exist.
- [ ] Active legacy consumer count is zero after cutover.
- [ ] Reintroduction guard is green.
- [ ] Closure receipt is complete and `migration_complete=true`.

## Closure rule

Do not close this Issue for:

- a design document alone;
- a shadow-only green check;
- a fixture-only green check;
- a generated artifact without accepted authority;
- a PR merged while active specs consumers remain;
- a green admission result without required effect readback.

Close only when the full migration-complete state in `roccho-dev/adrs#234` is
read back and its receipt is attached."}

{"body":"## Status

```text
authority=false
effectful=false
blockedUntilAcceptedADRS=true
migrationComplete=false
```

## Purpose

Implement the accepted ADRS contract-modeling decision in `governance`, migrate
the historical behavior of `jsonl-datamodeling-duckdb-ci`, and close the migration
with deterministic proof rather than a documentation-only move.

## Baseline

Already demonstrated:

- provider-detached ADRS Issue/file JSONL adapters;
- pagination and transport receipt separation;
- canonical ledger sealing;
- closed schema validation;
- explicit-supersession reduction;
- provider-invariant semantic output;
- exact candidate SHA evidence;
- deterministic Nix materialization.

Not yet demonstrated:

- recursive contract-modeling envelope across package and data-model profiles;
- derived model-admission decisions;
- the legacy DuckDB gate set in the current authority boundary;
- promotion bound to accepted ADRS digest and explicit purpose path;
- production admission and effect readback;
- complete removal of active specs consumers.

## Dependency

This Issue may be implemented in shadow mode before acceptance, but it may not
claim production authority or cutover until the ADRS decision digest is accepted.

Required references:

```text
ADRS_ISSUE=roccho-dev/adrs#234
ACCEPTED_DECISION_ID=
ACCEPTED_DECISION_DIGEST=
ACCEPTED_RELEASE=
```

## Owned here

- provider-neutral claim-ledger reader;
- canonicalization and sealing;
- closed envelope schema and V1 profile schemas;
- explicit supersession and recursive containment reduction;
- data-model admission compiler;
- package-contract admission compiler;
- DuckDB projections and gates;
- purpose and responsibility closure;
- exact-SHA evidence join;
- deterministic generated artifacts;
- findings and receipts;
- shadow and final-gate adapters.

## Not owned here

- accepted meaning or waivers;
- package-owner intent;
- production database/registry/deployment effects;
- branch/ref/ruleset mutation;
- business outcome claims.

## Repository layout

```text
tools/contract-modeling/
  README.md
  schema/
    envelope.v1.schema.json
    package-contract.v1.schema.json
    data-model.v1.schema.json
    receipt.v1.schema.json
  engine/
    canonicalize
    reduce
    derive
    promote
    project
  duckdb/
    load.sql
    derive.sql
    gates.sql
    abi.sql
  adapters/
    issue
    file
    package-packet
  fixtures/
    legacy
    positive
    destructive
    real-packages
    model-only-package
  nix/
    materialize.nix
  tests/
```

Shared adapter/canonicalization code should be extracted from the prior bounded
code-governance implementation only where two real consumers now need it. Do not
create an abstract plugin framework.

## Deliverables

### D1. Common envelope and recursive graph

Implement stable opaque `subject_key`, typed edges, explicit supersession, and
derived display paths.

Required invariants:

- no fixed semantic depth;
- no containment cycle;
- exactly one active row per logical subject;
- deterministic result independent of input order/chunking;
- unknown kinds/properties fail closed.

### D2. Package-contract profile

Support and enforce:

- input;
- output;
- error/residual;
- effect;
- dependency/port;
- lifecycle;
- evidence/receipt;
- purpose linkage.

Join accepted organization policy with package assertions. A local assertion may
strengthen but may not weaken the accepted rule.

### D3. Data-model profile

Support:

- schema/field contracts;
- semantic terms;
- equivalence/distinctness;
- compatibility/migration;
- projection/query contracts;
- witnesses/counterexamples;
- destructive fixtures.

### D4. Derived admission

Inputs contain claims and evidence only.

Derive:

- duplicate/equivalent candidates;
- ambiguity;
- breaking classification;
- migration coverage/losslessness status;
- query impact;
- decision;
- promotion eligibility;
- responsibility closure level.

Emit one of the eight defined decisions. Quarantine conflicts and preserve the
previous current epoch.

### D5. DuckDB gate port

Port the stable legacy invariants, but separate proof-corpus constants from
production policy.

The production gate catalog must include:

- no raw direct SQL;
- no equivalent duplicate new model;
- no ambiguous approved model;
- no breaking promotion without destructive and migration proof;
- projection/query contract completeness;
- promotion-only current;
- old/new shared ABI where compatibility is claimed;
- replay equality;
- bounded active ABI and model growth from accepted policy;
- complete reasons, owners, purpose paths, and digests.

Legacy PoC counts such as exact source-file count or exact request count remain
fixture assertions, not organization policy.

### D6. Legacy migration ledger

Produce one row for every active legacy responsibility:

```text
legacy_id
legacy_source_digest
new_subject_key
new_semantic_kind
disposition = mapped | retired | quarantined
reason
owner
accepted_decision_digest
```

Block while any active legacy row is unexplained.

### D7. Responsibility closure projection

Emit `responsibility-closure.v1` with:

```text
responsibility_id
responsibility_kind
accepted_decision_id
accepted_decision_digest
purpose_root_id
purpose_path_digest
claim_digest
candidate_sha
receipt_set_digest
promotion_id
current_epoch
effect_receipt_digest
closure_level
residuals
```

Closure levels:

```text
unlinked
decision-linked
purpose-linked
evidence-closed
effect-closed
outcome-observed
```

Only the first five are in this implementation scope. `outcome-observed` remains
a separate business-evidence plane.

### D8. Bounded model-only package proof

Create one deterministic fixture with no handwritten application logic:

```text
JSONL input
→ validate
→ deterministic transform
→ output
→ receipt
```

The model compiles to an execution contract. A shell/Nix wrapper may be generated,
but shell text is not authority.

### D9. Real package proof

Connect two unrelated real packages from the accepted required-package universe.

Prove:

- package input/output contract completeness;
- internal subjects at multiple depths;
- package assertions cannot weaken organization constraints;
- exact candidate SHA receipts;
- findings identify expected, actual, delta, owner, and next action.

### D10. Cutover and anti-regression

After accepted cutover:

- final admission check is required for selected scope;
- active consumers of `specs/packages/jsonl-datamodeling-duckdb-ci` are zero;
- CI rejects legacy authority imports and editable generated current state;
- effectful consumers use accepted artifacts and return readback receipts.

## Work sequence

1. Freeze and digest legacy source/evidence.
2. Add envelope and two closed profiles.
3. Reuse/extract only proven adapter/reducer primitives.
4. Add migration ledger.
5. Implement recursive reduction.
6. Implement derived admission and DuckDB gates.
7. Emit current/ABI/query/responsibility projections.
8. Add destructive tests.
9. Run frozen legacy differential proof.
10. Connect two real packages.
11. Add bounded model-only package proof.
12. Run shadow mode and read back artifacts.
13. Accept cutover.
14. Remove active specs consumers and enable negative guard.
15. Publish closure receipt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Accepted ADRS decision ID/digest is pinned.
- [ ] Legacy source snapshot and digest are pinned.
- [ ] Every active legacy row has a disposition; unexplained count is zero.
- [ ] Envelope and both profile schemas are closed.
- [ ] No trusted self-reported decision fields exist.
- [ ] Recursive reduction has no fixed schema depth and rejects cycles/orphans.
- [ ] Eight-way admission is deterministic and explained.
- [ ] Conflicts quarantine without changing previous current state.
- [ ] Promotion rows bind decision, policy, input, purpose, proof, and candidate digests.
- [ ] Current state has no source other than promotion.
- [ ] Full replay equals incremental byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Old/new compatibility fixture uses the same versioned ABI.
- [ ] Approved query contracts do not read raw JSONL.
- [ ] Production policy is separated from PoC fixture counts.
- [ ] Two unrelated real packages pass exact-SHA admission.
- [ ] Model-only package fixture passes.
- [ ] At least 26 destructive cases fail for their expected reason.
- [ ] Governance performs no production mutation.
- [ ] Effect readback receipts are joined where effects exist.
- [ ] Active legacy consumer count is zero after cutover.
- [ ] Reintroduction guard is green.
- [ ] Closure receipt is complete and `migration_complete=true`.

## Closure rule

Do not close this Issue for:

- a design document alone;
- a shadow-only green check;
- a fixture-only green check;
- a generated artifact without accepted authority;
- a PR merged while active specs consumers remain;
- a green admission result without required effect readback.

Close only when the full migration-complete state in `roccho-dev/adrs#234` is
read back and its receipt is attached."}

4. attaches the selected client and causes required didOpen/sync;

The third-party client may perform native mechanical filtering/sorting.
For canonical hq fixtures, the visible output must preserve:
The client/adapter must not add domain/history/redaction semantics or an independent hq rank model.
Raw RPC response inspection is not sufficient.
2. make the expected candidate visibly selectable;
4. display complete multi-line documentation before acceptance;
6. apply the server-supplied multi-line text edit;
9. verify exact pre-accept query is restored.

- isolate all required non-public APIs in one compatibility module;
- no client-internal type or method may leak into hq protocol meaning;
- a client commit update triggers the full conformance suite;
- incompatibility fails closed rather than silently bypassing sync/position/UI behavior.
Using real Linux Vim and native Windows Vim:
3. show recent safe presets after hq#117 exists;
5. show expected template and safe preset;
9. accept and materialize exact multi-line object;
14. HqSubmit once and prove one fresh row;

- exact hq commit and binary digest;
- exact Vim versions and minimum patch conclusion;
- screenshots or terminal capture showing popup and documentation;
- accepted-row counts before selection and after submit;
- plugin identity added as permanent hq meaning;
- raw Vim byte columns sent as LSP positions;
- raw RPC label check claimed as native UI proof;
- candidate removed or relative order changed in canonical fixtures;
- multi-line edit requires edits-owned text-edit reimplementation;
- one acceptance requires multiple undo operations;
- Vimscript parses accepted history or command semantics;
- Windows-only green with Linux failure, or vice versa.

- zero-write selection and one-write HqSubmit pass;
- no prohibited semantics entered edits production code.

{"body":"Parent: #37

## Purpose

Ensure the auto-complete no-degrade workflow is proven on the target branch after merge, not only on the PR head.

Why this contributes: it removes the false-green path where PR head CI passes but the merged `proposals` branch state is never validated.

## Current gap

PR #38 head CI succeeded, but the merge commit had no associated workflow run.

## Required work

- Make the auto-complete workflow run on `push` to `proposals` for changes under `packages/auto-complete/**` and `.github/workflows/auto-complete-golden.yml`.
- After the fixing PR merges, verify the post-merge `proposals` branch run exists.
- Record the post-merge run id and conclusion on #37.

## False-positive prevention

A PR cannot be treated as fully no-degrade unless the target branch state also has a successful run.

## False-negative prevention

Keep the path filters narrow to auto-complete paths so unrelated repository changes do not trigger unnecessary failures.

## Done when

- A post-merge workflow run is visible for the merge commit or target branch head.
- The run conclusion is `success`.
- #37 has a comment with the post-merge run id.
"}

body: This Issue owns deterministic governance projection and join inputs only. It does not accept the decision, implement `web-publication`, implement the renderer, deploy a site, authorize legacy deletion, or make local package green final authority.

Once the `web-publication` architecture decision is accepted through ADRS, compile its exact decision digest into package-facing obligations for `roccho-dev/web` and `roccho-dev/ui`, require exact candidate-SHA receipts, diagnose drift, and expose the result to the final-scope join.
| Scope | Turn accepted prose/records into machine-consumable web/ui obligations. |
| Product | Prevent `web-publication` from claiming completion without the renderer, quality, scale, boundary, and retirement evidence. |
| Architecture | Enforce ownership separation across ADRS, web, ui, governance, and future delivery. |
| Review | Make missing/stale/contradictory claims and receipts actionable. |
| Transfer | Let a future reviewer verify the product without interpreting mutable Issue prose. |
| Meta | Lower diligence and migration risk for the reusable Web product asset. |
Do nothing production-like until the validated ADRS path provides:
The mutable body of `adrs#244` is not sufficient input.
Require a `webPublication.packageClaim.v1` assertion pinned to the accepted decision digest and receipts for:
- generated 5,000-page scale proof with readiness not claimed;
- exact legacy inventory/retirement status and rollback digest;
Require a renderer claim pinned to the same accepted decision digest and receipts for:
- exact renderer revision/digest and external consumer conformance.
Produce deterministic repo/package-facing rules and findings for at least:

Each blocking finding should identify package ID, contract ID, ADRS ref/digest, expected, actual, delta, diagnostic class, likely owner, next action, assertion digest, and receipt digest where available.
Governance selftests must fail closed when:
1. accepted ADRS input is absent, proposed, stale, or digest-mismatched;
2. web claim omits the UI renderer exact ref/digest;
4. web claim owns a second semantic renderer;
7. generated output is represented as authority;
8. Astro is required by the canonical selected proof;
10. provider credential/deploy state enters the publication package;
11. retirement receipt lacks exact inventory, consumers, rollback, or authorization;
12. historical parity is claimed under the source-unavailable route;
13. receipts are green for a different candidate SHA;
14. standalone package CI is represented as organization-active without the final join;
15. one required repo/package is omitted from the universe.
- [ ] Projection consumes only the accepted digest-pinned ADRS input.
- [ ] Web and UI obligations are separate and traceable to one decision.
- [ ] Claims and receipts bind to exact package IDs and candidate SHAs.
- [ ] All listed overclaim and ownership drifts produce blocking findings.
- [ ] The projected contract is deterministic and replays to the same digest.
- [ ] Package repos can consume obligations without reading ADRS prose.
- [ ] Generated governance outputs remain non-authority evidence.
- [ ] No target repository, branch protection, provider, deployment, or deletion effect occurs here.
- [ ] Final-scope join input distinguishes package proof from organization-active admission.
- [ ] Residual historical parity/deletion blockers remain explicit instead of being hidden by other green receipts.
- writing implementation into web or ui;
- claiming parent `web#1` complete by governance output alone.

Merge the projection/selftest implementation only after an accepted ADRS decision digest exists, or keep all work explicitly fixture/shadow-only with `blockedUntilAcceptedADRS=true`. No projected rule may silently treat the proposed Issue body as accepted authority.

Close when the accepted decision projects deterministically, web/ui package obligations and negative fixtures pass, exact claims/receipts are consumable by the final-scope join, and current residuals are reported with owner/next action. Organization-active completion remains owned by the accepted final join/cutover.

body: This Issue owns deterministic governance projection and join inputs only. It does not accept the decision, implement `web-publication`, implement the renderer, deploy a site, authorize legacy deletion, or make local package green final authority.

Once the `web-publication` architecture decision is accepted through ADRS, compile its exact decision digest into package-facing obligations for `roccho-dev/web` and `roccho-dev/ui`, require exact candidate-SHA receipts, diagnose drift, and expose the result to the final-scope join.
| Scope | Turn accepted prose/records into machine-consumable web/ui obligations. |
| Product | Prevent `web-publication` from claiming completion without the renderer, quality, scale, boundary, and retirement evidence. |
| Architecture | Enforce ownership separation across ADRS, web, ui, governance, and future delivery. |
| Review | Make missing/stale/contradictory claims and receipts actionable. |
| Transfer | Let a future reviewer verify the product without interpreting mutable Issue prose. |
| Meta | Lower diligence and migration risk for the reusable Web product asset. |
Do nothing production-like until the validated ADRS path provides:
The mutable body of `adrs#244` is not sufficient input.
Require a `webPublication.packageClaim.v1` assertion pinned to the accepted decision digest and receipts for:
- generated 5,000-page scale proof with readiness not claimed;
- exact legacy inventory/retirement status and rollback digest;
Require a renderer claim pinned to the same accepted decision digest and receipts for:
- exact renderer revision/digest and external consumer conformance.
Produce deterministic repo/package-facing rules and findings for at least:

Each blocking finding should identify package ID, contract ID, ADRS ref/digest, expected, actual, delta, diagnostic class, likely owner, next action, assertion digest, and receipt digest where available.
Governance selftests must fail closed when:
1. accepted ADRS input is absent, proposed, stale, or digest-mismatched;
2. web claim omits the UI renderer exact ref/digest;
4. web claim owns a second semantic renderer;
7. generated output is represented as authority;
8. Astro is required by the canonical selected proof;
10. provider credential/deploy state enters the publication package;
11. retirement receipt lacks exact inventory, consumers, rollback, or authorization;
12. historical parity is claimed under the source-unavailable route;
13. receipts are green for a different candidate SHA;
14. standalone package CI is represented as organization-active without the final join;
15. one required repo/package is omitted from the universe.
- [ ] Projection consumes only the accepted digest-pinned ADRS input.
- [ ] Web and UI obligations are separate and traceable to one decision.
- [ ] Claims and receipts bind to exact package IDs and candidate SHAs.
- [ ] All listed overclaim and ownership drifts produce blocking findings.
- [ ] The projected contract is deterministic and replays to the same digest.
- [ ] Package repos can consume obligations without reading ADRS prose.
- [ ] Generated governance outputs remain non-authority evidence.
- [ ] No target repository, branch protection, provider, deployment, or deletion effect occurs here.
- [ ] Final-scope join input distinguishes package proof from organization-active admission.
- [ ] Residual historical parity/deletion blockers remain explicit instead of being hidden by other green receipts.
- writing implementation into web or ui;
- claiming parent `web#1` complete by governance output alone.

Merge the projection/selftest implementation only after an accepted ADRS decision digest exists, or keep all work explicitly fixture/shadow-only with `blockedUntilAcceptedADRS=true`. No projected rule may silently treat the proposed Issue body as accepted authority.

Close when the accepted decision projects deterministically, web/ui package obligations and negative fixtures pass, exact claims/receipts are consumable by the final-scope join, and current residuals are reported with owner/next action. Organization-active completion remains owned by the accepted final join/cutover.

{"body":"## Purpose

After PR #11 and #12, `main` has valuable proof, but the repo identity is now mixed:

- Python still looks like a product baseline.
- Go now looks like the product runtime.
- The README and module names still carry proof / POC wording.
- Linux and Windows Tab proof are good, but protocol ownership is not yet explicit.

This issue defines the desired final state in detail before opening cleanup PRs.

## Final one-line shape

`hq` is a protocol-first, Go-runtime JSONL autocomplete compiler.

It reads JSONL schema, existing rows, and the current cursor buffer; returns compile-ready suggestions; accepts one human-selected suggestion; and appends a verified instruction JSONL row.

Python is not the product runtime. Python remains only as tooling, fixture generation, preview rendering, compatibility checks, or migration support.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Purpose | Directness |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Remove post-merge ambiguity from `main` | Direct |
| 1 | Make exactly one product identity visible: `hq` | Direct |
| 2 | Put protocol fixtures, not implementation language, at the center of correctness | Direct |
| 3 | Make Go the official terminal runtime | Direct |
| 4 | Demote Python from product runtime to tools / reference checks | Direct |
| 5 | Keep Linux and Windows interactive Tab proof as UI-operation contracts | Direct |
| 6 | Separate product code, proof docs, generated artifacts, and vendored/offline material | Direct |
| 7 | Make the repo easy to understand for future maintainers and buyers | Indirect |
| 8 | Preserve a small reusable core for multiple business workflows | Indirect |
| 9 | Support high-margin software asset creation | Indirect |
| 10 | Support company value and sale-readiness | Meta |

## Current problem to resolve

The problem is not simply “Python vs Go”.

The problem is that product authority is split:

| Area | Current ambiguity |
|---|---|
| README | Presents the proof/runtime in a way that can read as the whole repo identity |
| Go module | Still carries proof / POC identity |
| command name | `hq-reflective` reads as a proof command, not the official CLI |
| Python package | Uses product-looking names and remains in CI |
| dist artifacts | Built binaries in repo can be mistaken for source authority |
| proof material | Proof and product material are not cleanly separated |
| CI | Operation proof exists, but protocol-contract ownership is not yet explicit |

## Final architecture

### Ownership model

| Layer | Owner | Final rule |
|---|---|---|
| Protocol | `spec/` | Source of correctness for JSONL world, cursor context, suggestions, compileDraft, acceptance, and instruction rows |
| Runtime | Go | Official CLI/REPL runtime for terminal use |
| Tools | Python | Fixture generation, preview generation, migration helpers, compatibility checks only |
| Proof | CI + `docs/proofs/` | Evidence that terminal UX claims are real on Linux and Windows |
| Artifacts | GitHub Actions / release artifacts | Generated binaries and proof captures live outside the committed source tree |
| Docs | README + ADRs | Explain the product, ownership, and why this split exists |

### Data flow

| Step | Input | Output | Owner |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | JSONL schema + existing rows + current buffer | `CursorContext` | Protocol / Go core |
| 2 | `CursorContext` + `JsonlWorld` | `Suggestion[]` | Go core |
| 3 | suggestion list + human choice | accepted suggestion | Runtime |
| 4 | accepted suggestion | `Instruction` / `compileDraft` finalization | Go core |
| 5 | instruction | append-only instruction JSONL row | Runtime |
| 6 | runtime session | Linux/Windows proof artifact | CI |

### Product identity

The repo must read as:

```text
hq
  JSONL-aware autocomplete compiler
  protocol-first
  Go runtime
  Python tooling
  Linux/Windows terminal proof
```

The repo must not read as:

```text
hq-reflective-poc
  Python POC + Go POC + proof files + committed binaries
```

## Final repo shape

| Path | Desired final role |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Product entrypoint for `hq`; no root-level POC identity |
| `docs/adr/0001-runtime-ownership.md` | Decision record: protocol-first, Go runtime, Python tooling |
| `docs/proofs/` | Human-readable proof notes for PR #11/#12 and future UI proof |
| `spec/` | Protocol schema and golden fixtures |
| `spec/fixtures/` | Golden JSON inputs/outputs for context, suggestions, compileDraft, acceptance, queue rows |
| `cmd/hq/` | Official CLI entrypoint |
| `internal/hq/` | Go core: JsonlWorld, CursorContext, Suggestion, Acceptance, InstructionQueue |
| `examples/` | Minimal schema, queue, and manual entry examples |
| `tools/` | Python tooling only; not product runtime |
| `.github/workflows/` | Protocol contract, Go runtime, Linux Tab proof, Windows Tab proof, docs/preview checks |
| `dist/` | Not committed; generated only as CI/release artifact |
| `third_party/` | Either removed or reduced to a manifest explaining exact offline proof material |

## Naming cleanup

| Current name / shape | Desired name / shape | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `hq-reflective-poc` | `hq` | Product should not identify as a POC |
| `cmd/hq-reflective` | `cmd/hq` | Official command must be clear |
| Python package named like product runtime | `tools/...` or `tests/reference/...` | Avoid two product runtimes |
| root proof docs | `docs/proofs/...` | Proof is important but not the root product |
| committed `dist/*` | CI/release artifact | Generated files should not be source authority |
| ad-hoc proof names | stable workflow/artifact names | CI must be reviewable and durable enough for PR review |

## Protocol contract: final minimum

The protocol contract must define at least these records:

| Record | Required fields | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `JsonlWorld` | schema, existing rows, known keys, required keys, allowed types | World state for suggestions |
| `CursorContext` | buffer, cursor position, object state, partial token, missing keys | Where the user is typing |
| `Suggestion` | label, detail, edit, kind, compileDraft | A meaning-bearing, accept-ready candidate |
| `Acceptance` | suggestion id, before buffer, after buffer, accepted at | Human choice boundary |
| `Instruction` | op, target, payload, provenance | Queueable final result |
| `QueueAppend` | path, row, append mode, expected behavior | Append-only instruction write |

A suggestion is not just a string completion. It must be an edit plus meaning plus compile draft.

## Golden fixture families

Add fixtures in small families. Each family should have input and expected output.

| Fixture family | Must prove |
|---|---|
| object-open-key-suggestions | At `{` cursor, required keys appear |
| partial-key-suggestions | At `{"ta` cursor, only matching valid keys appear |
| missing-required-key | Missing required keys are suggested before optional noise |
| existing-row-awareness | Known keys from existing rows can be reflected when schema allows |
| unknown-key-rejection | Unknown/out-of-context keys do not appear |
| compile-draft-present | Every suggestion carries compileDraft |
| accept-finalizes-instruction | Only accepted suggestion becomes an instruction row |
| unaccepted-is-not-queued | Candidate display alone never writes queue |
| schema-swap-changes-candidates | Changing JSONL schema changes suggestions without Go code changes |
| manual-entry-minimum | Manual JSONL entry gets key/value help without external API or agent dependencies |

## CI final state

| Workflow | Purpose | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `protocol-contract` | Protocol fixtures pass | golden JSON result artifact |
| `go-runtime` | Go tests and CLI smoke pass | test output |
| `linux-interactive-tab-proof` | Linux real terminal Tab UX works | `SENT_KEYS`, `SENT_BYTES_HEX: 7b2209`, visible candidates |
| `windows-interactive-tab-proof` | Windows terminal Tab UX works | `SENT_KEYS`, `SENT_BYTES_HEX: 7b2209`, visible candidates |
| `docs-preview` | README/proof docs match generated behavior where applicable | generated preview/text artifact |

Linux/Windows Tab proof must remain operation proof, not just `--complete` proof.

## Completion proof requirements

For any interactive Tab proof workflow:

- It must send literal Tab input, not only call non-interactive completion APIs.
- Artifact must include `SENT_KEYS`.
- Artifact must include `SENT_BYTES_HEX: 7b2209` for `{"` + Tab.
- Artifact must include visible candidates from a proof-only schema, such as `tabProofA`, `tabProofB`, `tabProofC`.
- Candidate names should not appear in seeded history, so history autosuggest cannot make the proof pass.
- Failure artifact should be uploaded where practical.
- The workflow should fail if marker grep fails.

## Product behavior final state

### CLI / REPL

| Behavior | Expected final result |
|---|---|
| user types JSONL object start | required key suggestions appear |
| user types partial key | low-noise matching key candidates appear |
| user presses Tab | visible candidates appear in terminal |
| user previews candidate | edit result and compileDraft are visible or inspectable |
| user accepts candidate | only accepted candidate becomes instruction |
| user does nothing | no queue write occurs |
| schema changes | suggestions change without code changes |
| Linux/Windows | same proof contract, OS-specific terminal harness allowed |

### Queue behavior

| Rule | Expected final result |
|---|---|
| queue target | JSONL only for this phase |
| append behavior | append-only, deterministic row |
| provenance | accepted suggestion and source context captured |
| unaccepted suggestions | never written |
| invalid instruction | rejected before queue append |

## Python final state

Python should remain only if it has a clear non-runtime role.

Allowed Python roles:

- generate fixtures
- check compatibility against protocol fixtures
- render preview HTML/screenshots
- migrate old fixture formats
- provide reference-only tests

Disallowed Python roles:

- product CLI authority
- second official runtime
- separate suggestion semantics not checked against `spec/`
- root package identity that makes Python look like the product

## Go final state

Go owns the product runtime.

Required Go ownership:

- `cmd/hq` official command
- `internal/hq` core model
- JSONL-aware completion
- compileDraft generation
- acceptance/finalization
- instruction queue append
- terminal integration
- Linux/Windows proof support

Go must not hardcode business-specific keys as product semantics. Business key sets must come from schema/fixtures/examples.

## Documentation final state

README must answer these in the first screen:

1. What is `hq`?
2. What problem does it solve?
3. What is the protocol?
4. What is the official runtime?
5. What proof exists for terminal Tab UX?
6. Where are Python tools, and why are they not product runtime?
7. How does a reviewer verify correctness?

ADR must answer:

1. Why protocol-first?
2. Why Go runtime?
3. Why Python tooling remains?
4. Why proof docs are separated?
5. Why binaries are not committed?
6. What future implementation additions are allowed?

## Non-goals for this issue

| Non-goal | Reason |
|---|---|
| Add remote API targets | Keep target JSONL-only for now |
| Add agent execution | `hq` builds queue; execution belongs elsewhere |
| Make fzf/vim/cmp core dependencies | They are UI projections, not core |
| Remove all Python immediately | Preserve useful tooling and migration value |
| Replace Linux/Windows proof with `--complete` only | That loses the operation proof we just added |
| Expand business domain schemas | First stabilize protocol ownership |

## Destructive objections to clear

| # | Objection | Required defense |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Python and Go both look like product runtimes | Move Python to tools/reference role and make Go the only runtime |
| 2 | Root README still reads as POC | Rewrite root README as `hq` product |
| 3 | Go module still says POC | Rename module/command identity |
| 4 | Committed binaries make repo heavy and ambiguous | Move generated binaries to artifact/release |
| 5 | vendored or stubbed deps make trust unclear | Remove or manifest/pin explicitly |
| 6 | Proof docs hide product intent | Move proof under docs/proofs and keep README product-first |
| 7 | Tab proof is strong but protocol is weak | Add protocol golden fixtures |
| 8 | Future implementations can reintroduce乱立 | ADR: new implementations are adapters/tools unless explicitly promoted |
| 9 | Windows proof can be flaky | Keep failure transcript and dependency pinning |
| 10 | Refactor can delete useful old knowledge | Move, do not blindly delete; preserve proof docs and tools where useful |

## Acceptance criteria

This issue can close only when all are true:

- [ ] README presents `hq`, not `hq-reflective-poc`, as the product identity.
- [ ] Go command path and binary name are `hq` or otherwise documented as the official runtime.
- [ ] Go module identity no longer carries proof/POC meaning.
- [ ] Python code is moved or renamed so it cannot be mistaken for the product runtime.
- [ ] Python role is documented as tools/reference/preview/migration only.
- [ ] `spec/` exists with golden fixtures for context, suggestion, compileDraft, acceptance, and instruction rows.
- [ ] Go tests consume the protocol fixtures.
- [ ] Python tooling, if retained, consumes the same protocol fixtures or is clearly outside semantic authority.
- [ ] `dist/*` committed binaries are removed or justified by a manifest and not treated as source authority.
- [ ] proof docs are under `docs/proofs/`.
- [ ] ADR exists for runtime ownership and protocol authority.
- [ ] Linux interactive Tab proof still passes.
- [ ] Windows interactive Tab proof still passes.
- [ ] CI artifacts still show `SENT_KEYS`, `SENT_BYTES_HEX: 7b2209`, and visible proof candidates.
- [ ] No workflow depends only on non-interactive `--complete` for the interactive Tab claim.
- [ ] A reviewer can tell, within one README screen, which parts are product, protocol, tools, and proof.

## Suggested PR slicing

Prefer multiple small PRs rather than one large cleanup PR.

| PR | Scope | Done when |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | README + ADR product identity | The intended final shape is visible without moving code |
| 2 | Rename Go module/command from proof identity to product identity | `cmd/hq` and official build path exist |
| 3 | Move Python to tools/reference role | Python no longer looks like runtime authority |
| 4 | Add `spec/fixtures` and protocol-contract CI | Correctness source is fixture-based |
| 5 | Remove committed binaries / clean generated artifacts | Source tree is lean |
| 6 | Move proof docs and stabilize proof artifact names | Proof remains reviewable but not root identity |

## Final expected repo readback

A maintainer should be able to say:

> `hq` is a Go terminal runtime for JSONL-aware autocomplete compilation. Its correctness is defined by protocol fixtures. Python is tooling. Linux and Windows terminal Tab UX are protected by interactive proof CI. Generated binaries and proof captures are artifacts, not source authority.

If that sentence is not true after the cleanup, this issue is not complete."}
