Connect `web-publication` to one versioned semantic HTML renderer owned by `roccho-dev/ui`, without copying renderer meaning into `web` and without letting the renderer own publication routes, admission, sources, relations, or bundle semantics.
| Scope | Replace the local pre-proof renderer coupling with a checked port. |
| Product | Make `web-publication` usable with a shared semantic renderer rather than a fixture-only implementation. |
| Architecture | Preserve one-directional dependency: `web-publication -> renderer port -> ui renderer`. |
| Reuse | Allow renderer replacement without changing publication graph or bundle contracts. |
| Transfer | Make ownership and compatibility failures explicit through receipts. |
| Meta | Reduce lock-in and duplicate implementation risk in the transferable product asset. |
The renderer must not receive provider credentials or become aware of hosting/CDN targets.
Define `ui.semanticHtmlRenderer.v1` with the smallest portable request/response surface.
Request must include only what rendering needs, such as:
- semantic component tree or approved A2UI surface/data;
- optional interaction attributes already determined by the publication plan.
It must not return routes, canonical decisions, page admission, publication graph mutations, provider deployment plans, or authority claims.
- add the consumer-side port types and validation;
- pin the selected `ui` renderer by exact revision/output digest;
- implement one adapter from `webPublication.plan.v1` to renderer requests;
- render both full documents and citation/interaction fragments through the same semantic catalog;
- inject renderer output into materialization without post-render semantic rewriting;
- record renderer input/output digests in the bundle and proof receipt;
- reject unknown renderer versions and semantic findings;
- add a temporary test double only for port conformance tests, never as selected product output.
- [ ] Full documents and fragments use the same selected renderer/version.
- [ ] Renderer cannot alter routes, canonicals, source identities, or admission.
- [ ] `web-publication` does not contain a second semantic component-to-HTML implementation.
- [ ] Raw HTML from external JSONL is rejected or escaped by the selected renderer.
- [ ] Renderer output bytes are not semantically rewritten by the materializer.
- [ ] Renderer revision/digest is present in `webPublication.proofReceipt.v1` and `webPublication.bundle.v1`.
- [ ] Same render request produces the same body digest.
- [ ] A conformance test proves another test renderer can satisfy the port without changing publication contracts.
- renderer returns route or canonical authority fields;
- renderer output contains unresolved raw HTML injection;
- full-page and fragment renderer versions differ;
- `web` copies `ui` renderer source into product core;
- `ui` begins importing page admission or publication bundle logic.
- defining the shared renderer implementation in this Issue;

Merge only after the selected `ui` renderer Issue is available at an exact revision, all conformance and destructive cases pass, dependency direction is mechanically checked, and a representative document plus fragment are included in a non-authority receipt.

body: Turn the implemented `web-publication` product into exact, replayable package claims and receipts consumable by governance and due diligence. Ensure clean-checkout reconstruction, exact candidate-SHA evidence, provider-neutral release output, and explicit residuals before parent closure.
| Scope | Wire the selected product checks and artifacts into one reproducible package/CI entrypoint. |
| Product | Make the actual package claim its identity, renderer, quality, scale, framework, and bundle state. |
| Governance | Bind every claim to the accepted ADRS digest and exact candidate SHA. |
| Transfer | Prove a third party can delete outputs and rebuild/inspect the product from pinned inputs. |
| Business | Expose measurable product evidence without treating generated sites as source authority. |
| Meta | Reduce diligence, migration, and hidden-dependency risk in the Web product asset. |
Before organization-active claims or parent closure:
- `adrs#244` must have an accepted validated decision record and exact digest;
- `ui#146` and #3 must provide/pin the selected renderer and digest;
- #5 must provide exact legacy status, even if historical parity remains explicitly unavailable/blocked;
- `governance#167` must define the accepted package-facing obligations.
Fixture/shadow work may precede ADRS acceptance only if clearly marked non-authority and blocked from final claims.
Claims must not state ranking, indexing, AI citation, traffic, revenue, deployment, or company sale outcomes.
If governance selects generic company-wide receipt kinds, package-local compatibility aliases must not create a second meaning authority.
Provide one pinned, non-interactive selected proof entrypoint that:
1. starts from declared external JSONL and exact renderer input;
2. builds the curated and scale proofs;
4. performs a deleted-output clean double build;
5. emits the provider-neutral bundle and all receipts;
7. packages generated pages as CI/Nix artifacts only;
8. returns nonzero on any missing/stale/unknown input or finding.
Declare every provider workflow in `ci.intent.v1.jsonl`. Provider YAML is an adapter artifact, not authority.
From a clean checkout at the exact candidate SHA:
- delete all generated output and caches;
- execute the selected proof using documented commands;
- reproduce all required receipts and bundle root digest;
- show no untracked source/config is required;
- show no credentials/network deployment effects are required;
- record environment/toolchain identity without making one host authoritative;
- provide a reviewer readback explaining owner boundaries and how to rebuild.
- candidate SHA differs from receipt target;
- any required proof/readiness/browser/determinism receipt is absent or stale;
- generated output is tracked or described as authority;
- Astro is required by the selected proof;
- provider SDK/credential/deploy state enters the package;
- legacy status is omitted or parity overclaimed;
- clean checkout cannot reproduce the bundle root digest;
- governance package response omits `web-publication` or its required receipt set.
Expose a repo/package evidence packet consumable by `governance#167`, containing:
- candidate SHA and accepted ADRS digest.
No branch-protection/cutover effect is part of this Issue.
- [ ] One documented selected proof command emits all required artifacts.
- [ ] All claims bind accepted decision digest and exact candidate SHA.

- legacy status is omitted or parity overclaimed;
- clean checkout cannot reproduce the bundle root digest;
- governance package response omits `web-publication` or its required receipt set.

- candidate SHA and accepted ADRS digest.

{"body":"## Purpose

Let edits verify that a queue row it wrote is the same queue row referenced by the ops cross-repo receipt.

## Scope

- Read an ops cross-repo receipt fixture.
- Compare receipt queueDigest with the digest of an edits-generated queue row.
- Fail clearly on mismatch.
- Keep verification local and non-authority.

## Done

- Matching queue digest passes.
- Mismatched queue digest fails.
- Verification does not run ops worker, admission, or ui preview.
- Docs explain that edits writes queue rows and ops owns receipt generation.

## Scope-achievement declaration

This issue is complete only when all of the following are true:

- Purpose lineage: directly proves the editor side of editor-to-queue-to-ui and indirectly supports cross-repo auditability.
- Core/port/adapter: digest calculation and comparison are pure core; reading receipt/queue fixtures is adapter; receipt schema is an ops port.
- Pure/effect split: digest compare has no side effects; file reads are isolated in adapter code.
- False-positive exclusion: matching queueDigest/queue row pairs must pass.
- False-negative exclusion: mismatched, mutated, or authority-confusing queue rows must fail.
- Authority boundary: edits verifies receipt references only; it does not generate ops receipts or accepted state.
- Repo cleanliness: no ops worker, admission, projection, or ui preview code is introduced into edits.

## Non-goals

- Do not generate ops receipts in edits.
- Do not write accepted ledger.
- Do not render UI.

## Checks

- queue digest match/mismatch checks.
- edits command conversion checks still pass.
- Boundary check still passes.

## Depends on

- #51
- #52
- roccho-dev/ops#51

## Why this matters

This closes the edits-side proof that the editor surface produced the exact queue intent processed downstream."}

body: This is the repository-owned parent implementation and closure issue for `roccho-dev/web/packages/web-publication`.

Accepted meaning remains in `roccho-dev/adrs`. This mutable Issue is an implementation and review surface, not independent decision authority. Opening it authorizes no deployment, provider credential use, DNS/CDN mutation, production cutover, or legacy deletion.

Establish `web-publication` as a reusable product package that compiles an external JSONL knowledge graph into deterministic, discovery-ready, internally linked Web publication bundles through a replaceable semantic renderer.
> `web-publication` turns external meaning into deterministic, index-ready and citation-addressable Web publication bundles. It does not deploy or host them.
SEO, GEO, AIO, AEO, and LLMO are evaluation concerns represented by one discovery-readiness contract. They are not separate product authorities and must not become hard-coded core vocabularies.
| Scope | Move the non-Astro pre-proof into a checked package and make it reproducible from a clean checkout. |
| Product | Expose a domain-neutral JSONL-to-publication library and CLI instead of a one-off fixture script. |
| Quality | Prove semantic initial HTML, canonical routes, crawlable links, sources, citations, and HTMX fragment integrity. |

| Architecture | Keep publication graph and route ownership in `web`, semantic HTML rendering in `ui`, accepted meaning in ADRS, governance joins in `governance`, and physical delivery outside this repo. |
| Reuse | Prove the same compiler with a curated quality fixture and a generated 5,000-page scale fixture without domain-specific core changes. |
| Operations | Emit a provider-neutral bundle that a future delivery owner can deploy without changing publication meaning. |
| Business | Make domain-specific Web networks primarily a data/configuration change rather than a new site implementation. |
| Transfer | Allow a new operator to delete generated output, rebuild it from pinned inputs, verify it, and identify every owner boundary. |
| Meta | Produce a separately inspectable, reproducible product asset that contributes to a higher-value and more transferable company. |

Closing this Issue does not claim that company sale, search ranking, indexing, or AI citation has occurred. It closes the verified causal contribution from implementation scope to those upper purposes.
`roccho-dev/web` is currently a new repository with no product implementation. A local non-authority pre-proof showed an Astro-free replacement is feasible, but it is not yet an active product asset.
| browser HTMX runtime | NOT YET EXECUTED |
| external indexing observation | OUT OF SCOPE |
This evidence proves replacement feasibility only. It is not selected production proof and is not authority.
Owns the repository map and `packages/web-publication` product boundary. Root must not become an implementation package.
- projection into a versioned semantic renderer port;
`web-publication` must consume this through a versioned renderer port and must not create a second semantic renderer authority.
Owns accepted purpose, repository responsibilities, framework policy, deletion conditions, exceptions, and the accepted decision digest.
Owns projection of the accepted ADRS decision into package claims, required receipts, drift findings, and final-scope joins.
Owns domain, hosting, CDN, credentials, provider APIs, release promotion, rollback, and public crawl/index/citation observations. No physical delivery implementation is required here.
| `webPublication.graph.v1` | External page, source, relation, and citation meaning. |
| `webPublication.discoveryProfile.v1` | Search-, AI-, and agent-facing readiness requirements. |

{"body":"## Normative status

This is the repository-owned parent implementation and closure issue for `roccho-dev/web/packages/web-publication`.

```text
decisionAuthority=false
runtimeEffects=false
physicalDeploymentOutOfScope=true
legacyDeletionAuthorized=false
historicalParity=BLOCKED_SOURCE_NOT_RECOVERED
generatedArtifactsAreAuthority=false
```

Accepted meaning remains in `roccho-dev/adrs`. This mutable Issue is an implementation and review surface, not independent decision authority. Opening it authorizes no deployment, provider credential use, DNS/CDN mutation, production cutover, or legacy deletion.

## Purpose

Establish `web-publication` as a reusable product package that compiles an external JSONL knowledge graph into deterministic, discovery-ready, internally linked Web publication bundles through a replaceable semantic renderer.

> `web-publication` turns external meaning into deterministic, index-ready and citation-addressable Web publication bundles. It does not deploy or host them.

SEO, GEO, AIO, AEO, and LLMO are evaluation concerns represented by one discovery-readiness contract. They are not separate product authorities and must not become hard-coded core vocabularies.

## Scope-to-meta closure

| Level | Required contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Move the non-Astro pre-proof into a checked package and make it reproducible from a clean checkout. |
| Product | Expose a domain-neutral JSONL-to-publication library and CLI instead of a one-off fixture script. |
| Quality | Prove semantic initial HTML, canonical routes, crawlable links, sources, citations, and HTMX fragment integrity. |
| Architecture | Keep publication graph and route ownership in `web`, semantic HTML rendering in `ui`, accepted meaning in ADRS, governance joins in `governance`, and physical delivery outside this repo. |
| Reuse | Prove the same compiler with a curated quality fixture and a generated 5,000-page scale fixture without domain-specific core changes. |
| Operations | Emit a provider-neutral bundle that a future delivery owner can deploy without changing publication meaning. |
| Business | Make domain-specific Web networks primarily a data/configuration change rather than a new site implementation. |
| Transfer | Allow a new operator to delete generated output, rebuild it from pinned inputs, verify it, and identify every owner boundary. |
| Meta | Produce a separately inspectable, reproducible product asset that contributes to a higher-value and more transferable company. |

Closing this Issue does not claim that company sale, search ranking, indexing, or AI citation has occurred. It closes the verified causal contribution from implementation scope to those upper purposes.

## Current state

`roccho-dev/web` is currently a new repository with no product implementation. A local non-authority pre-proof showed an Astro-free replacement is feasible, but it is not yet an active product asset.

Observed pre-proof:

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| replacement feasibility | PASS |
| content pages | 5,000 |
| source pages | 100 |
| relation edges | 10,000 |
| citations / fragments | 5,000 |
| broken internal links | 0 |
| orphan pages | 0 |
| unresolved HTMX targets | 0 |
| destructive tests | 12 / 12 PASS |
| active Astro findings | 0 |
| active retired-specs references | 0 |
| deterministic double build | PASS |
| root digest | `ee618eec8c58d0c6349deb8fb2181f3d18d2b0745eb53ccebf485b246ac55a49` |
| browser HTMX runtime | NOT YET EXECUTED |
| external indexing observation | OUT OF SCOPE |
| historical semantic parity | BLOCKED |
| deletion authorized | false |

Pre-proof archive SHA-256:

```text
18b5c9a032c15c2e143316cb6d1809767c1c93bfd4a20cc7c68f9cd634feab98
```

This evidence proves replacement feasibility only. It is not selected production proof and is not authority.

## Ownership boundary

### `roccho-dev/web`

Owns the repository map and `packages/web-publication` product boundary. Root must not become an implementation package.

### `packages/web-publication`

Owns:

- publication graph validation;
- page/source/relation/citation records;
- page admission and route planning;
- projection into a versioned semantic renderer port;
- static page-network materialization;
- provider-neutral publication bundle generation;
- discovery-readiness verification;
- proof, readiness, and legacy-retirement receipts.

### `roccho-dev/ui`

Owns:

- A2UI/SDUI semantic component catalog;
- component-to-semantic-HTML rendering;
- escaping and raw-HTML rejection;
- full-document and fragment rendering;
- renderer-specific evidence.

`web-publication` must consume this through a versioned renderer port and must not create a second semantic renderer authority.

### `roccho-dev/adrs`

Owns accepted purpose, repository responsibilities, framework policy, deletion conditions, exceptions, and the accepted decision digest.

### `roccho-dev/governance`

Owns projection of the accepted ADRS decision into package claims, required receipts, drift findings, and final-scope joins.

### Future physical delivery owner

Owns domain, hosting, CDN, credentials, provider APIs, release promotion, rollback, and public crawl/index/citation observations. No physical delivery implementation is required here.

## Public contracts

| Contract | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `webPublication.graph.v1` | External page, source, relation, and citation meaning. |
| `webPublication.discoveryProfile.v1` | Search-, AI-, and agent-facing readiness requirements. |
| `webPublication.plan.v1` | Admitted pages, routes, canonicals, fragments, assets, and output plan. |
| `ui.semanticHtmlRenderer.v1` | Replaceable semantic document/fragment renderer port consumed from `ui`. |
| `webPublication.bundle.v1` | Provider-neutral files, routes, assets, redirects, headers, sitemaps, and root digest. |
| `webPublication.proofReceipt.v1` | Input, renderer, build, output, determinism, and scale evidence. |
| `webPublication.discoveryReadinessReceipt.v1` | Semantic HTML, link, citation, canonical, admission, and browser evidence. |
| `webPublication.legacyRetirementReceipt.v1` | Legacy inventory, parity/absence finding, deletion manifest, and rollback digest. |
| `webPublication.packageClaim.v1` | Repo claim against the exact accepted ADRS decision digest. |

Every generated bundle must carry:

```text
generatedArtifactsAreAuthority=false
```

## Publication bundle boundary

`webPublication.bundle.v1` is this package's terminal output. It may contain route-to-file mappings, HTML documents/fragments, assets, canonicals, redirects, provider-neutral headers, sitemaps, source/input/renderer/build digests, and one deterministic root digest.

It must not contain credentials, DNS mutations, provider ownership, release approval, production promotion authority, or provider runtime state.

## Positive proofs

### Curated quality proof

A small human-reviewed fixture must prove:

- one explicit page intent per admitted page;
- unique route and canonical;
- meaningful initial HTML without client rendering;
- exactly one primary H1;
- supported factual content and traceable sources where claims are made;
- crawlable internal `a[href]` relations;
- zero exact normalized-content duplicates;
- root reachability;
- JavaScript-free navigation fallback.

Only this fixture may claim `discoveryReadiness=PASS`.

### Generated scale proof

Must reproduce or exceed:

- 5,000 content pages;
- 100 source pages;
- 10,000 relation edges;
- 5,000 citations/fragments;
- zero broken links, orphan pages, unresolved fragments, duplicate routes, or duplicate canonicals;
- two clean builds with the same root digest.

It must carry:

```text
proofOnly=true
publishableContentClaim=false
```

It proves topology, scale, and determinism—not human value, ranking, indexing, or citation success.

## Browser proof

A headless browser must prove:

1. representative full page loads over HTTP;
2. primary content exists before client JavaScript;
3. citation control triggers the expected HTMX request;
4. expected fragment is inserted into the declared target;
5. citation retains a crawlable/fallback link;
6. history-visible URLs direct-load as complete documents;
7. no blocking client error prevents reading or navigation.

## Destructive proofs

At least these must fail closed:

1. duplicate route;
2. duplicate canonical;
3. dangling internal relation;
4. orphan admitted page;
5. missing citation source;
6. unsafe/path-traversal route;
7. unsupported semantic component;
8. missing primary H1;
9. raw HTML injection;
10. Astro dependency, command, or `.astro` source reintroduction into the canonical proof;
11. active reference to retired `specs-main/packages/jsonl-surface-lib-proof`;
12. output manifest tampering;
13. duplicate normalized content in the curated fixture;
14. scale fixture claiming publication readiness;
15. provider credentials or provider SDK entering the package;
16. generated output represented as authority.

## Framework policy

The canonical proof must have zero required Astro dependencies, `.astro` files, Astro commands, Astro-owned page/layout/route/component meaning, and active retired `spec`/`specs` package paths.

A future Astro adapter may exist only as an optional outer adapter. It must not be required for the selected proof, define publication meaning, or change the canonical bundle contract.

## Historical Astro retirement

Legacy retirement must use an exact deletion manifest. Wildcard claims such as “remove all Astro repositories” are forbidden.

For every candidate record repository, exact path, candidate kind, current consumers, replacement path, replacement evidence digest, rollback source/digest, status, blocker, and deletion PR SHA.

Two valid closure routes exist:

### Route A — exact source recovered

Execute the historical proof unchanged, create a semantic snapshot, execute `web-publication` from the same canonical input, require 100% parity for agreed semantic fields, select the replacement, delete only exact candidates, and prove rollback restores the historical proof.

### Route B — no active historical surface

Inventory all active references/consumers, prove the selected package has no Astro dependency/source/command, prove no active command points to the retired path, remove only confirmed stale references, and record:

```text
historicalParity=NOT_CLAIMED_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
```

No reconstructed historical evidence may be represented as original evidence.

## Required implementation slices

- [ ] Current-tree inventory and collision receipt.
- [ ] Repository and product identity.
- [ ] Framework-neutral product core and bundle contract.
- [ ] Versioned semantic renderer boundary with `ui`.
- [ ] Curated quality, 5,000-page scale, browser, deterministic, and destructive proofs.
- [ ] Pinned package/Nix build, CI intent, claims, receipts, and artifacts.
- [ ] Exact historical inventory, parity/absence route, deletion manifest, and rollback proof.
- [ ] Accepted ADRS digest and governance handoff.

Child issues own implementation slices. This parent alone owns final product closure.

## Non-goals

This Issue does not deploy or host, select a domain, mutate DNS, own provider configuration or credentials, guarantee crawl/index/ranking/AI citation/traffic/revenue, create a CMS/editorial workflow/customer database, make A2UI or generated HTML meaning authority, turn `web` into an experiment dump, delete unrelated Astro repositories, require Astro, replace ADRS authority, or make local package green equivalent to organization-active compliance.

## Required evidence outputs

```text
webPublication.packageClaim.v1.jsonl
webPublication.proofReceipt.v1.json
webPublication.discoveryReadinessReceipt.v1.json
webPublication.legacyRetirementReceipt.v1.json
webPublication.bundle.v1.json
MANIFEST.sha256
```

Generated pages and bundles are CI/Nix artifacts, not tracked authority.

## Parent close condition

Do not close because a package directory exists, 5,000 files were generated, a screenshot exists, local tests pass, a CI artifact uploaded, Astro disappeared from one manifest, or one child PR merged.

Close only after a final review comment records:

- accepted ADRS ref and decision digest;
- all child Issue and PR numbers;
- selected exact commit SHA;
- clean CI result;
- curated readiness receipt digest;
- scale proof receipt digest;
- bundle root digest;
- renderer ref and digest;
- legacy retirement status and receipt digest;
- remaining residuals;
- explicit human approval to close.

## Reviewer readback

At completion a reviewer must be able to say:

> `roccho-dev/web` contains one bounded product package, `web-publication`. It compiles external JSONL meaning into deterministic, discovery-ready Web publication bundles through a replaceable semantic HTML renderer owned by `ui`. It owns publication planning, page networks, materialization, bundle generation, and readiness checks, but not accepted meaning, physical deployment, credentials, or external search/AI outcomes. Quality, scale, determinism, browser behavior, framework independence, legacy retirement, and ADRS/governance handoff are proven by reproducible receipts.

If the repository, package, tests, or receipts no longer support that sentence, the product boundary is broken."}

{"body":"Ref: #312 — UI projection / view boundary design normalization

Ref: roccho-dev/adrs#468
Rel: implements-ui-boundary

Refs: #207 #212 #277 #190 #302 #310
Related: roccho-dev/adrs#382

## Status

```text
record_type: repository completion target
status: OPEN
parent: roccho-dev/adrs#468
implementation_started: false
accepted_meaning_authority: false
provider_delivery_owned_here: false
```

## Purpose

ADRS #468 のうち、UI が所有する完成状態だけを閉じる。

> upstream source から、必須だが値集合は固定しない audience 次元で安全な projection を作り、既存の view / semantic zoom / invocation / shell を使って、再現可能な URL と portable single HTML へ到達できるようにする。

このIssueは新しいUI architectureを作らない。#207 / #212 / #277 / #190 の現行境界を再利用し、Audienceをrendererやproviderへ混ぜない。

## Target state

```text
Upstream Source
  ↓
Project(audience_ref)
  ↓
Allowed UI Projection
  ↓
View(profile + focus + depth / LOD)
  ↓
artifact-invocation/2
  ↓
Artifact Shell
  ├─ canonical reproducible URL
  └─ portable single HTML
```

意味は次で固定する。

```text
Audience = その受け手へ存在を渡してよい世界
View     = その安全な世界をどう見るか
Renderer = A2UI / Semantic Map 等でどう描くか
Host     = invocationをどう再現・実行するか
```

## Dynamic audience invariant

`audience` は projection の必須次元とする。ただし値集合は固定しない。

```text
required dimension: audience_ref
allowed values: open set of exact trusted profiles
hard-coded enum: none
unknown profile: BLOCK
removed/stale profile: BLOCK
fallback to dev/root: forbidden
```

`dev / client / ops / team` は現在の代表例・fixtureにはできるが、schemaの列挙値やcore分岐にはしない。

新しいaudienceの追加・既存audienceの削除は、同じprojection contractを満たす限りcore source変更を要求しない。

## Existing boundaries to preserve

- `source-compiler`: upstream/source → UI projection seam
- `ui-ir`: renderer-neutral capability invocation boundary
- A2UI: structured UI renderer capability
- Semantic Map: graph / seq / map と focus / zoom / LOD を扱うsemantic/spatial renderer
- maxGraph: Semantic Mapの描画adapter。意味sourceにはしない
- `artifact-invocation/2`: shareable/replayable view invocation
- Artifact Shell: generic browser/runtime composition root

Audience profileはA2UI、maxGraph、Artifact Shell、provider名へ埋め込まない。

## Required behavior

1. projection前のsourceから、exact audience profileで開示可能範囲を決定する。
2. 許可されない値はrendererへ渡さず、HTML/URL payloadにも含めない。
3. audienceとviewを独立させる。同じaudienceでgraph / seq / map / structured、focus、depthを変えられる。
4. View操作から exact invocation を生成し、新しいbrowser/reload/back-forwardで同じsemantic viewを再現できる。
5. 同じsource/profile/view identityから同じsemantic invocation identityを得る。
6. focus / depth / projection profileのmaterialな変更は別view identityになる。
7. portable HTMLはそのaudienceに許されたprojectionだけを含む。
8. portable HTMLはJavaScript無効でも最低限の意味を読める。
9. UI projection、URL、HTML、receiptはいずれもupstream meaning authorityにならない。
10. renderer/hostはupstream Sourceへ直接到達せず、安全化済みProjectionだけをconsumeする。

## Proof / acceptance

- [ ] 任意名のaudience profile A / B / newly-added Cを、core分岐追加なしで処理できる
- [ ] unknown / removed / stale audience profileがfail closedする
- [ ] root/full profileへの暗黙fallbackがない
- [ ] forbidden sentinelがProjection、invocation payload、URL、portable HTML bytesのいずれにも存在しない
- [ ] audienceを固定したままview/focus/depthを変えられる
- [ ] same exact source + audience profile + view → same semantic invocation identity
- [ ] A2UIで一つのprojected viewをreal browser表示できる
- [ ] Semantic Mapで一つのprojected viewをgraph/seq/mapまたは該当する既存profileでreal browser表示できる
- [ ] zoom/focus/LOD後のviewをURL化しfresh browserで再現できる
- [ ] 同じviewからportable single HTMLを生成しfresh browserで読める
- [ ] JavaScript無効時も最低限の本文・provenance/canonical referenceを読める
- [ ] source/profile/view/invocation/artifactのexact identityを追跡できる
- [ ] existing #207 / #212 / #277 / #190 semanticsを複製・置換しない

## PR closure rule

本Issueは1つ以上のPRで実現してよい。PR数・file配置は固定しない。

各PRはこのIssueの一部の完成条件を、exact source + test + evidenceで閉じる。最後のPRまたはfinal readbackで上記acceptanceを同一current treeに対して満たした時に本Issueをcloseする。

## Non-goals

- audience値を `dev/client/ops/team` に固定する
- audienceごとの専用renderer / app / source schemaを作る
- 新しい万能View DSLを作る
- 新しいURL codecを作る
- A2UIとSemantic Mapを一つのrendererへ統合する
- maxGraph/SVGをmeaning authorityにする
- Slack / Teams / Discord / Gmail等のdeliveryをUIが所有する
- UIが利用者の実permissionや公開許可を発明する
- provider capability、delivery retry、remote readbackをUIへ入れる
- #207 / #212 / #277 / #190 / #302 / #310を本Issueのcloseだけで自動closeする
"}

{"body":"Ref: #312 — UI projection / view boundary design normalization

Ref: roccho-dev/adrs#468
Rel: implements-ui-boundary

Refs: #207 #212 #277 #190 #302 #310
Related: roccho-dev/adrs#382

## Status

```text
record_type: repository completion target
status: OPEN
parent: roccho-dev/adrs#468
implementation_started: false
accepted_meaning_authority: false
provider_delivery_owned_here: false
```

## Purpose

ADRS #468 のうち、UI が所有する完成状態だけを閉じる。

> upstream source から、必須だが値集合は固定しない audience 次元で安全な projection を作り、既存の view / semantic zoom / invocation / shell を使って、再現可能な URL と portable single HTML へ到達できるようにする。

このIssueは新しいUI architectureを作らない。#207 / #212 / #277 / #190 の現行境界を再利用し、Audienceをrendererやproviderへ混ぜない。

## Target state

```text
Upstream Source
  ↓
Project(audience_ref)
  ↓
Allowed UI Projection
  ↓
View(profile + focus + depth / LOD)
  ↓
artifact-invocation/2
  ↓
Artifact Shell
  ├─ canonical reproducible URL
  └─ portable single HTML
```

意味は次で固定する。

```text
Audience = その受け手へ存在を渡してよい世界
View     = その安全な世界をどう見るか
Renderer = A2UI / Semantic Map 等でどう描くか
Host     = invocationをどう再現・実行するか
```

## Dynamic audience invariant

`audience` は projection の必須次元とする。ただし値集合は固定しない。

```text
required dimension: audience_ref
allowed values: open set of exact trusted profiles
hard-coded enum: none
unknown profile: BLOCK
removed/stale profile: BLOCK
fallback to dev/root: forbidden
```

`dev / client / ops / team` は現在の代表例・fixtureにはできるが、schemaの列挙値やcore分岐にはしない。

新しいaudienceの追加・既存audienceの削除は、同じprojection contractを満たす限りcore source変更を要求しない。

## Existing boundaries to preserve

- `source-compiler`: upstream/source → UI projection seam
- `ui-ir`: renderer-neutral capability invocation boundary
- A2UI: structured UI renderer capability
- Semantic Map: graph / seq / map と focus / zoom / LOD を扱うsemantic/spatial renderer
- maxGraph: Semantic Mapの描画adapter。意味sourceにはしない
- `artifact-invocation/2`: shareable/replayable view invocation
- Artifact Shell: generic browser/runtime composition root

Audience profileはA2UI、maxGraph、Artifact Shell、provider名へ埋め込まない。

## Required behavior

1. projection前のsourceから、exact audience profileで開示可能範囲を決定する。
2. 許可されない値はrendererへ渡さず、HTML/URL payloadにも含めない。
3. audienceとviewを独立させる。同じaudienceでgraph / seq / map / structured、focus、depthを変えられる。
4. View操作から exact invocation を生成し、新しいbrowser/reload/back-forwardで同じsemantic viewを再現できる。
5. 同じsource/profile/view identityから同じsemantic invocation identityを得る。
6. focus / depth / projection profileのmaterialな変更は別view identityになる。
7. portable HTMLはそのaudienceに許されたprojectionだけを含む。
8. portable HTMLはJavaScript無効でも最低限の意味を読める。
9. UI projection、URL、HTML、receiptはいずれもupstream meaning authorityにならない。
10. renderer/hostはupstream Sourceへ直接到達せず、安全化済みProjectionだけをconsumeする。

## Proof / acceptance

- [ ] 任意名のaudience profile A / B / newly-added Cを、core分岐追加なしで処理できる
- [ ] unknown / removed / stale audience profileがfail closedする
- [ ] root/full profileへの暗黙fallbackがない
- [ ] forbidden sentinelがProjection、invocation payload、URL、portable HTML bytesのいずれにも存在しない
- [ ] audienceを固定したままview/focus/depthを変えられる
- [ ] same exact source + audience profile + view → same semantic invocation identity
- [ ] A2UIで一つのprojected viewをreal browser表示できる
- [ ] Semantic Mapで一つのprojected viewをgraph/seq/mapまたは該当する既存profileでreal browser表示できる
- [ ] zoom/focus/LOD後のviewをURL化しfresh browserで再現できる
- [ ] 同じviewからportable single HTMLを生成しfresh browserで読める
- [ ] JavaScript無効時も最低限の本文・provenance/canonical referenceを読める
- [ ] source/profile/view/invocation/artifactのexact identityを追跡できる
- [ ] existing #207 / #212 / #277 / #190 semanticsを複製・置換しない

## PR closure rule

本Issueは1つ以上のPRで実現してよい。PR数・file配置は固定しない。

各PRはこのIssueの一部の完成条件を、exact source + test + evidenceで閉じる。最後のPRまたはfinal readbackで上記acceptanceを同一current treeに対して満たした時に本Issueをcloseする。

## Non-goals

- audience値を `dev/client/ops/team` に固定する
- audienceごとの専用renderer / app / source schemaを作る
- 新しい万能View DSLを作る
- 新しいURL codecを作る
- A2UIとSemantic Mapを一つのrendererへ統合する
- maxGraph/SVGをmeaning authorityにする
- Slack / Teams / Discord / Gmail等のdeliveryをUIが所有する
- UIが利用者の実permissionや公開許可を発明する
- provider capability、delivery retry、remote readbackをUIへ入れる
- #207 / #212 / #277 / #190 / #302 / #310を本Issueのcloseだけで自動closeする
"}

{"body":"結論：**まだ解決済みではない。  
ただし、解く型はかなり明確です。**

最も理想はこれです。

| 層 | 責務 |
|---|---|
| `data/world model` | repo/package/dir/file/symbol と依存graphを持つ |
| `LOD reducer` | z値に応じて「今見せる粒度」を決める |
| `layout adapter` | treemap / Voronoi / 将来別layoutを差し替える |
| `camera adapter` | scroll → z / pan / scale を扱う |
| `relation overlay` | 依存線を集約・展開して重ねる |
| `A2UI renderer` | browser component registryで描くだけ |

大事なのは、**層をUXにしないこと**です。

```text
悪い:
repo層 → package層 → dir層 → file層 → symbol層

良い:
continuous z
  → そのzで最も意味があるnode集合を選ぶ
  → 依存線もその粒度へ集約する
  → 見た目は地図のまま
```

つまり、内部にはLOD段階があってよい。  
でもユーザー体験は **無段階z** にする。

地図ライブラリも実際には完全な無段階情報表示ではなく、ズーム値に応じて tile / label / feature density を切り替えています。近い既存概念は semantic zoom で、Prefuse など古い可視化基盤にも geometric / semantic zoom はあります。([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefuse?utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
最近の研究でも、semantic zoom と edge bundling を組み合わせて、macro / meso / micro 表現を切り替える方向が使われています。([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08823?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

ただし、**ui.gitの現状はそこまで行っていない**です。  
#109 は `Contract Model Atlas` を read-model artifact として追加し、`preview/index.html` や `data.contract-model-atlas.v1.jsonl` を生成するものです。fileciteturn8file0L34-L54  
実装も JSONL fixture を読み、静的preview HTMLを生成する形で、scroll-z探索ではありません。fileciteturn16file0L31-L46  
CI artifact は出ており、#110 head の workflows は success ですが、これは生成・証跡の成功であって、地図的drilldownの完成ではありません。fileciteturn30file0L1-L1

理想形は **“repo map OS”** です。

| 概念 | 意味 |
|---|---|
| map world | 全repoの構造と依存を持つ世界 |
| camera.z | 抽象度。repo遠景からsymbol近景まで |
| focus | 現在見ている中心。nodeとは限らずregionでもよい |
| LOD | zに応じた表示粒度 |
| aggregate edge | 遠景用の依存線。symbol依存をpackage/file単位へ畳む |
| detail edge | 近景用の依存線。symbol単位 |
| hit target | そのzで操作可能な最小意味単位 |

依存graphはこう扱うのが美しいです。

| z | node表示 | edge表示 |
|---:|---|---|
| 遠い | repo / package | package間の集約依存 |
| 中間 | dir / file | file間の集約依存 |
| 近い | symbol | symbol間の実依存 |
| かなり近い | symbol detail | call/import/reference の種別表示 |

重要なのは、**edgeもzに応じて畳む**ことです。

```text
symbol A → symbol B
symbol C → symbol D
symbol E → symbol F

遠景では:
package X → package Y  dependencies: 3
```

これで「全容」と「深掘り」が両立します。

今のCI結果の失敗は、**1枚の静的な面で抽象度を解決しようとしたこと**です。  
それだと、見えるものを固定するしかない。  
treeの良さである「制限」は得られるが、地図の良さである「移動しながら全容を保つ」は得られない。

なので次に作るべきものは、rendererではなくこれです。

| 作るもの | 役割 |
|---|---|
| `repoMap.world.v1.jsonl` | containment + dependency のtyped graph |
| `repoMap.lod.v1` | zごとの表示粒度ルール |
| `repoMap.projection.v1` | z/camera/focusからA2UI用viewへ畳む |
| `layoutAdapter.treemap.v1` | 暫定配置 |
| `layoutAdapter.voronoi.v1` | 将来配置 |
| `relationOverlay.v1` | 依存線の集約・展開 |
| `cameraState` | scrollで変わる一時状態。永続authorityではない |

A2UI/component registry はそのままでよいです。  
変えるべきは **A2UI契約ではなく、A2UIへ渡す前の projection** です。

最終判断：

**この世界一般では、semantic zoom / map-like graph / edge bundling という部品は存在する。  
でも “repo全体の構造 + 依存graph + CI証跡 + A2UI契約 + scroll-driven z drilldown” としては、ui.gitでは未解決。**

最も理想的な方向は、  
**静的Atlasを捨てるのではなく、Atlasを `world model → LOD projection → A2UI render` に昇格させること**です。"}

{"body":"結論：**まだ解決済みではない。  
ただし、解く型はかなり明確です。**

最も理想はこれです。

| 層 | 責務 |
|---|---|
| `data/world model` | repo/package/dir/file/symbol と依存graphを持つ |
| `LOD reducer` | z値に応じて「今見せる粒度」を決める |
| `layout adapter` | treemap / Voronoi / 将来別layoutを差し替える |
| `camera adapter` | scroll → z / pan / scale を扱う |
| `relation overlay` | 依存線を集約・展開して重ねる |
| `A2UI renderer` | browser component registryで描くだけ |

大事なのは、**層をUXにしないこと**です。

```text
悪い:
repo層 → package層 → dir層 → file層 → symbol層

良い:
continuous z
  → そのzで最も意味があるnode集合を選ぶ
  → 依存線もその粒度へ集約する
  → 見た目は地図のまま
```

つまり、内部にはLOD段階があってよい。  
でもユーザー体験は **無段階z** にする。

地図ライブラリも実際には完全な無段階情報表示ではなく、ズーム値に応じて tile / label / feature density を切り替えています。近い既存概念は semantic zoom で、Prefuse など古い可視化基盤にも geometric / semantic zoom はあります。([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefuse?utm_source=chatgpt.com))  
最近の研究でも、semantic zoom と edge bundling を組み合わせて、macro / meso / micro 表現を切り替える方向が使われています。([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08823?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

ただし、**ui.gitの現状はそこまで行っていない**です。  
#109 は `Contract Model Atlas` を read-model artifact として追加し、`preview/index.html` や `data.contract-model-atlas.v1.jsonl` を生成するものです。fileciteturn8file0L34-L54  
実装も JSONL fixture を読み、静的preview HTMLを生成する形で、scroll-z探索ではありません。fileciteturn16file0L31-L46  
CI artifact は出ており、#110 head の workflows は success ですが、これは生成・証跡の成功であって、地図的drilldownの完成ではありません。fileciteturn30file0L1-L1

理想形は **“repo map OS”** です。

| 概念 | 意味 |
|---|---|
| map world | 全repoの構造と依存を持つ世界 |
| camera.z | 抽象度。repo遠景からsymbol近景まで |
| focus | 現在見ている中心。nodeとは限らずregionでもよい |
| LOD | zに応じた表示粒度 |
| aggregate edge | 遠景用の依存線。symbol依存をpackage/file単位へ畳む |
| detail edge | 近景用の依存線。symbol単位 |
| hit target | そのzで操作可能な最小意味単位 |

依存graphはこう扱うのが美しいです。

| z | node表示 | edge表示 |
|---:|---|---|
| 遠い | repo / package | package間の集約依存 |
| 中間 | dir / file | file間の集約依存 |
| 近い | symbol | symbol間の実依存 |
| かなり近い | symbol detail | call/import/reference の種別表示 |

重要なのは、**edgeもzに応じて畳む**ことです。

```text
symbol A → symbol B
symbol C → symbol D
symbol E → symbol F

遠景では:
package X → package Y  dependencies: 3
```

これで「全容」と「深掘り」が両立します。

今のCI結果の失敗は、**1枚の静的な面で抽象度を解決しようとしたこと**です。  
それだと、見えるものを固定するしかない。  
treeの良さである「制限」は得られるが、地図の良さである「移動しながら全容を保つ」は得られない。

なので次に作るべきものは、rendererではなくこれです。

| 作るもの | 役割 |
|---|---|
| `repoMap.world.v1.jsonl` | containment + dependency のtyped graph |
| `repoMap.lod.v1` | zごとの表示粒度ルール |
| `repoMap.projection.v1` | z/camera/focusからA2UI用viewへ畳む |
| `layoutAdapter.treemap.v1` | 暫定配置 |
| `layoutAdapter.voronoi.v1` | 将来配置 |
| `relationOverlay.v1` | 依存線の集約・展開 |
| `cameraState` | scrollで変わる一時状態。永続authorityではない |

A2UI/component registry はそのままでよいです。  
変えるべきは **A2UI契約ではなく、A2UIへ渡す前の projection** です。

最終判断：

**この世界一般では、semantic zoom / map-like graph / edge bundling という部品は存在する。  
でも “repo全体の構造 + 依存graph + CI証跡 + A2UI契約 + scroll-driven z drilldown” としては、ui.gitでは未解決。**

最も理想的な方向は、  
**静的Atlasを捨てるのではなく、Atlasを `world model → LOD projection → A2UI render` に昇格させること**です。"}

{"body":"## Purpose

Evaluate and, if accepted, implement `svg-pan-zoom` as a thin camera adapter for the repo map UI.

This issue is separate from #112 because #112 defines the ideal no-external-library implementation target. This issue tests a narrower alternative:

> Keep our own headless core, world model, LOD reducer, projection, and coordinate-preserving SVG renderer, but outsource only pan / zoom / fit camera behavior to `svg-pan-zoom`.

## Context

Current working invariant:

```text
repo = packages[]
package = models[]
```

The UI must preserve this containment visually:

```text
repo rect
  package rect[]
    model rect[]
```

Expected map-like semantic zoom:

```text
far:
  repos visible

zoom in:
  packages become visible inside repos

zoom in further:
  models become visible inside packages

zoom out:
  detail disappears while global context remains
```

This is not time-based animation. It is input-synchronous camera state and LOD projection.

## Required architecture

```text
JSONL data
  ↓
CRUD event contract
  ↓
model graph reducer
  ↓
projection / LOD reducer
  ↓
coordinate-preserving SVG renderer
  ↓
svg-pan-zoom camera adapter
```

## Hard boundaries

`svg-pan-zoom` may own only camera behavior:

- pan
- zoom
- fit
- wheel handling
- basic touch/pointer behavior if supported

`svg-pan-zoom` must not own:

- repo/package/model semantics
- containment model
- dependency model
- LOD rules
- font policy
- projection rules
- generated artifact authority
- state store

## Data boundary

Input data remains JSONL or generated projection data.

JSONL is an adapter input, not a renderer requirement.

Minimum model:

```jsonl
{"kind":"repoMap.node.v1","id":"repo:a","role":"repo","label":"a.git"}
{"kind":"repoMap.node.v1","id":"pkg:a/core","role":"package","parent":"repo:a","label":"core"}
{"kind":"repoMap.node.v1","id":"model:a/core/user","role":"model","parent":"pkg:a/core","label":"user.v1"}
{"kind":"repoMap.edge.v1","from":"model:a/core/user","to":"model:b/api/user","kind":"depends_on"}
```

## Required visual behavior

### z=far

- repo rectangles are visible.
- package/model labels are not falsely shown.
- map is not empty.
- global context is preserved.

### z=middle

- selected/focused repo remains visible.
- packages inside that repo become visible.
- package rectangles are visibly contained inside repo rectangle.
- unrelated edges are not shown.

### z=near

- selected/focused package remains visible.
- models inside that package become visible.
- model rectangles are visibly contained inside package rectangle.
- label size remains screen-stable.
- SVG text must not grow huge because of zoom transform.

### zoom out

- models disappear before packages.
- packages disappear before repo overview.
- context remains map-like.

## Font policy

Font must be screen-stable.

Allowed:

```text
font-size = policy × z × depth × inverseZoom
```

or equivalent screen-space label overlay.

Forbidden:

```text
font inside zoomed SVG group scales freely with geometry
```

Regression example to prevent:

```text
model label such as "m01" becomes huge after zoom
```

## Edge policy

- Do not show all edges all the time.
- Far view may show aggregate repo/package edges only.
- Near view may show selected-neighborhood model edges.
- Edges must connect visible geometry meaningfully.
- Offscreen or misleading long edges must be culled.
- Edge labels must be hidden unless they add meaning.

## Product UI policy

Product UI must not include debug-only controls.

Allowed product controls:

- `-`
- `+`
- `fit`

Forbidden in product UI:

- repo button row
- z debug text
- HUD
- count-only debug panel
- fake green status
- visual test-only switches

Debug/test API may remain hidden for E2E.

## Mobile requirements

Mobile must be checked visually, not only by counts.

Required:

- no horizontal overflow
- initial view is useful
- no large dead blank region
- zoom controls are tappable
- package/model visibility is preserved at tested z levels
- labels are not clipped or huge

## E2E requirements

E2E must not be count-only.

Required DOM geometry gates:

- package rect is inside repo rect at middle z.
- model rect is inside package rect at near z.
- visible labels are inside or near their target.
- labels are not taller than target by an invalid ratio.
- product UI has no debug row / HUD / z text.

Required visual gates:

```text
desktop:
  z=0
  z=middle
  z=near

mobile:
  z=0

{"body":"## Purpose

Evaluate and, if accepted, implement `svg-pan-zoom` as a thin camera adapter for the repo map UI.

This issue is separate from #112 because #112 defines the ideal no-external-library implementation target. This issue tests a narrower alternative:

> Keep our own headless core, world model, LOD reducer, projection, and coordinate-preserving SVG renderer, but outsource only pan / zoom / fit camera behavior to `svg-pan-zoom`.

## Context

Current working invariant:

```text
repo = packages[]
package = models[]
```

The UI must preserve this containment visually:

```text
repo rect
  package rect[]
    model rect[]
```

Expected map-like semantic zoom:

```text
far:
  repos visible

zoom in:
  packages become visible inside repos

zoom in further:
  models become visible inside packages

zoom out:
  detail disappears while global context remains
```

This is not time-based animation. It is input-synchronous camera state and LOD projection.

## Required architecture

```text
JSONL data
  ↓
CRUD event contract
  ↓
model graph reducer
  ↓
projection / LOD reducer
  ↓
coordinate-preserving SVG renderer
  ↓
svg-pan-zoom camera adapter
```

## Hard boundaries

`svg-pan-zoom` may own only camera behavior:

- pan
- zoom
- fit
- wheel handling
- basic touch/pointer behavior if supported

`svg-pan-zoom` must not own:

- repo/package/model semantics
- containment model
- dependency model
- LOD rules
- font policy
- projection rules
- generated artifact authority
- state store

## Data boundary

Input data remains JSONL or generated projection data.

JSONL is an adapter input, not a renderer requirement.

Minimum model:

```jsonl
{"kind":"repoMap.node.v1","id":"repo:a","role":"repo","label":"a.git"}
{"kind":"repoMap.node.v1","id":"pkg:a/core","role":"package","parent":"repo:a","label":"core"}
{"kind":"repoMap.node.v1","id":"model:a/core/user","role":"model","parent":"pkg:a/core","label":"user.v1"}
{"kind":"repoMap.edge.v1","from":"model:a/core/user","to":"model:b/api/user","kind":"depends_on"}
```

## Required visual behavior

### z=far

- repo rectangles are visible.
- package/model labels are not falsely shown.
- map is not empty.
- global context is preserved.

### z=middle

- selected/focused repo remains visible.
- packages inside that repo become visible.
- package rectangles are visibly contained inside repo rectangle.
- unrelated edges are not shown.

### z=near

- selected/focused package remains visible.
- models inside that package become visible.
- model rectangles are visibly contained inside package rectangle.
- label size remains screen-stable.
- SVG text must not grow huge because of zoom transform.

### zoom out

- models disappear before packages.
- packages disappear before repo overview.
- context remains map-like.

## Font policy

Font must be screen-stable.

Allowed:

```text
font-size = policy × z × depth × inverseZoom
```

or equivalent screen-space label overlay.

Forbidden:

```text
font inside zoomed SVG group scales freely with geometry
```

Regression example to prevent:

```text
model label such as "m01" becomes huge after zoom
```

## Edge policy

- Do not show all edges all the time.
- Far view may show aggregate repo/package edges only.
- Near view may show selected-neighborhood model edges.
- Edges must connect visible geometry meaningfully.
- Offscreen or misleading long edges must be culled.
- Edge labels must be hidden unless they add meaning.

## Product UI policy

Product UI must not include debug-only controls.

Allowed product controls:

- `-`
- `+`
- `fit`

Forbidden in product UI:

- repo button row
- z debug text
- HUD
- count-only debug panel
- fake green status
- visual test-only switches

Debug/test API may remain hidden for E2E.

## Mobile requirements

Mobile must be checked visually, not only by counts.

Required:

- no horizontal overflow
- initial view is useful
- no large dead blank region
- zoom controls are tappable
- package/model visibility is preserved at tested z levels
- labels are not clipped or huge

## E2E requirements

E2E must not be count-only.

Required DOM geometry gates:

- package rect is inside repo rect at middle z.
- model rect is inside package rect at near z.
- visible labels are inside or near their target.
- labels are not taller than target by an invalid ratio.
- product UI has no debug row / HUD / z text.

Required visual gates:

```text
desktop:
  z=0
  z=middle
  z=near

mobile:
  z=0
  z=middle
  z=near
```

A test is not PASS unless the screenshot is visually acceptable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New code keeps `repo = packages[]` and `package = models[]` documented in README.
- [ ] JSONL adapter remains separate from reducer.
- [ ] model graph reducer is renderer-independent.
- [ ] projection / LOD reducer is renderer-independent.
- [ ] `svg-pan-zoom` is isolated to camera adapter.
- [ ] coordinate-preserving SVG renderer remains the main renderer.
- [ ] z controls package/model visibility.
- [ ] labels are screen-stable under zoom.
- [ ] product UI contains only `-`, `+`, `fit`.
- [ ] no debug HUD / repo button row / z text in product UI.
- [ ] desktop E2E passes with geometry + screenshot evidence.
- [ ] mobile E2E passes with geometry + screenshot evidence.
- [ ] generated standalone HTML exists.
- [ ] generated artifact is evidence only, not authority.
- [ ] CI can build standalone HTML and E2E report.
- [ ] No G6, MSAGL, tldraw, map library, or additional renderer is introduced.

## Non-scope

- No G6 retry.
- No MSAGL retry.
- No tldraw spike.
- No Canvas/WebGL migration.
- No map tile library.
- No generic diagram editor.
- No time-based animation.
- No new state store.
- No generated artifact authority.
- No broad A2UI rewrite.

## Merge condition

Merge only if the implementation proves:

```text
repo = packages[]
package = models[]
```

visually, across zoom levels, on desktop and mobile.

Count-based PASS is not enough.

## Merge-blocking conditions

- package/model records exist but are not visually contained.
- label size explodes under zoom.
- debug UI leaks into product UI.
- mobile screenshot has large blank or clipped map state.
- E2E checks only counts.
- `svg-pan-zoom` owns semantics or projection.
- more than one renderer library is introduced.
- generated HTML is described as source authority.

## Final decision requested

Accept `svg-pan-zoom` only as a camera adapter.

Reject it if it cannot preserve:

```text
headless core
  + coordinate-preserving SVG renderer
  + semantic LOD projection
  + repo/package/model containment
```"}

body: This issue is complete only if its output contributes to selected real package `closure-pass`.
`handoff-ready`, `report-generated`, artifact output, drift rows, and work-order rows are not pass.
Demote old check surfaces so only the final gate remains as merge authority while useful tests continue as producers, artifacts, selftests, or internal steps.
- old final-looking check names no longer act as independent merge signals.
- useful validations are preserved under non-authority roles.
- there is no gap where neither old checks nor final gate protect the repo.
- `oldCiAudit`: no final-looking old required check remains.
- `oldCiDemotionDigest`: mapping from old check to retained role.
- `branchProtectionAudit`: required check path is final gate only.
Do not merge child PRs when:
- final gate cutover is not complete.
- useful validations are removed without replacement role.
- old checks still look like final pass surfaces.
- validation output showing final gate remains available.
- PR comment listing each old check and its final role.
This issue changes CI surface classification. It must not weaken final gate enforcement.

body: Close the remaining product-path gap between explicit Vim acceptance and worker execution.
The installed environment must not require an operator to run a separate one-shot worker command after every `:HqSubmit`.
-> managed hq-worker observes and claims intent
This issue defines the hq-owned worker lifecycle and recovery semantics. Windows installation, activation, and host supervision of that lifecycle remain envs responsibilities.
| Scope | Remove the manual `hq-worker` / `hq run --once` step after submit. |
| Product | Make the installed Vim-to-hq path operate after one environment apply and normal Vim use. |
| Architecture | Keep worker processing semantics in hq and target-host process activation in envs. |
| Quality | Prevent duplicate concurrent claims and false-green recovery after crashes. |
| Operations | Provide start, stop, health, restart, and durable recovery behavior. |
| Transferability | Replace operator-only worker startup knowledge with an explicit contract. |
| meta^10 | Reduce hidden runtime dependencies, intervention cost, and handoff risk. |
| `hq` | worker loop, claim/lease protocol, lifecycle command contract, shutdown behavior, recovery decisions, canonical evidence |
| `envs` | install exact hq artifact, declare/activate the managed worker process, host startup/restart supervision, health verification |
| `ops` | cross-repo CI and evidence that no manual worker command is used |
`envs` must not reinterpret queue meaning or write hq result evidence. `hq` must not own machine-specific Windows service/scheduled-task layout.
Provide a long-running worker surface equivalent to:
hq-worker stop     # only if an explicit control channel is adopted
The exact command names may differ, but the official artifact must expose:
- restart-safe recovery from canonical durable evidence;
A manual one-shot mode may remain for diagnostics/tests, but it must not be the installed product path.
- One canonical intent/run has at most one active worker claim at a time.
- Claims carry a worker identity, attempt identity, acquisition time, and bounded lease/heartbeat semantics.
- A worker cannot execute before its claim and required policy/provider checks are durably associated with the canonical run.
- Restart reconstructs state from canonical instruction/result evidence, not in-memory state.
- Completed or terminal runs are never executed again by normal recovery.
- Two explicit submits of identical text remain two distinct canonical intents/runs.
- Worker shutdown stops new claims and allows an in-flight attempt to finish or become explicitly recoverable.
- Unknown, malformed, stale, or conflicting claim state fails closed.
## Crash semantics and the exactly-once boundary
Do not claim unconditional exactly-once external side effects.
There is an unavoidable ambiguity window when a process crashes after an external provider performs an effect but before the corresponding durable `result.v1` is recorded.
| before claim | another healthy worker may claim normally |
| after claim, before invocation is durably marked | expired claim may be recovered according to the canonical lease rule |
| after durable invocation-start, before provider effect | resume only when the adapter contract proves it is safe |

| after provider may have effected, before durable result | do **not** blindly re-execute; emit/block as `reconcile_required` or equivalent typed non-green evidence unless the provider supports an idempotency token |
| after terminal durable result | never re-execute normally |
Exactly-once semantic execution may be claimed only for providers that support a verified idempotency key/deduplication contract covering the ambiguity window.
For providers without that contract, the required guarantee is:
> no concurrent duplicate execution, no automatic duplicate after an ambiguous crash, and no false completed result.
The long-running worker may use bounded polling, filesystem notification plus rescan, or another deterministic local mechanism.
- no intent is permanently missed because a notification was lost;
- restart performs a complete canonical rescan/reduction;
- malformed rows cannot block later valid rows without typed evidence;
- only canonical accepted/mapped intent is eligible for processing.
Do not add a general message broker or database unless a demonstrated requirement cannot be met by the existing append-only evidence model.
Machine-readable health must distinguish at least:
A running process alone is not sufficient proof of readiness.
- `:HqSubmit` E2E passing only because CI manually invokes a one-shot worker;
- two workers concurrently executing the same canonical run;
- a stale lease being treated as proof that no provider effect occurred;
- automatic re-execution across an ambiguous provider-effect crash window;
- process existence being treated as worker readiness;
- worker startup through arbitrary shell or PowerShell text;
- a second private queue/result lifecycle for the managed loop;
- envs process receipts substituting for hq `result.v1`.
- a diagnostic one-shot worker mode outside the installed default path;
- clean restart after no provider invocation occurred;
- recovery through verified provider idempotency keys;
- multiple worker binaries installed while only one deployment binding is active;
- two explicit identical submits as distinct runs;
- offline operation using the verified local envs deployment and canonical evidence.
- lease expiry and safe claim recovery;
- ambiguous post-effect crash becomes typed reconciliation state, not automatic retry;
- idempotent provider token permits safe retry only when its contract is verified.
- worker begins processing without a per-submit manual command;
- forced termination and restart recover safe cases;
- a second worker cannot duplicate an active run;
- health reports readiness and failure causes accurately;
- no shell is used to start providers.
After `envs apply` has activated the environment:
The proof must also restart/terminate the managed worker at each relevant lifecycle boundary and verify the recovery matrix above.
- The installed product path requires no manual worker command after `:HqSubmit`.
- hq exposes a supported managed worker mode and machine-readable health contract.
- start, graceful stop, forced restart, single-claim behavior, and durable recovery are mechanically tested.
- ambiguous crash windows fail closed instead of silently duplicating an external effect.
- provider-specific exactly-once claims require and prove an idempotency contract.
- envs can activate/supervise the worker without owning hq processing semantics.
- `ops#85` proves the full path without directly invoking a one-shot worker after submit.
- Do not add a distributed scheduler.
- Do not add a general message broker or database.
- Do not claim unconditional exactly-once external side effects.
- Do not move provider execution into envs.
- Do not make Vim supervise the worker.
- Do not require a remote hq service.
- Do not add arbitrary shell-based service definitions.

{"body":"## Purpose

Close the remaining product-path gap between explicit Vim acceptance and worker execution.

The installed environment must not require an operator to run a separate one-shot worker command after every `:HqSubmit`.

Required user-visible path:

```text
:HqSubmit
  -> canonical accepted.instruction
  -> managed hq-worker observes and claims intent
  -> canonical instruction.v1 processing
  -> provider execution
  -> result.v1
  -> session.v1 projection
```

This issue defines the hq-owned worker lifecycle and recovery semantics. Windows installation, activation, and host supervision of that lifecycle remain envs responsibilities.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Remove the manual `hq-worker` / `hq run --once` step after submit. |
| Product | Make the installed Vim-to-hq path operate after one environment apply and normal Vim use. |
| Architecture | Keep worker processing semantics in hq and target-host process activation in envs. |
| Quality | Prevent duplicate concurrent claims and false-green recovery after crashes. |
| Operations | Provide start, stop, health, restart, and durable recovery behavior. |
| Transferability | Replace operator-only worker startup knowledge with an explicit contract. |
| meta^10 | Reduce hidden runtime dependencies, intervention cost, and handoff risk. |

## Depends on

- Canonical architecture: `hq#95`
- Canonical LSP/acceptance path: `hq#96`
- Worker/provider execution path: `hq#97`
- Nix-compiled environment plan: `roccho-dev/envs#4`
- Windows realization agent: `roccho-dev/envs#5`
- Cross-repo proof: `roccho-dev/ops#85`

## Ownership boundary

| Owner | Owns |
|---|---|
| `hq` | worker loop, claim/lease protocol, lifecycle command contract, shutdown behavior, recovery decisions, canonical evidence |
| `envs` | install exact hq artifact, declare/activate the managed worker process, host startup/restart supervision, health verification |
| `ops` | cross-repo CI and evidence that no manual worker command is used |
| `edits` | explicit human submit only |

`envs` must not reinterpret queue meaning or write hq result evidence. `hq` must not own machine-specific Windows service/scheduled-task layout.

## Minimal command/runtime contract

Provide a long-running worker surface equivalent to:

```text
hq-worker serve --profile <name>
hq-worker health --profile <name>
hq-worker stop     # only if an explicit control channel is adopted
```

The exact command names may differ, but the official artifact must expose:

- a managed long-running processing mode;
- deterministic readiness/health output;
- graceful shutdown;
- restart-safe recovery from canonical durable evidence;
- no shell requirement;
- no ambient path/config fallback.

A manual one-shot mode may remain for diagnostics/tests, but it must not be the installed product path.

## Claim and processing invariants

- One canonical intent/run has at most one active worker claim at a time.
- Claims carry a worker identity, attempt identity, acquisition time, and bounded lease/heartbeat semantics.
- A worker cannot execute before its claim and required policy/provider checks are durably associated with the canonical run.
- Restart reconstructs state from canonical instruction/result evidence, not in-memory state.
- Completed or terminal runs are never executed again by normal recovery.
- Two explicit submits of identical text remain two distinct canonical intents/runs.
- Worker shutdown stops new claims and allows an in-flight attempt to finish or become explicitly recoverable.
- Unknown, malformed, stale, or conflicting claim state fails closed.

## Crash semantics and the exactly-once boundary

Do not claim unconditional exactly-once external side effects.

There is an unavoidable ambiguity window when a process crashes after an external provider performs an effect but before the corresponding durable `result.v1` is recorded.

Required behavior:

| Crash point | Recovery |
|---|---|
| before claim | another healthy worker may claim normally |
| after claim, before invocation is durably marked | expired claim may be recovered according to the canonical lease rule |
| after durable invocation-start, before provider effect | resume only when the adapter contract proves it is safe |
| after provider may have effected, before durable result | do **not** blindly re-execute; emit/block as `reconcile_required` or equivalent typed non-green evidence unless the provider supports an idempotency token |
| after terminal durable result | never re-execute normally |

Exactly-once semantic execution may be claimed only for providers that support a verified idempotency key/deduplication contract covering the ambiguity window.

For providers without that contract, the required guarantee is:

> no concurrent duplicate execution, no automatic duplicate after an ambiguous crash, and no false completed result.

## Worker observation

The long-running worker may use bounded polling, filesystem notification plus rescan, or another deterministic local mechanism.

The implementation must guarantee:

- no intent is permanently missed because a notification was lost;
- observation does not change authority;
- restart performs a complete canonical rescan/reduction;
- idle operation is bounded;
- malformed rows cannot block later valid rows without typed evidence;
- only canonical accepted/mapped intent is eligible for processing.

Do not add a general message broker or database unless a demonstrated requirement cannot be met by the existing append-only evidence model.

## Health contract

Machine-readable health must distinguish at least:

- configured and ready;
- not configured;
- source/profile unavailable;
- evidence invalid;
- provider/capability unavailable;
- worker already active;
- worker stale/unhealthy;
- reconciliation required.

A running process alone is not sufficient proof of readiness.

## False-positive exclusions

Reject/prove impossible:

- `:HqSubmit` E2E passing only because CI manually invokes a one-shot worker;
- two workers concurrently executing the same canonical run;
- a stale lease being treated as proof that no provider effect occurred;
- automatic re-execution across an ambiguous provider-effect crash window;
- process existence being treated as worker readiness;
- worker startup through arbitrary shell or PowerShell text;
- a second private queue/result lifecycle for the managed loop;
- recovery fabricating a completed result;
- envs process receipts substituting for hq `result.v1`.

## False-negative exclusions

Accept/preserve:

- a diagnostic one-shot worker mode outside the installed default path;
- clean restart after no provider invocation occurred;
- recovery through verified provider idempotency keys;
- multiple worker binaries installed while only one deployment binding is active;
- two explicit identical submits as distinct runs;
- offline operation using the verified local envs deployment and canonical evidence.

## Required tests

### Pure lifecycle tests

- start/ready/shutdown state transitions;
- single active claim;
- lease expiry and safe claim recovery;
- terminal run suppression;
- repeated explicit intents remain separate;
- restart reduction from durable evidence;
- malformed/conflicting claim evidence fails closed;
- ambiguous post-effect crash becomes typed reconciliation state, not automatic retry;
- idempotent provider token permits safe retry only when its contract is verified.

### Process integration tests

- worker begins processing without a per-submit manual command;
- graceful shutdown stops new claims;
- forced termination and restart recover safe cases;
- a second worker cannot duplicate an active run;
- health reports readiness and failure causes accurately;
- no shell is used to start providers.

### Installed Windows E2E

After `envs apply` has activated the environment:

```text
open Vim
  -> :HqStart
  -> :HqSubmit
  -> no separate worker command
  -> provider effect or typed failure
  -> canonical result.v1
```

The proof must also restart/terminate the managed worker at each relevant lifecycle boundary and verify the recovery matrix above.

## Done

- The installed product path requires no manual worker command after `:HqSubmit`.
- hq exposes a supported managed worker mode and machine-readable health contract.
- start, graceful stop, forced restart, single-claim behavior, and durable recovery are mechanically tested.
- ambiguous crash windows fail closed instead of silently duplicating an external effect.
- provider-specific exactly-once claims require and prove an idempotency contract.
- envs can activate/supervise the worker without owning hq processing semantics.
- `ops#85` proves the full path without directly invoking a one-shot worker after submit.
- implementation PRs reference `hq#95/#96/#97`, `envs#4/#5`, `ops#85`, and `adrs#203`.

## Non-goals

- Do not add a distributed scheduler.
- Do not add a general message broker or database.
- Do not claim unconditional exactly-once external side effects.
- Do not move provider execution into envs.
- Do not make Vim supervise the worker.
- Do not require a remote hq service.
- Do not add arbitrary shell-based service definitions."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Close the remaining product-path gap between explicit Vim acceptance and worker execution.

The installed environment must not require an operator to run a separate one-shot worker command after every `:HqSubmit`.

Required user-visible path:

```text
:HqSubmit
  -> canonical accepted.instruction
  -> managed hq-worker observes and claims intent
  -> canonical instruction.v1 processing
  -> provider execution
  -> result.v1
  -> session.v1 projection
```

This issue defines the hq-owned worker lifecycle and recovery semantics. Windows installation, activation, and host supervision of that lifecycle remain envs responsibilities.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Remove the manual `hq-worker` / `hq run --once` step after submit. |
| Product | Make the installed Vim-to-hq path operate after one environment apply and normal Vim use. |
| Architecture | Keep worker processing semantics in hq and target-host process activation in envs. |
| Quality | Prevent duplicate concurrent claims and false-green recovery after crashes. |
| Operations | Provide start, stop, health, restart, and durable recovery behavior. |
| Transferability | Replace operator-only worker startup knowledge with an explicit contract. |
| meta^10 | Reduce hidden runtime dependencies, intervention cost, and handoff risk. |

## Depends on

- Canonical architecture: `hq#95`
- Canonical LSP/acceptance path: `hq#96`
- Worker/provider execution path: `hq#97`
- Nix-compiled environment plan: `roccho-dev/envs#4`
- Windows realization agent: `roccho-dev/envs#5`
- Cross-repo proof: `roccho-dev/ops#85`

## Ownership boundary

| Owner | Owns |
|---|---|
| `hq` | worker loop, claim/lease protocol, lifecycle command contract, shutdown behavior, recovery decisions, canonical evidence |
| `envs` | install exact hq artifact, declare/activate the managed worker process, host startup/restart supervision, health verification |
| `ops` | cross-repo CI and evidence that no manual worker command is used |
| `edits` | explicit human submit only |

`envs` must not reinterpret queue meaning or write hq result evidence. `hq` must not own machine-specific Windows service/scheduled-task layout.

## Minimal command/runtime contract

Provide a long-running worker surface equivalent to:

```text
hq-worker serve --profile <name>
hq-worker health --profile <name>
hq-worker stop     # only if an explicit control channel is adopted
```

The exact command names may differ, but the official artifact must expose:

- a managed long-running processing mode;
- deterministic readiness/health output;
- graceful shutdown;
- restart-safe recovery from canonical durable evidence;
- no shell requirement;
- no ambient path/config fallback.

A manual one-shot mode may remain for diagnostics/tests, but it must not be the installed product path.

## Claim and processing invariants

- One canonical intent/run has at most one active worker claim at a time.
- Claims carry a worker identity, attempt identity, acquisition time, and bounded lease/heartbeat semantics.
- A worker cannot execute before its claim and required policy/provider checks are durably associated with the canonical run.
- Restart reconstructs state from canonical instruction/result evidence, not in-memory state.
- Completed or terminal runs are never executed again by normal recovery.
- Two explicit submits of identical text remain two distinct canonical intents/runs.
- Worker shutdown stops new claims and allows an in-flight attempt to finish or become explicitly recoverable.
- Unknown, malformed, stale, or conflicting claim state fails closed.

## Crash semantics and the exactly-once boundary

Do not claim unconditional exactly-once external side effects.

There is an unavoidable ambiguity window when a process crashes after an external provider performs an effect but before the corresponding durable `result.v1` is recorded.

Required behavior:

| Crash point | Recovery |
|---|---|
| before claim | another healthy worker may claim normally |
| after claim, before invocation is durably marked | expired claim may be recovered according to the canonical lease rule |
| after durable invocation-start, before provider effect | resume only when the adapter contract proves it is safe |
| after provider may have effected, before durable result | do **not** blindly re-execute; emit/block as `reconcile_required` or equivalent typed non-green evidence unless the provider supports an idempotency token |
| after terminal durable result | never re-execute normally |

Exactly-once semantic execution may be claimed only for providers that support a verified idempotency key/deduplication contract covering the ambiguity window.

For providers without that contract, the required guarantee is:

> no concurrent duplicate execution, no automatic duplicate after an ambiguous crash, and no false completed result.

## Worker observation

The long-running worker may use bounded polling, filesystem notification plus rescan, or another deterministic local mechanism.

The implementation must guarantee:

- no intent is permanently missed because a notification was lost;
- observation does not change authority;
- restart performs a complete canonical rescan/reduction;
- idle operation is bounded;
- malformed rows cannot block later valid rows without typed evidence;
- only canonical accepted/mapped intent is eligible for processing.

Do not add a general message broker or database unless a demonstrated requirement cannot be met by the existing append-only evidence model.

## Health contract

Machine-readable health must distinguish at least:

- configured and ready;
- not configured;
- source/profile unavailable;
- evidence invalid;
- provider/capability unavailable;
- worker already active;
- worker stale/unhealthy;
- reconciliation required.

A running process alone is not sufficient proof of readiness.

## False-positive exclusions

Reject/prove impossible:

- `:HqSubmit` E2E passing only because CI manually invokes a one-shot worker;
- two workers concurrently executing the same canonical run;
- a stale lease being treated as proof that no provider effect occurred;
- automatic re-execution across an ambiguous provider-effect crash window;
- process existence being treated as worker readiness;
- worker startup through arbitrary shell or PowerShell text;
- a second private queue/result lifecycle for the managed loop;
- recovery fabricating a completed result;
- envs process receipts substituting for hq `result.v1`.

## False-negative exclusions

Accept/preserve:

- a diagnostic one-shot worker mode outside the installed default path;
- clean restart after no provider invocation occurred;
- recovery through verified provider idempotency keys;
- multiple worker binaries installed while only one deployment binding is active;
- two explicit identical submits as distinct runs;
- offline operation using the verified local envs deployment and canonical evidence.

## Required tests

### Pure lifecycle tests

- start/ready/shutdown state transitions;
- single active claim;
- lease expiry and safe claim recovery;
- terminal run suppression;
- repeated explicit intents remain separate;
- restart reduction from durable evidence;
- malformed/conflicting claim evidence fails closed;
- ambiguous post-effect crash becomes typed reconciliation state, not automatic retry;
- idempotent provider token permits safe retry only when its contract is verified.

### Process integration tests

- worker begins processing without a per-submit manual command;
- graceful shutdown stops new claims;
- forced termination and restart recover safe cases;
- a second worker cannot duplicate an active run;
- health reports readiness and failure causes accurately;
- no shell is used to start providers.

### Installed Windows E2E

After `envs apply` has activated the environment:

```text
open Vim
  -> :HqStart
  -> :HqSubmit
  -> no separate worker command
  -> provider effect or typed failure
  -> canonical result.v1
```

The proof must also restart/terminate the managed worker at each relevant lifecycle boundary and verify the recovery matrix above.

## Done

- The installed product path requires no manual worker command after `:HqSubmit`.
- hq exposes a supported managed worker mode and machine-readable health contract.
- start, graceful stop, forced restart, single-claim behavior, and durable recovery are mechanically tested.
- ambiguous crash windows fail closed instead of silently duplicating an external effect.
- provider-specific exactly-once claims require and prove an idempotency contract.
- envs can activate/supervise the worker without owning hq processing semantics.
- `ops#85` proves the full path without directly invoking a one-shot worker after submit.
- implementation PRs reference `hq#95/#96/#97`, `envs#4/#5`, `ops#85`, and `adrs#203`.

## Non-goals

- Do not add a distributed scheduler.
- Do not add a general message broker or database.
- Do not claim unconditional exactly-once external side effects.
- Do not move provider execution into envs.
- Do not make Vim supervise the worker.
- Do not require a remote hq service.
- Do not add arbitrary shell-based service definitions."}
