{"body":"### Describe the bug

`clang` from `llvmPackages_21` (21.1.8) on `x86_64-linux` emits ELF relocatable objects in which some `STT_SECTION` symbols have `st_shndx = SHN_UNDEF`. Relocations that go through those section symbols then fail to link with lld, which prints the nameless section symbol as an empty undefined symbol:

```
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: 
>>> referenced by obj.c:208 (aws-lc/crypto/obj/obj.c:208)
>>>               7ac4c9359514b807-obj.o:(aws_lc_0_46_0_OBJ_sn2nid) in archive .../libaws_lc_sys-b474c0aa794f516b.rlib
```

`llvm-readelf -W -s` on the object (`aws-lc/crypto/obj/obj.c` from the `aws-lc-sys` 0.46.0 crate, 53 section symbols, 12 of them undefined, interleaved with the healthy `.text.*`/`.bss.*`/`.rodata.*` ones):

```
    44: 0000000000000000     0 SECTION LOCAL  DEFAULT    29 .text.create_object_with_text_oid
    45: 0000000000000000     0 SECTION LOCAL  DEFAULT   UND <?>
    46: 0000000000000000     0 SECTION LOCAL  DEFAULT    33 .text.aws_lc_0_46_0_OBJ_create
    47: 0000000000000000     0 SECTION LOCAL  DEFAULT    35 .text.obj_next_nid
    48: 0000000000000000     0 SECTION LOCAL  DEFAULT   UND <?>
    ... (45, 48, 51, 54, 57, 60, 63, 66, 69, 72, 76, 79 are UND)
llvm-readelf: warning: unable to get section index for symbol with st_shndx = 0x0 (SHN_UNDEF)
```

403 relocations reference those symbols: 336 from `.rela.debug_info`, 17 `.rela.debug_loc`, 14 `.rela.debug_ranges`, 5 `.rela.eh_frame`, 5 `.rela.debug_line`, and the ones in code that lld trips on, e.g. 10 in `.rela.text.aws_lc_0_46_0_OBJ_create`, 4 in `.rela.text.aws_lc_0_46_0_OBJ_sn2nid`, 4 in `.rela.text.aws_lc_0_46_0_OBJ_ln2nid`:

```
0000000000000028  0000004200000002 R_X86_64_PC32          0000000000000000 <?> - 4
000000000000005e  0000004200000002 R_X86_64_PC32          0000000000000000 <?> - 4
```

The same LLVM 21.1.8 from an earlier nixpkgs-unstable, Debian's clang 21.1.5, gcc 16.2 from the same nixpkgs revision, and the darwin `clang` of the same revision all emit a correct object for the same source and flags. `zig cc` (zig 0.16.0, which links nixpkgs' `libclang`) emits the same defect for `aarch64-linux` (2 of 53 section symbols undefined, 32 relocations against them, `R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21`/`R_AARCH64_ADD_ABS_LO12_NC` in `OBJ_create`/`OBJ_sn2nid`/`OBJ_obj2nid` and the `.debug_*` sections), so cross builds through zig are affected too.

```sh
bad=github:NixOS/nixpkgs/8edc0c72e3a38faf5434e40d1f19431125fe4b30
nix shell "$bad#llvmPackages_21.clang" "$bad#llvmPackages_21.llvm"
curl -sL https://static.crates.io/crates/aws-lc-sys/aws-lc-sys-0.46.0.crate | tar xz
d=$PWD/aws-lc-sys-0.46.0
clang -O3 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -fPIC -gdwarf-4 -fno-omit-frame-pointer -m64 \
  --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -std=c11 \
  -I"$d/generated-include" -I"$d/include" -I"$d/aws-lc/include" \
  -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter -pthread -ffile-prefix-map="$d=" \
  -D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700 -DBORINGSSL_IMPLEMENTATION=1 -DBORINGSSL_PREFIX=aws_lc_0_46_0 \
  -DAWS_LC_STDALIGN_AVAILABLE=1 -DAWS_LC_BUILTIN_SWAP_SUPPORTED=1 -DHAVE_LINUX_RANDOM_H=1 \
  -c "$d/aws-lc/crypto/obj/obj.c" -o obj.o
llvm-readelf -W -s obj.o | grep -c 'SECTION.*UND'
```

On the object the failing CI build produced this is 12 (of 53 section symbols). At the good revision (`b3da656039dc7a6240f27b2ef8cc6a3ef3bccae7` in place of the hash above) the build emits a clean object and the count is 0.

**Caveat: I have not managed to reproduce this standalone, and I only have a GitHub Actions runner to try it on.** In the one attempt I could make at the bad revision, in the same devenv shell the failing build runs in:

- the command above, minus `-D_XOPEN_SOURCE=700` and `-pthread` (my mistake), did not compile (`pthread_rwlock_t` undeclared), so the exact flag set went untested;
- `clang -O3 -fPIC -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -g` (DWARF 5 instead of 4), the same without `-g`, `-O3 -fPIC -g`, and `-O0 -fPIC -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -g` on the same `obj.c` each gave 0 undefined section symbols (of 51, 43, 14 and 66), once each;

I have kept the two broken objects (x86_64 and aarch64, 268 KB each, `.comment` = `clang version 21.1.8`) and can attach them here.

### Expected behavior

Every `STT_SECTION` symbol in the emitted object is defined (`st_shndx` is its section's index), so lld can resolve relocations against it.

### Additional context

- Good: nixpkgs-unstable b3da656039dc7a6240f27b2ef8cc6a3ef3bccae7 (2026-05-08) — `llvmPackages_21` 21.1.8 built with gcc 15.2.0, glibc 2.42.

- Between the two, `clang`, `lld`, `binutils` (2.46), `zig` (0.16.0) and the cc-wrapper hardening flag set are identical, and LLVM's source did not change; what changed is the compiler that builds LLVM (gcc 15.2 → 16.2) and glibc (2.42 → 2.44).
- This looks like the clang-side twin of #571232 (`lld_21` built with gcc 16 writes `STT_SECTION` symbols with `st_shndx = SHN_UNDEF` into `ld -r` output, same empty-name `undefined symbol` at the final link). That one was traced in ClangBuiltLinux/linux#2162 to lld zeroing `Symbol` storage with `memset` and then placement-`new`ing into it, which gcc 16's lifetime DSE (r16-3962-g12975b8aa2dc38) is entitled to drop — LLVM stopped passing `-fno-lifetime-dse` to its own build in llvm/llvm-project@e3ef26df85c3, and `-fno-lifetime-dse` was confirmed to avoid the lld bug. It was fixed by #568680 (backport of llvm/llvm-project#198129, merged to `staging` 2026-10-07; on `master`, not yet in the `nixpkgs-unstable` channel as of today). That patch only touches `lld/ELF/Symbols.h`/`InputFiles.cpp`, so it cannot reach this case: here the object comes straight out of `clang -c` (the `.a` member is byte-identical to the rlib member; no `ld -r` anywhere), so the uninitialised state would be in LLVM's MC/ELF object writer rather than in lld. Building `llvmPackages_21` with `-fno-lifetime-dse` under gcc 16 may be a cheap check of that theory.

- Found while bumping a devenv project (hephbuild/heph#502, bisected in hephbuild/heph#503–#507); the project holds its nixpkgs input at the good revision for now.

### Metadata

- system: `x86_64-linux` (and `aarch64-linux`, cross-compiled through `zig cc` 0.16.0, which links the same nixpkgs `libclang`)
- bad: nixpkgs-unstable `8edc0c72e3a38faf5434e40d1f19431125fe4b30` (2026-10-08) — `llvmPackages_21.clang` 21.1.8, LLVM built with gcc 16.2.0 against glibc 2.44 (`/nix/store/jmgw1yz3xm3bpgrk9r84jkcynskdbd40-clang-21.1.8`, wrapper `/nix/store/2msw5nclhpsm80z65dqmjiv8kkras989-clang-wrapper-21.1.8`, `glibc-2.44-25`, `gcc-16.2.0-lib`)

body: <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: n/a, Agent Host with the Copilot provider (bundled `@github/copilot-win32-x64` 1.0.84-4)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent Host chat, `create_session` tool (`relationship: "currentSession"`)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Claude Opus 5.5, reasoning effort xhigh, 1M context (`long_context`)

An agent that works through a list of tasks by starting one chat per task with `create_session` can choose each chat's model, but not its reasoning effort or context tier. The agent host already supports both per chat: `_createSession` reads them from `model.config.thinkingLevel` and `model.config.contextTier`, and users can set them in the model picker. The tool doesn't expose either.
Passing `model` also loses the caller's reasoning effort:
- Without `model`, `create_session` uses `getCreationDefaults(chat).model`, the calling chat's whole model selection, so the new chat gets the caller's effort and tier.
- With `model`, it sends only `{ id: model.id }`, so the new chat starts with no reasoning effort, which means the model's default.
`create_chat` goes through the same code, and `independent` sessions are also created with `model: { id }` only.
1. In an Agent Host chat, select Claude Opus 5.5 with reasoning effort xhigh and the 1M context.

2. Have the agent call `create_session` with `relationship: "currentSession"` and no `model`. The new chat's `session.start` has `"selectedModel":"claude-opus-5.5","reasoningEffort":"xhigh","contextTier":"long_context"`.
3. Have it call `create_session` again with `model: "claude-opus-5.5"`. The new chat's `session.start` has `"selectedModel":"claude-opus-5.5","contextTier":"long_context"` and no `reasoningEffort`.

body: <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not recorded; reproduced with the Copilot SDK agent-host experience.
- VS Code Version: Insiders; source investigation and fix based on main at 341e0fa9346520e7a6a09803a80c5ecd3027f3cb (1.143.0 development sources).
- OS Version: Windows (exact OS build not recorded).
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent-host chat with filesystem sandboxing enabled.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Reproduced with gpt-6-astra; the failure is in confirmation UI handling.
- Logs: Relevant runtime excerpts, with request identities omitted:
Rejecting invalid sandbox path grant response
1. Enable agent sandboxing and choose a directory outside the sandbox's writable paths.
2. Ask the agent to create a text file in that directory, for example a file in Downloads, with simple text content.
3. When the pending file-edit preview asks to add the path to user sandbox settings and retry, click Allow.
4. Compare with approving a read-access request: the read approval saves its sandbox setting successfully.
The explicit Allow choice saves the offered read/write grant to user sandbox settings and grants access for the pending SDK request, allowing the write to proceed inside the sandbox.

The write is rejected with `Permission denied by host policy`. The read/write settings update is not reached. The completion event contains `result.kind: denied-interactively-by-user` and `decisionSource: host_policy`, despite the user approving the prompt.

The edit-preview path in `stateToProgressAdapter.ts` supplies legacy `options: ['Allow']` to `ChatModifiedFilesConfirmationSubPart`. That component builds its buttons from these labels rather than `confirmationMessages.customOptions`, returning `selectedButton: 'Allow'` instead of the protocol ID `save-sandbox-path`.

`AgentHostSessionHandler` resolves the choice by option ID. The label does not match, so `selectedOptionId` is undefined and the settings-save branch is skipped. `CopilotAgentSession.respondToPermissionRequest` then correctly rejects an approval that did not explicitly select the sandbox-path grant action.

Read confirmations use the shared custom-option renderer and preserve the option ID. The write UI should do the same, retaining approval/denial IDs and kinds without weakening host sandbox validation.

body: (I suspect this also applies to Claude chat)
The CoPilot chat no longer shows diffs and lets me review and confirm (or skip) the modifications. I reallly want this back.
I've desperately tried to get it back but after more than 3 hours of conversations with Github Copilot it mentioned that this is no longer possible due to an upgrade of VS Code. WTF?
The diff / Keep / Undo feature seems to be still available in the inline chat, but that is not what I want; the inline chat does not show the 'thought process' steps.
In the chat window I saw this info popup:
This agent harness opens up new ways to work across windows and apps. Continue as usual, and let us know how it goes."
That will NOT get a thumbs up from me!

{"body":"
Summary

VS Code's context management for custom OpenAI-compatible models is currently very poor in long-running conversations, especially when multiple MCP servers, tools, and extensions are enabled.

I am using a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model through the OpenCode inference endpoint, configured through my model/provider setup. The model is declared in VS Code with the appropriate context-window, input-token, and output-token settings for the intended 1,000,000-token context configuration.

A fresh conversation initially works correctly. However, after using the model for some time, requests start failing with HTTP 400 "context_length_exceeded". This occurs even though the model's context-related fields are explicitly configured and the problem did not occur before I added several additional MCP servers and extensions.

Importantly, I can reproduce this with the Local Harness, so this does not appear to be limited to the Copilot Agent Host.

The current experience is extremely frustrating. VS Code's context budgeting, tool handling, and overflow prevention are not reliable enough for serious long-context agent workflows. The application should manage the context it constructs, account for its own instructions and registered tools, and avoid sending requests that exceed the effective context limit of the selected endpoint.

Environment

- VS Code: Latest Stable release at the time of reporting
- Harness: Local
- Model: "opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free"
- API endpoint observed in the error: "https://opencode.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions"
- API format: OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions
- Model configuration: Explicit context-window, input-token, and output-token limits
- Integrations: Multiple MCP servers and extensions, including official/maintained integrations using the supported VS Code and MCP interfaces

body: kin-openapi: Nil-pointer dereference panic in openapi3filter for OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas missing items

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From 0.136.0 until 0.143.0, openapi3filter accepts OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas without an items keyword and then dereferences the nil Schema.Items value while decoding application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data request bodies, response headers, and other array parameter surfaces. A remote unauthenticated client can reach an affected operation with a nonempty request or matching response and deterministically trigger a nil-pointer panic during ValidateRequest or ValidateResponse. OpenAPI 3.0 documents are not affected because document validation rejects arrays without items, and JSON request bodies use a different decoder path. This issue is fixed in version 0.143.0.

OpenJPH through 0.32.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write in HTJ2K Cleanup-Pass Decoder

OpenJPH through 0.32.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the HTJ2K cleanup-pass decoder that allows attackers to corrupt memory via one-row codeblocks. Attackers can supply a crafted .j2c or .jph codestream with small precinct sizes, causing the decoder to write a second row past the codeblock buffer, resulting in memory corruption and crashes.

- [VulnCheck Advisory: OpenJPH through 0.32.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write in HTJ2K Cleanup-Pass Decoder](https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/openjph-through-0.32.0-heap-out-of-bounds-write-in-htj2k-cleanup-pass-decoder) (`third-party-advisory`)

body: kin-openapi: Unauthenticated panic (DoS) in openapi3filter legacy router via non-canonical/unsupported HTTP method on a static path

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. Prior to 0.145.0, openapi3filter.ValidationHandler uses the routers/legacy router, which passes an unsupported or non-canonical HTTP method for an existing static path to openapi3.PathItem.GetOperation. The default branch of GetOperation panics before authentication runs, so an unauthenticated remote client can repeatedly send methods such as PROPFIND or lowercase get to abort connections and generate stack-trace log growth. The specific panic requires an exact static path; a concrete path matched only by a templated route does not reach the same sink. This issue is fixed in version 0.145.0.
kin-openapi: Incomplete Fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5: Three Unpatched nil-Items Panic Paths in openapi3filter

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From 0.136.0 until 0.149.0, three openapi3filter decoder paths that were missed by the fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 lack a nil-items guard for legal OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger a deterministic nil-pointer panic through an array query parameter, a deepObject query parameter containing an array property, or an application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body whose array property appears inside an allOf, anyOf, or oneOf subschema. The query and composed-body paths reach urlValuesDecoder.parseArray, while the deepObject path reaches buildResObj, and all pass a nil items schema into code that dereferences it. This issue is fixed in version 0.149.0.
kin-openapi deepObject query decoding repeatedly compiles an invariant regular expression

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From 0.145.0 until 0.146.0, openapi3filter repeatedly calls regexp.MustCompile for the same parameter-name regular expression inside the per-query-key loop in urlValuesDecoder.DecodeObject used to decode a deepObject query parameter. An unauthenticated remote client can send an affected endpoint a request containing many unrelated query keys, causing ValidateRequest to perform work and allocations proportional to the attacker-controlled key count for every deepObject parameter. The expression itself is fixed and this is not regular expression denial of service; the resource consumption comes from loop-invariant recompilation. This issue is fixed in version 0.146.0.
kin-openapi: Uncontrolled Recursion on Circular allOf/anyOf/oneOf Schemas Causes Fatal Process Crash

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. Prior to 0.149.0, runtime request, response, and direct schema validation lacks cycle detection when an allOf, anyOf, or oneOf chain refers back to an ancestor schema, even though loading and document validation accept the circular reference. A request or response that reaches the affected schema causes unbounded recursion in Schema.visitJSON or openapi3filter.decodeValue and exhausts the Go goroutine stack. The resulting fatal stack overflow cannot be caught with recover and terminates the entire process, including unrelated requests. This issue is fixed in version 0.149.0.
kin-openapi spec loader panics on a self-referential additionalProperties $ref (nil-pointer DoS)

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. Prior to 0.145.0, openapi3.Loader can dereference a nil SchemaRef.Value while resolving a self-referential additionalProperties JSON Reference such as a schema that points to its own additionalProperties member. Loading an attacker-controlled OpenAPI document through LoadFromData, LoadFromFile, or LoadFromURI reaches resolveComponent before document validation and can panic the loading process. Resolved additionalProperties schemas and ordinary recursive schemas do not take the vulnerable nil-value path. This issue is fixed in version 0.145.0.
kin-openapi: YAML NaN/Inf Values Bypass Built-in Guards and Panic via OAS 3.1 Validation Path

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. Prior to 0.148.0, the OpenAPI 3.1 validation path passes YAML NaN and infinity numeric values to santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema v6.0.2 without applying kin-openapi's existing finite-number guards. A remote unauthenticated client can send an application/yaml or application/x-yaml request body containing .nan, .inf, or -.inf to an operation with a numeric constraint, causing the dependency to create and dereference a nil big.Rat during ValidateRequest. Standard net/http servers recover the panic per connection, while other hosts or application goroutines may terminate the process. This issue is fixed in version 0.148.0.

kin-openapi openapi3filter: nil-pointer panic in ValidateResponse on a response header declared with content

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. Prior to 0.146.0, openapi3filter.ValidateResponse passes a nil response header schema to decodeValue when an OpenAPI document declares the header with content instead of schema. The document passes validation, but every response validation for the affected operation dereferences the nil schema and panics even when the response does not contain the declared header. Applications that ingest an untrusted specification can expose this as remote availability impact, while applications using only trusted local specifications still crash when the affected operation is exercised. This issue is fixed in version 0.146.0.

body: kin-openapi: Unauthenticated panic (DoS) in openapi3filter legacy router via non-canonical/unsupported HTTP method on a static path

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. Prior to 0.145.0, openapi3filter.ValidationHandler uses the routers/legacy router, which passes an unsupported or non-canonical HTTP method for an existing static path to openapi3.PathItem.GetOperation. The default branch of GetOperation panics before authentication runs, so an unauthenticated remote client can repeatedly send methods such as PROPFIND or lowercase get to abort connections and generate stack-trace log growth. The specific panic requires an exact static path; a concrete path matched only by a templated route does not reach the same sink. This issue is fixed in version 0.145.0.
kin-openapi: Incomplete Fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5: Three Unpatched nil-Items Panic Paths in openapi3filter

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From 0.136.0 until 0.149.0, three openapi3filter decoder paths that were missed by the fix for GHSA-p6wj-qrr4-pgh5 lack a nil-items guard for legal OpenAPI 3.1 array schemas. An unauthenticated remote client can trigger a deterministic nil-pointer panic through an array query parameter, a deepObject query parameter containing an array property, or an application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body whose array property appears inside an allOf, anyOf, or oneOf subschema. The query and composed-body paths reach urlValuesDecoder.parseArray, while the deepObject path reaches buildResObj, and all pass a nil items schema into code that dereferences it. This issue is fixed in version 0.149.0.
kin-openapi deepObject query decoding repeatedly compiles an invariant regular expression

kin-openapi is a Go project for handling OpenAPI files. From 0.145.0 until 0.146.0, openapi3filter repeatedly calls regexp.MustCompile for the same parameter-name regular expression inside the per-query-key loop in urlValuesDecoder.DecodeObject used to decode a deepObject query parameter. An unauthenticated remote client can send an affected endpoint a request containing many unrelated query keys, causing ValidateRequest to perform work and allocations proportional to the attacker-controlled key count for every deepObject parameter. The expression itself is fixed and this is not regular expression denial of service; the resource consumption comes from loop-invariant recompilation. This issue is fixed in version 0.146.0.

ZoneMinder failed token handling bypasses web authentication ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. In versions 1.34.0 through 1.36.38, the web interface mishandles failed token authentication in web/includes/auth.php. validateToken() returns false when a token is malformed or has an invalid signature, but the caller assigns that value to the global $user variable; because web/index.php tests isset($user), boolean false is treated as a present user and the normal login redirect is skipped. This can dispatch views that rely on the outer authentication gate, including the zones view, which accepts an attacker-selected monitor ID and discloses monitor and zone metadata without an independent permission check. Permission helpers receive the false user value and deny privileged operations, so unauthorized state changes have not been established. This vulnerability is fixed in version 1.36.63, where conversion to ZM\User objects causes invalid token state to fail before view dispatch. Later defense-in-depth changes explicitly leave $user unset after failed token validation and reject non-ZM\User values at the web authentication gate.

Game Music Emu (libgme) through 0.6.5 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via AY Loader

Game Music Emu (libgme) through 0.6.5 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the AY loader get_data function caused by an integer underflow in the track-table bounds check. Attackers can supply a crafted ZXAYEMUL file with an oversized track table to read past the file buffer via gme_track_info or gme_start_track, crashing libgme consumers.

Dragonfly through 2.0.2 Unbounded Memory Allocation via Negative COUNT in HRANDFIELD, ZRANDMEMBER and SRANDMEMBER

Dragonfly through 2.0.2 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated clients to exhaust memory by passing a negative COUNT to HRANDFIELD, ZRANDMEMBER or SRANDMEMBER. Dragonfly through 2.0.2 Unbounded Memory Allocation via Negative COUNT in HRANDFIELD, ZRANDMEMBER and SRANDMEMBER

Dragonfly through 2.0.2 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated clients to exhaust memory by passing a negative COUNT to HRANDFIELD, ZRANDMEMBER or SRANDMEMBER. Attackers can send a single command against a one-element key with a huge negative COUNT to trigger the OOM killer, terminating the instance for all clients.

FluidSynth through 2.6.1 Out-of-Bounds Write via SoundFont Modulator Destination

FluidSynth through 2.6.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability that allows attackers to corrupt heap and stack memory by supplying unvalidated SoundFont modulator destination values. Attackers can craft an SF2 file with PMOD/IMOD destinations of 63 to 255 that, when loaded and played, write past the voice generator array and updated_gen_bit, causing memory corruption and crashes.

- [VulnCheck Advisory: FluidSynth through 2.6.1 Out-of-Bounds Write via SoundFont Modulator Destination](https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/fluidsynth-through-2.6.1-out-of-bounds-write-via-soundfont-modulator-destination) (`third-party-advisory`)

body: tinytag: Infinite loop when parsing certain M4A files containing invalid atoms

tinytag is a Python library for reading audio file metadata. From 2.0.0 until 2.3.0, an M4A file containing a sub-atom with a size of zero inside a ---- atom can cause the metadata parser to stop advancing through the input. The custom-field atom traversal repeatedly processes the malformed location, causing an infinite loop and denying service to a program that reads the crafted file. This issue is fixed in version 2.3.0.

ssldump Heap Buffer Overflow in FAN/1 X.509 Fingerprint Formatting The fanx_fingerprint function in ssl/sslxprint.c of ssldump allocates a heap buffer for formatting FAN/1 X.509 certificate fingerprints. The allocation size is computed as strlen(b64) + strlen(hex) + 31, but the format string "fan1:x509:server:passive:%s:sha256:%s" contains 33 fixed characters in addition to the two variable-length fields and a null terminator, requiring strlen(b64) + strlen(hex) + 34 bytes. This miscalculation results in a 3-byte heap-based buffer overflow on every invocation of the function with valid inputs. The overflow occurs because sprintf writes the full formatted string into the undersized heap buffer without bounds checking. An attacker who can supply a crafted pcap file containing a TLS X.509 certificate to a user running ssldump with FAN/1 fingerprinting enabled (for example with the -j -N options) can trigger the overflow. The resulting heap corruption may lead to denial of service through a crash or, in a worst-case scenario, arbitrary code execution in the context of the user running ssldump. The vulnerability is deterministic and requires no special privileges beyond the ability to provide input to the tool.

body: Text::CSV_XS versions before 1.65 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by allocating one entry per index of an RFC 7111 selector in fragment
Text::CSV_XS versions before 1.65 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by allocating one entry per index of an RFC 7111 selector in fragment.

fragment expands a row= or col= selector into an array with one element per selected index before it reads any data, and it does not clamp an explicit end column in a cell= selector to the row. Safing Portmaster before 2.2.5 Unauthenticated Forced Downgrade via /api/v1/updates/from-url

Safing Portmaster before 2.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unprivileged local processes to force updates by calling the POST /api/v1/updates/from-url endpoint registered with api.PermitAnyone. Attackers can supply an attacker-controlled index URL that bypasses version checks and auto-apply settings, installing older Safing-signed releases carrying previously fixed vulnerabilities.

libmng through 2.0.3 Heap Buffer Overflow via ORDR Chunk Reader mng_read_ordr libmng through 2.0.3 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in mng_read_ordr() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory because ORDR entry buffers are sized by 5-byte on-wire records instead of 8-byte in-memory entries. snac2 before 2.93 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in _xs_json_load_lexer() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending JSON strings containing a \^@ escape. smpeg through 2.0.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via MPEGsystem::FillBuffer smpeg through 2.0.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in MPEGsystem::FillBuffer() that allows attackers to read past the 16384-byte buffer by supplying a crafted system header stream table. Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes
<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
`code -w` in the integrated terminal waits until I close the file's tab, then exits. That's how it's supposed to work.
If I add `-g file:line`, the command never exits when I close the tab.
1. Open a terminal in VS Code in the browser with `code serve-web`.
2. Run `code -w README.md`. A tab opens. Go on and close it. The command exits. Works correctly
3. Run `code -w -g README.md:1`. A tab opens. Go on and close it. The command keeps running. Doesn't work.
Step 3 should exit when the tab is closed, like step 2.
Tools that open VS Code as an editor and wait for it hang forever. For example, pressing ctrl+g in Claude Code runs `code -w -g file:line` and gets stuck.
- Browser version (`code serve-web`), used as a PWA in Google Chrome on macOS
- VS Code server runs on Linux (aarch64) in a dev container
- The `code` command is the remote CLI: `~/.vscode/cli/serve-web/<commit>/bin/remote-cli/code`
The same steps work correctly in:
- desktop VS Code with dev container extension and "attach to running container"
The problem only happens in the browser version (`code serve-web`).

- VS Code Version: 1.142.0
- OS Version: container: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (aarch64) (macOS: 27.0.1)

## What happens

`code -w` in the integrated terminal waits until I close the file's tab, then exits. That's how it's supposed to work.

If I add `-g file:line`, the command never exits when I close the tab.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a terminal in VS Code in the browser with `code serve-web`.
2. Run `code -w README.md`. A tab opens. Go on and close it. The command exits. Works correctly
3. Run `code -w -g README.md:1`. A tab opens. Go on and close it. The command keeps running. Doesn't work.

## Expected

Step 3 should exit when the tab is closed, like step 2.

## Why it matters

Tools that open VS Code as an editor and wait for it hang forever. For example, pressing ctrl+g in Claude Code runs `code -w -g file:line` and gets stuck.

## Setup

- VS Code 1.142.0 (commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1)
- Browser version (`code serve-web`), used as a PWA in Google Chrome on macOS
- VS Code server runs on Linux (aarch64) in a dev container
- The `code` command is the remote CLI: `~/.vscode/cli/serve-web/<commit>/bin/remote-cli/code`

## Only in the browser version

The same steps work correctly in:

- desktop VS Code on macOS
- desktop VS Code with dev container extension and "attach to running container"

The problem only happens in the browser version (`code serve-web`).
"}

declaration.instruction: Using only the complete body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates, decide whether at least one statement declares a responsibility, functional capability, input/output relationship, permitted condition or acceptance condition as a specification. A present-tense description or quoted interface text can state a responsibility or what an action does or is for; formal requirement wording, future tense, adoption or implementation is not required. Count the declared relationship even inside a reproduction or report, and even if an observed result elsewhere differs. Distinguish a function or responsibility asserted by the body from an account of a particular performed action and its actual result. A causal explanation of a failure is not by itself a specification. Do not infer unstated intended functionality from symptoms, observed outputs or workarounds. Judge the role of the words in context, not their heading, tense or format. Quoted or hypothetical wording counts when used to declare such a specification, not when displayed only as an illustration. One qualifying statement anywhere is enough. Do not consult external content.

options.no: No statement of the specified kind is present anywhere in the body.

request.instruction: Using only the complete body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates, decide whether it states a necessary or desired action or state, or makes a genuine request for an action, answer, remedy, improvement or recovery. A person's own stated need or desired outcome counts; an instruction addressed to someone else is not required. Indirect wishes and conditional reporting or submission instructions count when the body actually expresses the required or desired condition or request. A requirement may be conditional, unimplemented, unadopted or unrelated to the main bug, and need not specify every detail. A completed action or achieved state alone does not state a requirement. A report of a symptom, inability, failure, observed result, workaround or causal explanation alone is not a request or a statement of a necessary or desired condition. A heading, recipient marker, question mark or imperative form does not by itself establish one; the content must express it in context. Quoted or hypothetical wording counts when used as an actual requirement or request, not when displayed only as an illustration. One qualifying statement anywhere is enough. Do not infer an unstated need, desired state or request and do not consult external content.

The pre-flight step correctly found that #14716 had already been assessed, produced an empty worklist, and caused zero model invocations.

```

```text
PR #14716: already assessed at 35c2bf381bb42655fb40ec8ebf2e0a0548ef7543, skipping
Work list: 0 PR(s) -> /tmp/gh-aw/dependabot-worklist.json
{
  "working_set": {
    "cumulative_input_tokens": 0,
    "peak_input_tokens": 0,
    "invocations": 0
  }
}
```

However, `gh-aw` records the job as started before its harness observes the noop. The daily guardrail then treats the empty accounting file as unknown and applies the `max-ai-credits` fallback.

Five consecutive no-work runs were each counted as `1000` AIC, which exhausted the `5000` daily guardrail.

[daily-workflow-aic] Computed run AIC: {"runId":39132745345,"aic":1000,"reason":"scan_cache"}
[daily-workflow-aic] Computed run AIC: {"runId":39128819878,"aic":1000,"reason":"scan_cache"}
[daily-workflow-aic] Computed run AIC: {"runId":39124342426,"aic":1000,"reason":"scan_cache"}
[daily-workflow-aic] Computed run AIC: {"runId":39120364428,"aic":1000,"reason":"scan_cache"}
[daily-workflow-aic] Completed AIC inspection window: {"currentAIC":5000,"threshold":5000,"exceeded":true}
```

* Each ready, unassessed Dependabot PR is dispatched for triage.
* The existing once-per-head-SHA behaviour remains unchanged.
* The `max-daily-ai-credits` guardrail remains enabled for genuine agent runs.

### Additional context

Lowering `max-ai-credits`, reducing the schedule frequency, or raising the daily limit would reduce the impact, but none fixes the false accounting path.

The underlying `gh-aw` behaviour should still be reported upstream. This repository-side split prevents that behaviour from blocking Dependabot triage while preserving the guardrail."}

1. Open a GitHub Codespace in Safari.

The webview should fill the available sidebar area and resize with it.
The webview overlay collapses to approximately 300 × 150 px, leaving most of the sidebar empty.
The overlay uses CSS anchor positioning:
The anchor exists and has valid dimensions. Both CSS feature checks return `true`:
However, the overlay does not receive the expected dimensions.
Manually assigning the overlay's width and height using the anchor's `getBoundingClientRect()` immediately fixes the rendering.
Attaching a `ResizeObserver` to the anchor and updating the overlay dimensions also preserves correct behavior when resizing the sidebar.

{"body":"## Nixpkgs version

Unstable (26.11), revision `0d927ee3b4dfd77e453f28d6289e58d55136975b`.

## Describe the bug

Evaluating `azure-cli.drvPath` fails because its dependency `python3.14-fabric-3.2.3` is marked broken when used with Invoke >=3. The failure happens before a build starts.

   ```sh
   nix-instantiate --eval --strict --expr '

     in
       (import src {
         system = "aarch64-darwin";
         config = {};
         overlays = [];
       }).azure-cli.drvPath
   '
   ```

2. The command exits with status 1 and the Fabric broken-package error below.

The revision-pinned command above

`azure-cli.drvPath` evaluates successfully

NA

body: In a new **Copilot** (Agent Host) chat, the sandbox CA features don't work until you send a message:
- The **Sandbox trusted CA is not installed** alert doesn't show.
- **Sandbox: Manage Trusted CA** says **No agent host detected.**
1. Set `"chat.agent.sandbox.enabled": "on"`. Make sure the sandbox CA is not installed.
2. Open a new chat with the **Copilot** harness and click into the input. Don't send anything.
3. Run **Sandbox: Manage Trusted CA** from the Command Palette.
- The alert appears right away, and the command now opens the Install / Rotate / Remove picker.
**Expected:** Both work as soon as the Agent Host chat is open. TPI step 4 expects the alert before anything is sent.
Looks like the CA check only runs once the chat's session has actually started.
VS Code Insiders 1.143.0 (341e0fa), Windows 11, local agent host

body: The text in the **Sandbox trusted CA is not installed** alert wraps in the middle of words ("truste / d", "sand / box"):
1. Set `"chat.agent.sandbox.enabled": "on"`, with the sandbox CA not installed.
2. Send a message in a Copilot (Agent Host) chat so the alert shows.
3. Look at the alert text at the default Chat view width.

**Cause:** The description is built with `MarkdownString.appendText()` ([agentHostSandboxNotification.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/341e0fa9346520e7a6a09803a80c5ecd3027f3cb/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSandboxNotification.ts#L232)), which turns every space into ` ` ([htmlContent.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/341e0fa9346520e7a6a09803a80c5ecd3027f3cb/src/vs/base/common/htmlContent.ts#L75)). The sentence can't wrap between words, so it breaks anywhere.

{"body":"## Summary
Since updating to VS Code **1.142.0**, GitHub Copilot no longer works in a **WSL remote** window behind an authenticating corporate proxy. Before the update, the same setup worked without any configuration inside WSL.

The new `@github/copilot-sdk` (`1.0.19-unstable.38345923974.g3754b70`) bundled in the VS Code server appears to make its own network requests from inside WSL (`rust:rt_network`). Unlike the previous code path, it does not use the Windows-side proxy authentication or the Windows certificate store, even though `http.useLocalProxyConfiguration` and `http.systemCertificates` are at their defaults.

## Environment
- VS Code: 1.142.0 (commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1), Windows 11 x64 (10.0.26100)
- Remote: WSL 3.0.3, kernel 6.18.54.1, distro openSUSE Leap 15.6
- Proxy: `http.proxy` set in user settings (corporate Skyhigh Secure Web Gateway)
  - Responds with `407` and `Proxy-Authenticate: Negotiate`, `NTLM`, `Basic`
  - Performs TLS inspection with a corporate root CA that exists only in the Windows certificate store
- The Windows user is domain-joined and has a valid Kerberos TGT and service ticket for the proxy (`HTTP/<proxy>`).

## Error
```
Error: Request managedSettings.resolve failed with message: network fetch failed: proxy Negotiate authentication failed: failed to acquire proxy credentials: gss_init_sec_context failed: No credentials were supplied, or the credentials were unavailable or inaccessible; SPNEGO cannot find mechanisms to negotiate
    at handleResponse (.../vscode-jsonrpc/lib/common/connection.js:565:48)
    at Object.handleMessage (.../@github/copilot-sdk/dist/client.js:61:13)
```

`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log` (hostnames redacted):
```
[WARNING] [rust:rt_network::fetch] failed to acquire proxy Negotiate credentials {"proxy.host":"proxy.corp.example","proxy.port":8080,"target.host":"api.github.com","target.port":443,"spn":"HTTP/proxy.corp.example","custom_spn":false,"spn_source":"derived","reason":"credential_acquire_failed","error":"failed to acquire proxy credentials: gss_init_sec_context failed: No credentials were supplied, or the credentials were unavailable or inaccessible; SPNEGO cannot find mechanisms to negotiate"}
```

After a manual `kinit` inside WSL, proxy authentication succeeds, but certificate validation fails because the corporate inspection CA is not in the Linux trust store:
```
[WARNING] [rust:rt_network::fetch] proxy Negotiate tunnel failed {"proxy.host":"proxy.corp.example","proxy.port":8080,"target.host":"api.github.com","target.port":443,"reason":"io_error","error":"proxy tunnel failed: tunnel I/O error: invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer"}
```

## Steps to reproduce
1. On a domain-joined Windows machine behind a Negotiate/NTLM proxy with TLS inspection, set `"http.proxy"` in the user settings.
2. Open a WSL folder with VS Code 1.142.0. The distro has no Kerberos ticket and no corporate CA installed.
3. Use Copilot Chat. The request fails with the error above.

## Expected
The same behavior as before 1.142.0 and as for other remote extension host traffic:
- Use the local (Windows) proxy configuration and credentials (`http.useLocalProxyConfiguration`).
- Trust the system certificates from the local OS (`http.systemCertificates`).
- At least, fall back to NTLM or to the VS Code proxy agent instead of requiring a Kerberos ticket inside WSL.

## Workaround
Inside WSL: install `krb5-client`, configure the realm, run `kinit`, and copy the corporate root CA to `/etc/pki/trust/anchors/` followed by `update-ca-certificates`. This needs a new `kinit` every ~10 hours.

Related: microsoft/github-copilot-appmod#207, github/copilot-cli#2978"}

    at Object.handleMessage (.../@github/copilot-sdk/dist/client.js:61:13)

```
[WARNING] [rust:rt_network::fetch] failed to acquire proxy Negotiate credentials {"proxy.host":"proxy.corp.example","proxy.port":8080,"target.host":"api.github.com","target.port":443,"spn":"HTTP/proxy.corp.example","custom_spn":false,"spn_source":"derived","reason":"credential_acquire_failed","error":"failed to acquire proxy credentials: gss_init_sec_context failed: No credentials were supplied, or the credentials were unavailable or inaccessible; SPNEGO cannot find mechanisms to negotiate"}

- Trust the system certificates from the local OS (`http.systemCertificates`).
- At least, fall back to NTLM or to the VS Code proxy agent instead of requiring a Kerberos ticket inside WSL.

body: Since updating to VS Code **1.142.0**, GitHub Copilot no longer works in a **WSL remote** window behind an authenticating corporate proxy. Before the update, the same setup worked without any configuration inside WSL.

Unlike the previous code path, it does not use the Windows-side proxy authentication or the Windows certificate store, even though `http.useLocalProxyConfiguration` and `http.systemCertificates` are at their defaults.
- Remote: WSL 3.0.3, kernel 6.18.54.1, distro openSUSE Leap 15.6
- Proxy: `http.proxy` set in user settings (corporate Skyhigh Secure Web Gateway)
- Performs TLS inspection with a corporate root CA that exists only in the Windows certificate store
- The Windows user is domain-joined and has a valid Kerberos TGT and service ticket for the proxy (`HTTP/<proxy>`).

request.text:
{"body":"## Feature request

Provide a Quick Pick listing the available handlers for a link so users can choose which view opens its target.

## Expected behavior

- Show distinguishable handler names and identify the current/default handler where known.
- Open the target using the selected handler.
- Allow reopening the current target with another matching handler without reconstructing the link, preserving navigation context and placement where supported.
- Preserve the original target and opening intent (including opening to the side) when delegating to the selected handler.
- Cancelling leaves the current view unchanged.
- Ordinary link clicks should not require a picker every time.

Parent story: #342050.

## UX ideas to explore

These are alternatives to evaluate, not finalized interaction requirements:

- After opening a link, show a status bar action for approximately 20 seconds that lets the user change the handler used for that target. Use a slow fadeout rather than an abrupt disappearance.
- And/or let Ctrl+Alt+click or Ctrl+Alt+Enter open the handler Quick Pick directly, so the user can choose a handler before opening the target.
- Check platform conventions, existing keybinding conflicts, and accessibility (including reduced-motion behavior and a keyboard-accessible alternative to the transient action) before finalizing the gestures and fadeout.

Changing the handler for the current target is distinct from changing the default handler for future links; do not implicitly change the default."}

request.text:
{"body":"## Goal

Audit which link forms VS Code supports end to end, define what we should/can support, and track gaps with repeatable validation rather than assuming every link reaches the intended handler.

## Reported gaps to investigate

- Support Copilot CLI session links such as `copilotcli:/b2abb3b4-bf6c-4ee8-a0c4-213da0bd31cb`. Determine the session-resolution contract and opening behavior, including missing or unavailable sessions.
- Commit links reportedly do not open the native multi-diff editor. This observation has not yet been independently reproduced for this issue; capture the exact link form, build, repository context, and actual destination before classifying it as a regression.
- #342125 tracks completed support for repository/path-hinted commit links, not proof that every commit-link form is supported. Distinguish unsupported forms, missing prerequisites, and regressions in that implementation.

## Validation matrix

Cover these sources:
- Markdown editor.
- Chat messages and responses.
- Direct link input in Quick Open (Ctrl+P).

For each applicable combination, test ordinary opening, opening to the side, and explicit handler selection (#342544). Preserve the exact target, navigation context, and placement intent across handlers.

Representative targets:
- `copilotcli:/<session-id>` links, including the example above.
- `agent-host-session://` session and peer-chat links, including connection authority where applicable.
- Local and forge commit-link forms, with/without repository hints and with the repository open/closed. Verify which supported forms open the native multi-diff editor.
- Document links, including locations/selections.
- GitHub issue and PR links.
- Ordinary web links.

Record build/platform, exact link form, source, prerequisites, expected/actual handler, expected/actual placement, and supported/unsupported/failing status. Missing targets and unavailable handlers should have explicit, understandable behavior rather than silently opening an unrelated target.

## Deliverables

- A documented support matrix based on actual end-to-end checks.
- An explicit intended support contract: supported now, intended but broken/missing, and unsupported with rationale.
- Focused implementation/regression issues for gaps, linked back here and to the story.
- Repeatable test cases and automated coverage where appropriate for supported link forms.

## Related work

- Parent story: #342050.
- Commit multi-diff support: #342125 (completed in #341570).
- Agent-session open-to-side support: #342119 (implementation: #342109).
- General side opening: #340724.
- Handler Quick Pick and switching: #342544."}

body: 1. Open a page in VS Code's integrated browser.
2. Share the browser page with Copilot Chat.
"Read the currently shared browser page using the browser interaction tools.
Report whether an actual browser tool call succeeds."
4. Observe that the assistant cannot discover a callable browser page reader.
5. Reload VS Code, create a new chat, share the page, and repeat.
The shared page appears in the chat context with its page ID, title, and URL,
but no browser interaction call can be made.
The assistant reports that tool search exposes only an unrelated workspace
symbol-usage tool (`usages`), not browser tools such as `readPage`.
This affects both a direct request in a fresh chat and a delegated custom-agent
With browser tools enabled and a page shared, the assistant should be able to
invoke browser interaction tools to read the live page.
The issue persists after reloading VS Code and starting a fresh chat.
Copilot authentication succeeded before the failed requests.
The cause has not been established; no browser-tool registration error was
identified in the general Copilot Chat Output log.

body: Provide a consistent **Copy Link** action in editor tab context menus for link-addressable targets, rather than requiring users to discover a different sharing action in each view.

- Cover documents, chats, GitHub issue/PR views, and multi-diff views where a stable target link is supported. Define supported editor types and prerequisites explicitly rather than assuming every editor already has a link representation.

- Copy a canonical, reopenable target link, preserving meaningful target identity and navigation context rather than an incidental UI resource.
- Use consistent action naming and discoverability across supported tab types.
- Define clear unavailable behavior for targets that cannot be linked; do not copy an unrelated active target or an unusable link.
- Reuse the completed chat-tab implementation in #342121 (PR #341095) rather than reimplementing it.
- Validate copied links end to end with the support matrix in #342545.
- Chat active-editor restrictions are a separate bug, not the general cross-editor feature.

- Cover documents, chats, GitHub issue/PR views, and multi-diff views where a stable target link is supported. Define supported editor types and prerequisites explicitly rather than assuming every editor already has a link representation.
- Resolve the tab whose context menu was invoked, including inactive tabs, instead of relying on the active editor.
- Copy a canonical, reopenable target link, preserving meaningful target identity and navigation context rather than an incidental UI resource.
- Use consistent action naming and discoverability across supported tab types.
- Define clear unavailable behavior for targets that cannot be linked; do not copy an unrelated active target or an unusable link.
- Reuse the completed chat-tab implementation in #342121 (PR #341095) rather than reimplementing it.
- Validate copied links end to end with the support matrix in #342545.
- Chat active-editor restrictions are a separate bug, not the general cross-editor feature.

request.text:
{"body":"## Reported problem

Chat **Copy Link** reportedly only works when the chat is active and presented as a chat editor. Inactive chats and chats hosted outside an editor do not provide the same working experience.

This user report has not yet been independently reproduced. Capture the exact build, chat surface, command/menu entry, and clipboard result before narrowing the root cause.

## Cases to reproduce

1. Open two chats as editor tabs and activate one of them.
2. Invoke Copy Link on the other, inactive chat tab. Check command availability and that the copied link identifies that tab's chat, not the active chat.
3. Repeat with an active chat editor as the baseline.
4. Try Copy Link for a chat hosted outside an editor (for example, the Chat view). Record whether the action is unavailable or fails, and whether moving that chat into an active editor changes the result.

## Expected behavior

- Copy the explicitly targeted chat's canonical link without requiring the user to activate its editor first.
- Do not silently substitute the active chat when targeting another chat.
- Clarify and address Copy Link availability for non-editor chat surfaces, without requiring the chat to be moved to an editor merely to obtain its link.
- Preserve session identity, peer-chat identity, and connection authority where applicable.

## Scope distinction

#342121 (completed in #341095) explicitly promises inactive-tab support. Treat failure for an inactive editor tab as a potential regression or implementation gap in that existing contract. Copy Link for non-editor chat surfaces may require additional surface integration; do not assume it has the same root cause or was covered by that completed work.

## Tracking

- Parent story: #342050.
- Completed chat-tab Copy Link work: #342121.
- Link-support validation: #342545."}

body: List settings in the Settings editor can't be reordered by dragging. Rows are still marked `draggable`, and drag-to-reorder was added on purpose in #128884 (for #127424), so this is a regression rather than a missing feature.
2. Open the Settings editor and search for `git.branchProtection`.
3. Press on the `b` row and drag it above `a`.
The rows swap and settings.json updates to `["b", "a"]`.

{"body":"Refs: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340702
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/340779

- [ ] anyOS @rwoll 

Complexity: 3

Authors: @Giuspepe

[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23342569%0A%0A&assignees=Giuspepe)

---

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c967b88c-13b3-4917-8088-c27325a7f233


When managed settings require Copilot Agent Host, existing Claude and Codex Agent Host chats should remain accessible. Opening an eligible chat should copy it to Copilot and archive the original as read-only.

This tests **local Agent Host Claude and Codex sessions**, not sessions from the standalone OpenAI or Anthropic extensions.

Run the main flow for **both providers with each policy below**. Between runs, reset the managed settings file to `{}`, restart VS Code, and create fresh test sessions.

1. Back up any existing managed settings file, then start with no file or `{}`.

   | OS | Managed settings file |
   | --- | --- |
   | macOS | `/Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json` |
   | Windows | `%ProgramFiles%\GitHubCopilot\managed-settings.json` |
   | Linux | `/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json` |

2. Use VS Code Insiders containing #340702. Ensure Claude, Codex, and Copilot work before applying policy. Enable the Agent Host providers if needed:

   ```json
   {
       "chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled": true,
       "chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled": true
   }
   ```

3. In the Agents window, create three sessions with the provider being tested. Use a trusted local folder with **Folder** isolation for this flow. Give each session a recognizable title and a short conversation, such as “Remember that the test codeword is mango.”

4. Keep the first session open after its response finishes. Type “What is the test codeword?” and attach a file, but **do not send**.

5. Write one of these policies to the managed settings file. Wait for it to take effect without restarting.

   **Sandbox:**

   ```json
   {"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"allowBypass":false}}
   ```

   **Permissions:**

   ```json
   {"permissions":{"disableBypassPermissionsMode":"disable"}}
   ```

6. Confirm the open session automatically switches to a Copilot Agent Host copy. A migration message may appear briefly. Verify that:

   - The conversation and original title are preserved.
   - The unsent draft and attachment remain in the input.
   - No message is sent automatically.
   - Sending the draft now produces a Copilot response that uses the earlier conversation.

7. Check the session list. The other two Claude/Codex sessions should still be listed. Open the second session and confirm it also migrates to Copilot with its title and transcript preserved.

8. Open the first original session from **Archived**. Confirm its transcript is readable, it is read-only, and it does not automatically migrate again. Select **Continue in Copilot** and verify it opens the existing Copilot copy without creating a duplicate.

9. Fully quit and restart VS Code while the policy remains enabled. Confirm the third, unmigrated session is still listed. Open it and verify that its saved history loads and migration succeeds. Reopen an archived original and confirm its transcript is still readable.

10. Confirm that new Claude/Codex sessions and messages in the original sessions remain blocked. Copilot should remain usable under the applied policy.
"}

body: When managed settings require Copilot Agent Host, existing Claude and Codex Agent Host chats should remain accessible. Opening an eligible chat should copy it to Copilot and archive the original as read-only.
This tests **local Agent Host Claude and Codex sessions**, not sessions from the standalone OpenAI or Anthropic extensions.
Run the main flow for **both providers with each policy below**. Between runs, reset the managed settings file to `{}`, restart VS Code, and create fresh test sessions.
1. Back up any existing managed settings file, then start with no file or `{}`.
2. Use VS Code Insiders containing #340702. Ensure Claude, Codex, and Copilot work before applying policy. Enable the Agent Host providers if needed:

3. In the Agents window, create three sessions with the provider being tested. Use a trusted local folder with **Folder** isolation for this flow. Give each session a recognizable title and a short conversation, such as “Remember that the test codeword is mango.”
4. Keep the first session open after its response finishes. Type “What is the test codeword?” and attach a file, but **do not send**.
5. Write one of these policies to the managed settings file. Wait for it to take effect without restarting.
6. Confirm the open session automatically switches to a Copilot Agent Host copy. A migration message may appear briefly. Verify that:
- The conversation and original title are preserved.
- The unsent draft and attachment remain in the input.
- Sending the draft now produces a Copilot response that uses the earlier conversation.
7. Check the session list. The other two Claude/Codex sessions should still be listed. Open the second session and confirm it also migrates to Copilot with its title and transcript preserved.

8. Open the first original session from **Archived**. Confirm its transcript is readable, it is read-only, and it does not automatically migrate again. Select **Continue in Copilot** and verify it opens the existing Copilot copy without creating a duplicate.

9. Fully quit and restart VS Code while the policy remains enabled. Confirm the third, unmigrated session is still listed. Open it and verify that its saved history loads and migration succeeds. Reopen an archived original and confirm its transcript is still readable.
10. Confirm that new Claude/Codex sessions and messages in the original sessions remain blocked. Copilot should remain usable under the applied policy.

{"body":"From @alexdima 
By the way, I've been trying out the Bake Off, very cool, it feels a lot more polished! I have some small feedback:
[not a deal breaker] I find I would like to use it without a git folder, like from a folderless "Chat". I find going to different models good when ideating and I might want to see how different models would tackle something before doing actual work. I think this is useful for actual work too, but I just used it so far for ideas/plans and would have loved to have them work in a simple Chat too. I think today it only works once I pick a folder..I think 

> we can get this to work

with this model picker that opens by default the current model, it is a bit difficult to discover the icon (which is not suggestive at all). Maybe in this pane (see screenshot) we could have at the bottom a [+ Send query to multiple models]

> I think we all agree the icon is not great. I like his suggestion here.

the + and the icon (see the second screenshot). I am so silly I initially thought + would add a second model because it's like I add another one to the current one... It took me quite some time to realise that + is actually a configuration page and maybe should have the cogwheel icon and that the 3 rectangles at the right are the bake off. Maybe Lee can help with a vendor to help us with a more interesting icon, maybe like a competition trophy icon or maybe like two boxing hands or maybe two running people or a special brain, unsure...

> Agreed we need a better icon"}

{"body":"## Summary

In the **Copilot harness** (Agent Host) and the **GitHub Copilot app**, the `model` and `reasoning-effort` frontmatter of a custom agent are **not applied when the agent is selected as the main agent**. The session keeps the model and reasoning effort from the picker.

The same fields **are** applied when the agent runs as a **subagent**, and the **Local** harness applies the agent's model on selection.

The docs describe `model` as "the model to use in the Copilot harness" and `reasoning-effort` as "reasoning effort for the agent in the Copilot harness". This looks like a bug or a missing feature, not intended behavior.

## Expected behavior

Selecting a custom agent preselects its `model` (first available entry if a list) and `reasoning-effort` for the session, as in the Local harness. The user can still change them afterwards in the picker.

## Actual behavior

| Scenario | `model` / `reasoning-effort` from agent file |
|---|---|
| Local harness, agent selected | Applied |
| Copilot harness / Copilot app, agent **run as subagent** | Applied (`model`). A subagent without `reasoning-effort` inherits the parent's effort. |
| Copilot harness / Copilot app, agent **selected as main agent** | **Ignored**. Session keeps the picker's model and effort. |

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create `~/.copilot/agents/DevAgent.agent.md`:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: DevAgent
   description: Repro agent
   model: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (copilot)
   reasoning-effort: high
   ---
   Reply briefly.
   ```

2. Start a session in the Copilot harness (VS Code) or in the GitHub Copilot app.
3. In the model picker, select `claude-opus-5.5` with effort `medium`.
4. Select `DevAgent` in the agent picker and send any prompt.

**Result:** the session keeps using `claude-opus-5.5` at `medium`.
**Expected:** `claude-sonnet-5.5` at `high`.

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| VS Code | 1.141.1 |
| GitHub Copilot Chat | 0.69.0 |
| Copilot CLI runtime (VS Code harness) | 1.0.92-4 |
| Copilot CLI runtime (GitHub Copilot app) | 1.0.99-2 |
| OS | Windows 11 (10.0.26200) |
| Agent location | `~/.copilot/agents/` (user level) |"}

body: Reported in the Fusion bug bash: https://github.com/github/copilot-api/issues/40010#issuecomment-6271608674 (by @spurwaha)

On a **Free** (and presumably **Student/EDU**) account with Fusion enabled, the model picker's "Upgrade for More Models" section still lists a disabled **"HydraFusion"** entry with an **Upgrade** button, alongside the real upsell models (Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol).
The expectation is that the old "HydraFusion" name should not be visible anywhere in the UI now that it's surfaced as **Fusion**.

`filterModelPickerControlModelsForEntitlement` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/modelPicker/modelPickerPresentation.ts` intentionally keeps a single HydraFusion control-model entry as an upsell for Free/EDU entitlements ("One upsell stands for every HydraFusion model, so it takes the base model's name"). The tabbed picker then renders it in the "Upgrade for More Models" upsell section (`_getUpsellSectionLabel` in `modelPickerTabbedWidget.ts`).
With Fusion enabled, HydraFusion is exposed to users only as Fusion's tiers, so this upsell row leaks an internal name.
- No "HydraFusion" (or "HydraFusion Max") label in the model picker for Free/Student users.
- Either drop the HydraFusion upsell row when Fusion is presenting it, or upsell via Fusion's tier UI (e.g. the High/Max tiers) instead of a standalone model entry.
1. Sign in with a Copilot Free (or Student) account in VS Code Insiders with Fusion enabled.
3. Observe the "Upgrade for More Models" section.

body: **Version:** VS Code 1.142.0 (user setup), commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1, Windows 10.0.26200 x64, connected via Remote SSH to a Linux host. `@github/copilot` 1.0.95-0.unstable.r38345923974.g3754b70, `@github/copilot-sdk` 1.0.19.38345923974.g3754b70.
1. Start a new chat on the **Copilot** harness (the default for new sessions since 1.142).
2. Open the attach (+) picker in the chat input.

The picker lists only Files & Folders, Screenshot Window, Sessions, Issue and Pull Request, plus recently opened files. The **Instructions…** item that is available in the Local harness is absent. I did not find this change in the 1.142 release notes.

- `.instructions.md` files with an `applyTo` glob are only listed to the model by path, with a rule to read them before editing matching files. Their application is not guaranteed and may not survive context compaction.
- Attaching the file as a plain file (or as implicit editor context) gives no stated persistence guarantee.
- Previously, explicitly adding instructions to a session was how I made sure they applied for the whole session.
1. Restore **Instructions…** in the attach picker for the Copilot harness, with the same behavior as the Local harness; or
2. Document how instructions are loaded and persisted in the Copilot harness (full text vs. path, behavior after compaction) and provide a way to pin instruction files to a session.
- Is an instructions-type attachment treated differently from a plain file attachment?
- Does the Local harness behave differently here?
- #324136 and #326766 (terminal approval dialog parity between harnesses)

Start a new chat on the **Copilot** harness (the default for new sessions since 1.142). 2. Open the attach (+) picker in the chat input. ## Actual The picker lists only Files & Folders, Screenshot Window, Sessions, Issue and Pull Request, plus recently opened files. request.text:
{"body":"Extensions currently define Terminal toolbar buttons statically in package.json. Please provide an extension API to dynamically add, remove, rename and reorder terminal toolbar buttons at runtime, including the ability to update their icons, tooltips and bound commands.

Background
- Our extension reads terminal actions from settings.json and builds toolbar buttons for terminals. Any change to the button names, icons, count, or ordering requires rebuilding/reinstalling the extension and reloading VS Code because buttons are currently declared statically in package.json.
- This forces a poor UX: configuration changes must wait for an extension reload and cannot be applied to running terminals immediately.

Proposal
- Expose a mutable Terminal toolbar API (conceptually similar to StatusBarItem) on the Extension API that allows extensions to:
  - createTerminalAction(id: string, options: { text?, iconPath?, tooltip?, command?, alignment?, priority? }): TerminalAction
  - updateTerminalAction(action: TerminalAction, updates: { text?, iconPath?, tooltip?, command?, order? }): void
  - disposeTerminalAction(action: TerminalAction): void
  - a method to attach actions to a specific Terminal instance (or to all terminals)
- Actions should be immediately visible and interactive on the terminal toolbar when created/updated/disposed without requiring extension reloads or window reloads.
- Support for ordering and grouping of actions, and a way to provide accessible labels and tooltips.

Requirements / considerations
- Icons should accept ThemeIcon, URI, or built-in icon identifiers.
- Actions should be serializable to settings or workspace state so extensions can persist user-configured actions between sessions.
- Consider how actions behave with multiple terminal instances, split terminals, and terminal editors.
- Ensure accessibility: keyboard focus order, ARIA labels, and screen reader support for dynamic changes.

Benefits
- Allow extensions to implement configurable, clickable terminal action buttons that reflect live changes in the extension settings without forcing reloads or using QuickPick as a workaround.
- Improve UX for extensions that provide terminal tooling (runners, debuggers, task shortcuts, REPL helpers).

Related issues
- #110218
- #224090

Requested labels: api-proposal, terminal-tools, feature-request"}

request.text:
{"body":"## Problem

In the unified workspace picker, selecting an item from the **Chat** submenu with the mouse is difficult. Moving the pointer from the "Chat" row into its flyout submenu requires very precise movement — the path to the target item crosses other rows in the parent list, which can change or dismiss the flyout before the pointer reaches the intended entry.

This is the same category of issue previously fixed for the Remote flyout in #335876 (safe pointer travel / anchoring), but affects the **Chat** submenu specifically.

## Screenshot

See attached screenshot: the search/workspace picker is open with "Chat" highlighted, showing a submenu to the right listing "This Computer" and ah1-ah4 / sh1-sh4 entries. Reaching those submenu items with the mouse is error-prone.

## Expected behavior

The Chat submenu should tolerate natural pointer movement from the triggering row into the flyout (e.g. via a safe-triangle / submenu-intent interaction model), consistent with the fix applied to the Remote flyout in #335876.

## Reproduction

1. Open the unified workspace picker.
2. Hover/select the **Chat** row to open its submenu.
3. Try to move the mouse diagonally toward an entry in the submenu.
4. Notice the flyout can close or change before reaching the target, especially with several entries listed."}

The authorized ready-for-review transition succeeds, or the error clearly identifies a retryable service failure.

The connector succeeded at approximately 2026-10-19T17:29:54Z. No permissions or repository settings were changed between attempts. The PR is now ready, so it is no longer a reproduction target. No debug logs or credentials are included.

## Description

When using `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.sdkRoot` with a globally installed Codex CLI managed by pnpm, the Codex Agent Host fails to locate the platform-specific executable.

The Codex CLI itself works correctly, and the configured `sdkRoot` contains `node_modules/@openai/codex` as documented in #341553. However, Agent Host expects the platform package at a fixed top-level path that does not exist in the observed pnpm installation layout.

Creating a symlink at the expected location resolves the executable lookup failure.

## Environment

- VS Code Version: 1.142.0 (Stable)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Insider Preview Build 28020.3262
- WSL Version: 3.0.3.0
- WSL Distribution: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x64)
- pnpm Version: 12.14.0
- Codex CLI Version: 0.163.0
- Agent Host: Running in WSL

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Codex CLI globally using pnpm:

   ```bash
   pnpm add -g @openai/codex@0.163.0
   codex --version
   ```

   The CLI runs successfully and reports `codex-cli 0.163.0`.

2. Locate the pnpm global installation directory containing `node_modules/@openai/codex`.

   In my environment:

   ```text
   /home/<user>/.local/share/pnpm/global/v11/b479-18dffc010a6c82c9-0
   ```

3. Configure the WSL Agent Host to use this directory:

   ```json
   {
     "chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled": true,
     "chat.agentHost.codexAgent.sdkRoot": "/home/<user>/.local/share/pnpm/global/v11/b479-18dffc010a6c82c9-0"
   }
   ```

4. Restart VS Code and attempt to create a Codex Agent Host session.

## Actual Behavior

Agent Host correctly recognizes the `sdkRoot` override:

```text
[AgentSdkDownloader] codex: using dev override at <sdkRoot>
```

However, it fails to locate the executable:

```text
[Codex] thread/list failed: Codex binary not executable:
<sdkRoot>/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex
(ENOENT: no such file or directory)
```

### Package layout

Codex declares the Linux x64 platform dependency using an npm alias:

```json
{
  "optionalDependencies": {
    "@openai/codex-linux-x64": "npm:@openai/codex@0.163.0-linux-x64"
  }
}
```

Here, `@openai/codex-linux-x64` is the dependency alias, while the underlying published package is `@openai/codex` at version `0.163.0-linux-x64`.

With pnpm, the underlying platform package is present at:

```text
<sdkRoot>/node_modules/.pnpm/@openai+codex@0.163.0-linux-x64/node_modules/@openai/codex/
```

This directory contains the platform-specific binary under:

```text
vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex
```

The `@openai/codex` directory here belongs to the platform variant (`0.163.0-linux-x64`), not the main CLI package (`0.163.0`).

However, Agent Host attempts to access:

```text
<sdkRoot>/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/
```

That top-level alias path does not exist in this pnpm installation.

## Workaround

Creating a symlink from the top-level alias path expected by Agent Host to the actual platform package directory resolves the executable lookup failure:

```bash
SDK_ROOT="/home/<user>/.local/share/pnpm/global/v11/b479-18dffc010a6c82c9-0"

ln -s \
  "$SDK_ROOT/node_modules/.pnpm/@openai+codex@0.163.0-linux-x64/node_modules/@openai/codex" \
  "$SDK_ROOT/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64"
```

After restarting Agent Host, the logs show:

```text
[CodexProxyService] listening on http://127.0.0.1:46013
[Codex] spawning app-server from <sdkRoot>/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex
```

No changes to the Codex CLI package or VS Code source code were required.

This confirms that the workaround resolves executable discovery and allows Agent Host to initiate App Server startup.

## Expected Behavior

Agent Host should resolve the platform-specific executable from the installed Codex package's dependency graph, without assuming that the platform dependency alias exists directly under the root `node_modules` directory.

The Codex CLI itself already resolves the platform package using `require.resolve()` relative to its own entry point:

https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-cli/bin/codex.js

A similar dependency resolution approach in Agent Host could avoid assumptions about physical package layouts.

## Additional Context

This issue is reproducible with pnpm, but may also affect other installation layouts where dependency aliases are not hoisted to the top-level `node_modules` directory.

The documented `sdkRoot` override requires `node_modules/@openai/codex`, which is present in this installation. The additional requirement for a top-level platform dependency alias is not documented.

Related issue: #341553."}
