{"body":"### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Since the nixos-unstable update that moved patchelf from 0.15.2 to 0.19.2, `nvidia-smi` from `nvidia-x11` segfaults immediately on every invocation, before any library is loaded. The driver itself is unaffected (kernel module loads, desktop/GPU work); only the patched `bin/` executables are broken.

This looks like the upstream patchelf bug NixOS/patchelf#674: running `--interpreter` and `--set-rpath` in **one** patchelf invocation produces a broken binary. The nvidia-x11 builder does exactly that for `nvidia-smi`, `nvidia-cuda-mps-*`, `nvidia-debugdump` and `nvidia-powerd`:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc/pkgs/os-specific/linux/nvidia-x11/builder.sh#L203-L204

```sh
patchelf --interpreter "$(cat $NIX_CC/nix-support/dynamic-linker)" \
    --set-rpath $out/lib:$libPath $bin/bin/$i
```

In the resulting ELF the read-only `LOAD` segment overlaps the writable one and `.dynamic` ends up mapped read-only, so `ld.so` crashes with `SEGV_ACCERR` in `dl_main` (presumably when it writes `DT_DEBUG`).

Program headers of the old (working) and new (broken) build of the same driver:

```
old (patchelf 0.15.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x001000 RW
  DYNAMIC  0x000318 0x3ff318 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  LOAD     0x001000 0x400000 ... 0x003418 R
  Segment 03: .dynamic                                    <- inside the RW LOAD

new (patchelf 0.19.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x002670 RW              <- covers up to 0x401670
  LOAD     0x0012c4 0x4002c4 ... 0x003154 R               <- starts at 0x4002c4, overlaps
  DYNAMIC  0x002480 0x401480 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  Segment 06: .dynstr .dynamic .gnu.version ... .rela.plt <- .dynamic inside the R LOAD
```

Things ruled out:
- **glibc** (2.44-25 -> 2.44-57 changed in the same update): the old binary runs fine with the new `ld.so`, and the new binary crashes with the old `ld.so`.
- **Libraries**: `LD_DEBUG=libs` prints nothing before the crash, so no library has been loaded yet; forcing the previous openssl also still crashes.
- **Driver version**: unchanged (615.78.08) between the working and broken builds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On nixos-unstable (09063bd) with `hardware.nvidia` enabled (proprietary driver 615.78.08, RTX 4070 SUPER), run `nvidia-smi`.
2. It segfaults (exit 139).

Standalone reproducer, re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/` with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:

```sh
BIN=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(command -v nvidia-smi))))   # nvidia-x11-*-bin output
RP=$(patchelf --print-rpath $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)
INT=$(patchelf --print-interpreter $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)

# single invocation, as builder.sh does
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi single && chmod +w single
patchelf --interpreter $INT --set-rpath "$RP" single
cmp single $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi && echo identical   # -> identical to the nixpkgs binary
./single -L                                        # -> Segmentation fault (exit 139)

# two invocations, rpath first
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi split && chmod +w split
patchelf --set-rpath "$RP" split
patchelf --interpreter $INT split
./split -L                                         # -> GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER ... (exit 0)
```


### Minimal reproducer

```nix
Re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/`, with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:


BIN=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(command -v nvidia-smi))))   # nvidia-x11-*-bin output
RP=$(patchelf --print-rpath $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)
INT=$(patchelf --print-interpreter $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)

# single invocation, as builder.sh does
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi single && chmod +w single
patchelf --interpreter $INT --set-rpath "$RP" single
cmp single $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi && echo identical   # -> identical to the nixpkgs binary
./single -L                                        # -> Segmentation fault (exit 139)

# two invocations, rpath first
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi split && chmod +w split
patchelf --set-rpath "$RP" split
patchelf --interpreter $INT split
./split -L                                         # -> GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER ... (exit 0)
```

### Expected behaviour

`nvidia-smi` runs, as it did with the previous build of the same driver (patched with patchelf 0.15.2).

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
$ nvidia-smi
Segmentation fault (core dumped)

systemd-coredump stack trace:
#0  dl_main (/nix/store/...-glibc-2.44-57/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 + 0x25a74)
#1  _dl_sysdep_start
#2  _dl_start
#3  _start
Signal: 11 (SEGV) si_code: SEGV_ACCERR
```

### Additional context

- Any systemd unit that calls `nvidia-smi` (e.g. one running `nvidia-smi -pm 1` at boot) now fails on every boot and every `nixos-rebuild switch`.
- Upstream patchelf bug: https://github.com/NixOS/patchelf/issues/674 (another NixOS user confirms it with driver 595.104.02 on an RTX 3080).
- Possible fix in nixpkgs until patchelf is fixed: split the call in `builder.sh` into `patchelf --set-rpath ...` followed by a separate `patchelf --interpreter ...`.

AI disclosure (per the Nixpkgs automation/AI policy): the investigation and this write-up were done with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). I ran the reproducer from "Steps to reproduce" on my machine and reviewed the report before submitting.

### System metadata

- system: `"x86_64-linux"`
- host os: `Linux 7.2.11-zen1, NixOS, 26.11 (Zokor), 26.11.20261017.09063bd`
- multi-user?: `yes`
- sandbox: `yes`
- version: `nix-env (Nix) 2.34.9`
- nixpkgs: nixos-unstable at `09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc`
- NVIDIA driver: 615.78.08 (proprietary, `hardware.nvidia.open = false`)
- patchelf: 0.19.2 (previously 0.15.2)

### Notify maintainers

@Kiskae 
@edwtjo

---

- [x] I assert that this is not a [duplicate of an existing issue](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%220.kind%3A+bug%22+-label%3A%226.topic%3A+darwin%22+-label%3A%226.topic%3A+nixos%22).

- [x] I assert that I have read the [automation/AI policy](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automationai-policy) and that this issue report complies with it.

### Is this issue important to you?

[reaction]: https://github.blog/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/
[issues you find important]: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc

{"body":"### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Since the nixos-unstable update that moved patchelf from 0.15.2 to 0.19.2, `nvidia-smi` from `nvidia-x11` segfaults immediately on every invocation, before any library is loaded. The driver itself is unaffected (kernel module loads, desktop/GPU work); only the patched `bin/` executables are broken.

This looks like the upstream patchelf bug NixOS/patchelf#674: running `--interpreter` and `--set-rpath` in **one** patchelf invocation produces a broken binary. The nvidia-x11 builder does exactly that for `nvidia-smi`, `nvidia-cuda-mps-*`, `nvidia-debugdump` and `nvidia-powerd`:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc/pkgs/os-specific/linux/nvidia-x11/builder.sh#L203-L204

```sh
patchelf --interpreter "$(cat $NIX_CC/nix-support/dynamic-linker)" \
    --set-rpath $out/lib:$libPath $bin/bin/$i
```

In the resulting ELF the read-only `LOAD` segment overlaps the writable one and `.dynamic` ends up mapped read-only, so `ld.so` crashes with `SEGV_ACCERR` in `dl_main` (presumably when it writes `DT_DEBUG`).

Program headers of the old (working) and new (broken) build of the same driver:

```
old (patchelf 0.15.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x001000 RW
  DYNAMIC  0x000318 0x3ff318 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  LOAD     0x001000 0x400000 ... 0x003418 R
  Segment 03: .dynamic                                    <- inside the RW LOAD

new (patchelf 0.19.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x002670 RW              <- covers up to 0x401670
  LOAD     0x0012c4 0x4002c4 ... 0x003154 R               <- starts at 0x4002c4, overlaps
  DYNAMIC  0x002480 0x401480 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  Segment 06: .dynstr .dynamic .gnu.version ... .rela.plt <- .dynamic inside the R LOAD
```

Things ruled out:
- **glibc** (2.44-25 -> 2.44-57 changed in the same update): the old binary runs fine with the new `ld.so`, and the new binary crashes with the old `ld.so`.
- **Libraries**: `LD_DEBUG=libs` prints nothing before the crash, so no library has been loaded yet; forcing the previous openssl also still crashes.
- **Driver version**: unchanged (615.78.08) between the working and broken builds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On nixos-unstable (09063bd) with `hardware.nvidia` enabled (proprietary driver 615.78.08, RTX 4070 SUPER), run `nvidia-smi`.
2. It segfaults (exit 139).

Standalone reproducer, re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/` with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:

```sh
BIN=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(command -v nvidia-smi))))   # nvidia-x11-*-bin output
RP=$(patchelf --print-rpath $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)
INT=$(patchelf --print-interpreter $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)

# single invocation, as builder.sh does
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi single && chmod +w single
patchelf --interpreter $INT --set-rpath "$RP" single
cmp single $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi && echo identical   # -> identical to the nixpkgs binary
./single -L                                        # -> Segmentation fault (exit 139)

# two invocations, rpath first
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi split && chmod +w split
patchelf --set-rpath "$RP" split
patchelf --interpreter $INT split
./split -L                                         # -> GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER ... (exit 0)
```


### Minimal reproducer

```nix
Re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/`, with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:


BIN=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(command -v nvidia-smi))))   # nvidia-x11-*-bin output
RP=$(patchelf --print-rpath $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)
INT=$(patchelf --print-interpreter $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)

# single invocation, as builder.sh does
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi single && chmod +w single
patchelf --interpreter $INT --set-rpath "$RP" single
cmp single $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi && echo identical   # -> identical to the nixpkgs binary
./single -L                                        # -> Segmentation fault (exit 139)

# two invocations, rpath first
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi split && chmod +w split
patchelf --set-rpath "$RP" split
patchelf --interpreter $INT split
./split -L                                         # -> GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER ... (exit 0)
```

### Expected behaviour

`nvidia-smi` runs, as it did with the previous build of the same driver (patched with patchelf 0.15.2).

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
$ nvidia-smi
Segmentation fault (core dumped)

systemd-coredump stack trace:
#0  dl_main (/nix/store/...-glibc-2.44-57/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 + 0x25a74)
#1  _dl_sysdep_start
#2  _dl_start
#3  _start
Signal: 11 (SEGV) si_code: SEGV_ACCERR
```

### Additional context

- Any systemd unit that calls `nvidia-smi` (e.g. one running `nvidia-smi -pm 1` at boot) now fails on every boot and every `nixos-rebuild switch`.
- Upstream patchelf bug: https://github.com/NixOS/patchelf/issues/674 (another NixOS user confirms it with driver 595.104.02 on an RTX 3080).
- Possible fix in nixpkgs until patchelf is fixed: split the call in `builder.sh` into `patchelf --set-rpath ...` followed by a separate `patchelf --interpreter ...`.

AI disclosure (per the Nixpkgs automation/AI policy): the investigation and this write-up were done with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). I ran the reproducer from "Steps to reproduce" on my machine and reviewed the report before submitting.

- version: `nix-env (Nix) 2.34.9`
- nixpkgs: nixos-unstable at `09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc`
- NVIDIA driver: 615.78.08 (proprietary, `hardware.nvidia.open = false`)
- patchelf: 0.19.2 (previously 0.15.2)

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem

The harness-aware `*.agent.md` schema work in #342854 can validate static attribute names, YAML shapes, enums, nested MCP/GitHub structures, and Copilot hook actions. Several useful value checks cannot be correct from static tables alone because the accepted values depend on the active harness, session, model catalogue, installed customizations, or connected servers.

We should inventory these opportunities and add provider-backed completion, hover, and validation only where the source is authoritative. Until an inventory has settled, the editor must not mark a value unused or unknown.

## Dynamic value opportunities

### Models

- Complete and validate `model` against models available to the effective harness/session.
- Support both scalar models and ordered model preference arrays.
- Distinguish unavailable, policy-disabled, and unknown model identifiers where the provider exposes that distinction.
- Validate `model-policy: required` against the declared model list and current availability without treating transient catalogue loading as an error.
- Complete or validate `reasoning-effort` using the selected model's advertised capabilities, while preserving arbitrary strings when the runtime intentionally accepts and adapts them.

### Tools

- Complete and validate `tools` against the authoritative Copilot tool inventory for the active session.
- Include provider-native tools, client-provided tools, MCP tools/server namespaces, supported aliases, and wildcard forms.
- Do not suggest VS Code tool sets to Copilot; mark authored tool-set references unused with an explanation that Copilot requires individual tools.
- Differentiate an unknown tool from a known but unavailable/disabled tool when the provider can do so.
- Revalidate when tools, MCP server state, client tools, or enablement changes.

### Skills and customizations

- Complete and validate `skills` from the active harness's enabled skill inventory.
- Use `ICustomizationItemProvider`/`provideChatSessionCustomizations` rather than Local `IPromptsService` discovery for provider-backed harnesses.
- Consider descriptions and source information in completion details and hovers.
- Revalidate when customizations are installed, removed, enabled, disabled, or republished.

### GitHub MCP configuration

- Complete `github.toolsets` from an authoritative GitHub MCP toolset catalogue if one is available.
- Complete permission scopes and values only if the runtime/provider publishes a stable schema. The current runtime structurally accepts string maps, so the editor should not invent restrictions from stale documentation.
- Explain values that are recognized but unavailable because of authentication, policy, or server configuration.

### Agent-scoped MCP servers

- Where available, validate `mcp-servers.<name>.tools` against the server's advertised tools.
- Detect duplicate/conflicting server names and tool namespace collisions when the provider supplies enough information.
- Avoid starting or authenticating a server merely to provide editor validation.
- Treat unresolved or disconnected server inventories as pending, not as an empty authoritative set.

## Additional value checks that do not require live inventory

These can be implemented in code or static metadata when useful:

- Validate hook `matcher` values as regular expressions where the runtime does so.
- Apply event-specific hook constraints, including matcher support and authorization-affecting HTTP hook requirements.
- Validate command action `exec`/`args`, shell-vs-exec exclusivity, positive timeouts, HTTP URL schemes, and prompt actions being limited to `sessionStart`.
- Recognize Copilot body placeholders such as `{{cwd}}`, `{{homedir}}`, `{{configDir}}`, `{{grepToolName}}`, `{{globToolName}}`, `{{shellToolName}}`, and `{{shellCommandExamples}}`; optionally mark unknown placeholder-like values.
- Detect duplicate scalar/array values where duplicates have no runtime meaning.

## Provider/API requirements

Prefer narrow optional APIs on `ICustomizationItemProvider` (or another harness-owned capability) rather than coupling language providers to agent-host state internals. Candidate capabilities include:

- `provideAgentFileModels(sessionResource, token)`
- `provideAgentFileTools(sessionResource, token)`
- Existing customization inventory for skills and other customization references

Returned entries should include stable identifiers, descriptions, availability/enabled state where meaningful, and a way to distinguish authoritative settled results from pending discovery. Existing provider change events should trigger completion refresh and open-file revalidation.

Open decision: when explicit `target` disagrees with the active harness, determine which session/provider supplies dynamic inventory. Schema selection and inventory selection should not silently diverge.

## Diagnostics behavior

- Mark unsupported or authoritative-unknown values with `MarkerTag.Unnecessary` and a harness-specific explanation.
- Do not diagnose against a partial, stale, pending, or failed inventory as if it were complete.
- Surface provider failures explicitly rather than returning an empty success-shaped inventory.
- Preserve authored values that the runtime intentionally accepts for forward compatibility.

## Testing

Cover:

- Inventory pending, settled, refreshed, and failed states.
- Active harness switching and explicit `target` overrides.
- Models/tools/skills appearing and disappearing while a file is open.
- Disabled versus unknown values.
- MCP inventories without triggering connection/authentication side effects.
- Completion, hover, marker tags, and diagnostic messages for each authoritative value source.
- Local behavior remaining unchanged.

Follow-up to #342854.
"}

- Include provider-native tools, client-provided tools, MCP tools/server namespaces, supported aliases, and wildcard forms.

Prefer narrow optional APIs on `ICustomizationItemProvider` (or another harness-owned capability) rather than coupling language providers to agent-host state internals. Candidate capabilities include:
- Existing customization inventory for skills and other customization references

Returned entries should include stable identifiers, descriptions, availability/enabled state where meaningful, and a way to distinguish authoritative settled results from pending discovery. Existing provider change events should trigger completion refresh and open-file revalidation.

Open decision: when explicit `target` disagrees with the active harness, determine which session/provider supplies dynamic inventory. Schema selection and inventory selection should not silently diverge.
- Mark unsupported or authoritative-unknown values with `MarkerTag.Unnecessary` and a harness-specific explanation.
- Do not diagnose against a partial, stale, pending, or failed inventory as if it were complete.
- Surface provider failures explicitly rather than returning an empty success-shaped inventory.
- Preserve authored values that the runtime intentionally accepts for forward compatibility.
- Inventory pending, settled, refreshed, and failed states.
- Active harness switching and explicit `target` overrides.
- Models/tools/skills appearing and disappearing while a file is open.
- MCP inventories without triggering connection/authentication side effects.
- Completion, hover, marker tags, and diagnostic messages for each authoritative value source.

Hey VS Code team! 👋

I really like the new /vscode-pet feature. It’s a fun little addition that brings some personality to the coding experience.

I was thinking it would be awesome if we could take it a step further by adding small, playable mini-games that we can enjoy during breaks without leaving VS Code.

Some ideas that could be fun:

🐍 Snake — The classic game where you control a snake and collect food.
🧱 Tetris — A simple block-stacking puzzle game.
🏎️ Mini Racing Game — A small pixel-art car dodging obstacles or racing on a simple track.
🏓 Pong — A quick game of classic paddle and ball.
🐦 Flappy Bird-style Game — A simple side-scrolling game.
🐾 Take Care of Your Pet — Feed the pet, play with it, give it treats, and take care of its needs. Maybe the pet could have simple moods or reactions depending on how you interact with it.
The games could use the same playful, pixel-art style as the existing pet and run in a small, lightweight view or panel.

Maybe they could even be launched directly from the pet, with something like a small “Play” action.

The idea isn’t to turn VS Code into a gaming platform, but to add a few lightweight games for quick breaks while coding.

I think this could make the pet feature even more engaging and give developers another fun way to interact with VS Code.

What do you think? Would you enjoy having mini-games built into the VS Code pet feature? 🎮🐾"}

body: <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
I really like the new /vscode-pet feature. It’s a fun little addition that brings some personality to the coding experience.
I was thinking it would be awesome if we could take it a step further by adding small, playable mini-games that we can enjoy during breaks without leaving VS Code.
Some ideas that could be fun:
🐍 Snake — The classic game where you control a snake and collect food.
🧱 Tetris — A simple block-stacking puzzle game.
🏎️ Mini Racing Game — A small pixel-art car dodging obstacles or racing on a simple track.
🏓 Pong — A quick game of classic paddle and ball.
🐦 Flappy Bird-style Game — A simple side-scrolling game.
🐾 Take Care of Your Pet — Feed the pet, play with it, give it treats, and take care of its needs. Maybe the pet could have simple moods or reactions depending on how you interact with it.
The games could use the same playful, pixel-art style as the existing pet and run in a small, lightweight view or panel.
Maybe they could even be launched directly from the pet, with something like a small “Play” action.
The idea isn’t to turn VS Code into a gaming platform, but to add a few lightweight games for quick breaks while coding.
I think this could make the pet feature even more engaging and give developers another fun way to interact with VS Code.
What do you think? Would you enjoy having mini-games built into the VS Code pet feature? 🎮🐾

{"body":" Type: Bug Environment: macOS, VS Code 1.142.0. Server: https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp Copilot session: reports “requires authentication”; clicking Authenticate does not open a browser. Local session: the same Atlassian MCP configuration works reliably. Log evidence: VS Code successfully authenticated and discovered 32 tools, but the agent continued reporting “still requires authentication.” ### Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS, open VS Code **1.142.0** with the Atlassian MCP server configured: ```json "com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp" } ``` 2. In a **Copilot** session (Copilot SDK), attempt to use Atlassian MCP. 3. The chat displays: > The MCP server com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server requires authentication. Authenticate? 4. Click **Authenticate**. 5. **Nothing visibly happens:** no browser window opens, and Atlassian remains unavailable. ### Troubleshooting attempted — problem persists 6. Open the Command Palette using **Cmd+Shift+P**. 7. Run **MCP: List Servers**. 8. Select **com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server** and restart it, using **Restart Server** or **Stop Server → Start Server**. 9. Complete any authentication prompted through the MCP server controls rather than the chat card. 10. Start a **new Copilot chat** and retry Atlassian. 11. The authentication problem persists. The above restart/authentication/new-chat sequence was followed without resolving the issue. ### Expected result Clicking **Authenticate** should complete authentication—opening a browser if necessary—and make the Atlassian tools available to the Copilot session. ### Actual result and log evidence Clicking **Authenticate** does not open a browser, and the Copilot session continues to require authentication. Logs from the same VS Code run show: - **15:18:37:** Atlassian browser sign-in completed successfully. - **15:18:38:** VS Code connected to Atlassian and discovered **32 tools**. - **15:20:02:** The Copilot session still reported that authentication was required. - **15:22:04:** The agent reported: > MCP server "com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server" still requires authentication ### Working comparison / workaround 12. In the same VS Code installation, leave the Atlassian MCP configuration unchanged. 13. Open **New Chat (+)**. 14. Change **Session Target** from **Copilot** to **Local**, leaving the agent mode as **Agent**. 15. Attempt to use Atlassian MCP. **Result:** Atlassian works reliably in the **Local** session. This appears specific to the Copilot SDK session’s authentication path; the same server configuration works in Local sessions. - Fast launches (~1-2s until CDP is ready), incremental profile copies, optional run-directory reuse.
- Robust argument passing, no hang when capturing output, unique run directories with automatic cleanup, and a cross-platform cleanup that stops the recorded process tree.

- Arguments are passed through `cmd.exe` (`code.bat`), so paths or titles with `&` or `%` break.
- A PowerShell caller that captures the output hangs until Code OSS exits, because Electron inherits the capture pipe.
- Run directories can collide, are never garbage collected, and cleanup matches processes by command line (8-14s).

## Expected

- One TypeScript launcher core with thin PowerShell/bash wrappers.
- Fast launches (~1-2s until CDP is ready), incremental profile copies, optional run-directory reuse.
- Robust argument passing, no hang when capturing output, unique run directories with automatic cleanup, and a cross-platform cleanup that stops the recorded process tree.
"}

{"body":"## Feature request

Track the experiment and rollout for `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showPickerHint`.

The optional picker footer improves discovery of Agent bake off by showing **Send Query to Multiple Models** at the bottom of the model picker. It gives users a second, explicit entry point in addition to the Compare Models tab-bar toggle.

## Expected behavior

- Keep the setting disabled by default and controlled through experimentation.
- When enabled, show the **Send Query to Multiple Models** footer action while model comparison is available.
- Include the user's resolved `sessions.compareModels` keybinding in the action label when configured.
- Open comparison setup without selecting a single model.
- Keep the Compare Models tab-bar toggle available regardless of whether the footer hint is enabled.
- Preserve the existing **Add Models...** action and single-model picker behavior.

## Tracking

Setting: `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showPickerHint`

Implemented by #342656.
"}

{"body":"[Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-3110) ## [CVE-2026-110672](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57419) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110672))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a duplicate key or a missing colon in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a duplicate key or a missing colon in decode_hv. A quoted key of 24 or more bytes, or one containing a non-ASCII byte or an escape sequence, is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key or, from 4.09, for a duplicate key. Duplicate keys are an error unless allow_dupkeys, dupkeys_as_arrayref or relaxed is set. A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/532b53cf8d2ca5ab6bc24048325566d1f7132425.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110673](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/56996) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110673))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag. With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth. A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/995eb484a9351753e2a8ec3317918b5b4a4e086a.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110687](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57046) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110687))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.43 before 4.80 for Perl misorder byte-string keys during canonical encoding in utf16_cmp Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.43 before 4.80 for Perl misorder byte-string keys during canonical encoding in utf16_cmp. canonical sorts keys by UTF-16 code units. When any key in a hash is UTF-8 flagged, every key is decoded as UTF-8 for the comparison, including byte-string keys that the encoder writes out as Latin-1 characters. A byte-string key whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is sorted out of order, and two keys that encode differently can compare equal and are left in hash order. The same data can encode to different canonical documents across processes.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/bb9da30b67f637f4d57922f0e043376363f28f0c.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110682](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57081) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110682))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.42 before 4.80 for Perl let input chunking change the decoded value of top-level numbers in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.42 before 4.80 for Perl let input chunking change the decoded value of top-level numbers in incr_parse. allow_nonref is enabled by default and incr_parse inherits it. A top-level number, true, false or null has no closing delimiter, so the incremental parser decodes whatever has arrived. The bytes 12 decode as one value when read together, but as 1 and then 2 when split across two reads. A peer that can influence read boundaries can change how many messages a stream consumer decodes and what values they carry.

{"body":"<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured.
- VS Code Version: Insiders, commit `087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`, built 2026-10-20.
- OS Version: macOS, exact version not captured.
- Feature: Agents window > Customizations > Migration.
- Selected model: Not applicable.
- Logs: Agent Host debug export analyzed locally. The bundle is not attached because it contains sensitive session data.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open Customizations > Migration with user prompt files eligible for migration.
2. Open a prompt's context menu, choose Delete, and confirm.
3. Check the migration list. The deleted prompt can remain listed and still offer Delete.

Expected: Deleting a prompt removes its row and updates the migration counts.

Actual: The file is removed from disk, but the list can retain the row, making deletion appear unsuccessful. Repeating Delete can show another confirmation for the same prompt.

### Observed evidence

On October 20, local log timestamps show:

- 08:42:01: Delete confirmation for one prompt, followed by migration recomputation and a user-data filesystem change.
- 08:42:10: Delete confirmation for another prompt, followed by another filesystem change and multiple migration recomputations.
- 08:42:15 and 08:42:22: Delete confirmations appear again for the second prompt.

Both prompt files were absent on disk when checked after the capture. No matching filesystem-delete error appears in the renderer logs.

### RCA

A cancellation race was reproduced using the current source methods with controlled discovery timing. The relevant source matches the reported Insiders commit.

- [deleteCustomizationFile](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L2338) deletes the file and refreshes Migration. An immediate refresh can still read pre-delete discovery results before watcher invalidation.
- [refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1357) cancels the previous refresh when another invalidation arrives.
- [listPromptFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts#L377) shares an in-flight promise tied to its first caller's cancellation token. The replacement refresh can inherit that cancelled scan even though its own token remains live.
- [computeCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1475) ignores the resulting cancellation, leaving the previous rows without an error state or retry.

The controlled reproduction verified that both computations exit without applying updated candidates, while the replacement request's token is not cancelled. The logs are consistent with this race but do not record discovery cancellation directly, so attribution of this specific occurrence remains likely rather than conclusive. No live UI reproduction or fix validation was performed.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._"}

body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. The rendering happens in core chat (`ChatContentMarkdownRenderer`), so any chat response that contains such a table is affected.
- Surface: Agents window (Copilot CLI agent). The same code path renders every chat response.

When a chat response contains a markdown table with `
` inside a cell, the `
` is shown as literal text instead of a line break. A multi-line cell ends up as one paragraph full of `
` tags.

Models emit `
` here on purpose. GFM table cells cannot contain newlines, so `
` is the de facto way to break lines in a cell, and GitHub renders it that way.
1. Open a chat (I used the Agents window) and send:
> Can you give me a table of content about the 5 highest GDP countries. In the last column, give a few bullet points describing some demographic info like population size etc

2. The model answers with a table whose last column uses `
` between bullets (row reconstructed from the rendered output):
| Rank | Country | Nominal GDP (2026 est.) | GDP per capita (approx.) | Demographics |

| 1 | 🇺🇸 United States | ~$31.8T | ~$93,000 | • Population: about 342M, the 3rd largest in the world
• Median age: about 39
• About 83% of people live in cities
• Still growing slowly, mostly through immigration |
**Expected:** each `•` bullet starts on its own line within the cell, as on GitHub.
> • Population: about 342M, the 3rd largest in the world<br>• Median age: about 39<br>• About 83% of people live in cities<br>• Still growing slowly, mostly through immigration
Every row in the table is affected. The issue reproduces deterministically without a model:

const md = new MarkdownString('| a | b |\n| --- | --- |\n| x | one
two |');
chatContentMarkdownRenderer.render(md, { markedOptions: { gfm: true, breaks: true } });

1. Chat renders agent markdown **without** `supportHtml` (correctly, because the content is untrusted), and [`getChatMarkdownRenderOptions`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentMarkdownRenderer.ts) sets `sanitizerConfig.replaceWithPlaintext: true`.

2. marked lexes `
` in a table cell as an inline `html` token. In [`createMarkdownRenderer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/browser/markdownRenderer.ts), when `supportHtml` is off, `renderer.html` returns `escape(text)`, which produces `<br>`.
3. `br` is already in `allowedChatMarkdownHtmlTags`, so the sanitizer would accept it, but it is escaped before reaching the sanitizer.

Outside tables, chat already sets `breaks: true`, so a plain newline becomes `
` and models have no reason to write the tag. Table cells are the one place where `
` is the only way to get a line break.

A second, latent issue affects any fix built on marked's `walkTokens` hook. While a response is streaming (`fillInIncompleteTokens: true`), `renderMarkdown` calls `marked.lexer()` and `marked.parser()` directly, and those skip extension `walkTokens` hooks, whereas `marked.parse()` runs them. Such a fix would therefore show the literal `
` during streaming and the correct rendering only after the response completes.

- Add a table-scoped marked extension to the chat render options. Its `walkTokens` hook turns inline `html` tokens that are exactly `
`, `
`, or `
` (case-insensitive, including inside `**bold**`, links, and other nested inline tokens) into marked's native `br` token.
- In `renderMarkdown`, run `walkTokens` on the `fillInIncompleteTokens` path to match `marked.parse()`, so streaming and final rendering agree.

- `` `
` `` inside code spans and fenced code blocks stays literal.

- The output is a plain `
` without attributes, which the sanitizer already allows for chat.

body: In a long-standing copilot chat my MCPs Error the moment I click start with no output. In a fresh chat the MCPs all start fine and are usable.
Installed/launched a fresh copy of VS Code.
The fresh app restored the existing chat history and allowed messages to be sent successfully.
MCP failures persisted when switching to the existing SPARCK conversation.
Tested MCP functionality in a new chat.
Successfully fetched Jira issues, confirming that at least the Jira integration could work in a fresh chat.
Compared behavior between new and existing conversations.
In a fresh chat, MCPs showed as running and could successfully fetch Jira issues.
In SPARCK, MCPs initially showed as running, but failed when invoked and then stopped or errored during startup.
The SPARCK conversation itself continued to send and receive messages.
Inspected GitHub Copilot Chat and Agent Host logs.
Cannot start an MCP server because the session runtime is no longer available.
Observed ProtocolServer subscription failures with Resource not found for ahp-chat://subagent/... resources associated with the affected session.
Observed a session configuration refresh with reason=clientPluginsChanged, followed by SDK session shutdown and resumption.
The SDK resume reported outcome=success, and the built-in GitHub MCP subsequently reached connected (ready) in the log. Despite this, subsequent MCP tool invocations in SPARCK still failed.
Changed Chat > MCP > Autostart from newAndOutdated to onlyNew.
Retested the affected conversation; this did not resolve the issue.
The setting can be returned to its original default, newAndOutdated.
Chat > MCP: Access was set to all.
GitHub's built-in MCP support was enabled.
Inspected the chat's Tool Sets menu; it offered options to create a tool set, but no existing tool set was available to inspect.

Opened Agent Debug Logs, but the view prompted to enable logging in Settings, and searching Settings for agentDebugLog returned no matching setting. No additional debug logs were obtained through that view.
After the Jira MCP tool became unavailable in SPARCK, the agent attempted a direct Jira REST API request and received 401 Unauthorized.
This does not establish that the MCP's own authentication is broken, since the failure occurred on the direct REST API attempt.

body: <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

When viewing a Markdown document in Preview mode, have the Outline view display the table of contents exactly the same way it already does in Text Editor mode and Markdown Editor mode. It currently instead displays "The active editor cannot provide outline information."
This feature was previously requested in May 2026 but only got 16 of the 20 required votes: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316113

So I'm creating this new issue to try again to get 20 votes, because this is really important for navigating long documents when using VS Code for reading Markdown (like the many Markdown documents that LLM's create).
Note that this issue was recently provided (literally last week) for Markdown Editor mode: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328567

I tried using Markdown Editor mode, but it is not suitable because I want to basic viewing things like scroll downwards and upwards with the arrow keys or with space and shift+space, and Markdown Editor doesn't support any of those, even when in non-edit mode. In non-edit mode, pressing any navigation key just triggers a visual "shine" effect on the lock/edit toggle in the top-right corner. So it is completely broken as a basic viewer.

body: Compare Agents must not be offered when Dev Container execution is selected. Normal composer drafts explicitly require container execution, but comparison creates fresh sessions without carrying that requirement. Hiding the comparison controls and rejecting stale comparison sends is the intentional interim behavior; a normal single-agent request remains available.
The comparison launch architecture may change soon, so defer full container integration rather than expanding that path in the Environment picker PR.
- Carry explicit container execution intent through the comparison lifecycle and persisted state, including attempts, Judge/retries, and synthesis.

- Reuse the existing experimental container-worktree path (`chat.agentHost.devContainer.worktree.enabled`) where supported; preserve independent worktree isolation and never fall back to source-host or shared-folder execution.
- Preserve comparison attribution, participant identity/grouping, models, and permissions across the source-to-container session handoff. Validate access to attempt evidence from the Judge.
- Cover unsupported capabilities, partial launch failures, cancellation, reload/retry, and container/worktree cleanup.
- Restore comparison availability only for supported combinations; Dev Container samples currently do not support the worktree combination.

Selecting Dev Container removes comparison setup and clears an existing comparison selection once configuration settles. Returning to a compatible non-container destination restores comparison availability under its existing gates. Stale comparison sends report an explicit error instead of launching on the host.

{"body":"Follow-up to #342686.

## Current limitation

Compare Agents must not be offered when Dev Container execution is selected. Normal composer drafts explicitly require container execution, but comparison creates fresh sessions without carrying that requirement. Hiding the comparison controls and rejecting stale comparison sends is the intentional interim behavior; a normal single-agent request remains available.

The comparison launch architecture may change soon, so defer full container integration rather than expanding that path in the Environment picker PR.

## Follow-up scope

- Carry explicit container execution intent through the comparison lifecycle and persisted state, including attempts, Judge/retries, and synthesis.
- Reuse the existing experimental container-worktree path (`chat.agentHost.devContainer.worktree.enabled`) where supported; preserve independent worktree isolation and never fall back to source-host or shared-folder execution.
- Preserve comparison attribution, participant identity/grouping, models, and permissions across the source-to-container session handoff. Validate access to attempt evidence from the Judge.
- Cover unsupported capabilities, partial launch failures, cancellation, reload/retry, and container/worktree cleanup.
- Restore comparison availability only for supported combinations; Dev Container samples currently do not support the worktree combination.

## Expected interim UX

Selecting Dev Container removes comparison setup and clears an existing comparison selection once configuration settles. Returning to a compatible non-container destination restores comparison availability under its existing gates. Stale comparison sends report an explicit error instead of launching on the host."}

request.text:
{"body":"## Summary

An Agent Plugin (OpenPlugin-style `plugin.json` that declares `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `rules` through `paths` + `exclusive`, with its content under a `com.github.copilot/` folder) works end to end in the **VS Code Local harness**: hooks run, MCP servers start, instructions load. The same installed plugin does **not** behave the same in:

1. VS Code **Copilot harness** (Copilot SDK / Agent Host)
2. **Copilot CLI**
3. **GitHub Copilot Desktop / Agents window**

Each surface seems to use its own plugin loader and its own hook format, so a plugin cannot be authored once and behave the same everywhere.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.142.x, GitHub Copilot Chat extension, Windows 11
- Copilot CLI 1.0.x
- Plugin installed from a marketplace into `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>`

## Observed behavior

| Capability | VS Code Local | Copilot harness (SDK / Agent Host) | Copilot CLI | Desktop / Agents window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hooks discovered | yes | yes (Customizations > Hook Discovery Results lists every file as loaded) | `/hooks` shows nothing from the plugin | not verified |
| Hooks executed | yes | **no** | **no** | not verified |
| Plugin MCP servers | yes | not started automatically | not verified | not shown |
| Plugin instructions / rules | yes | not loaded | n/a | not verified |
| Custom hook path (`hooks.paths`, `exclusive`) | honored | unclear | appears ignored | unclear |

## Likely causes (partly from reading existing issues, not all verified)

- **Different hook schemas.** The Copilot harness appears to honor only Copilot-style entries (`bash` / `powershell`) and ignore VS Code-style entries (`command` with `windows` / `linux` / `osx`). See #342664.
- **Non-standard plugin layout.** The Copilot CLI documents plugin hooks as `hooks.json` or `hooks/hooks.json` inside the installed plugin directory. A hooks file reached only through `plugin.json` `hooks.paths` (for example under `com.github.copilot/`) is not found, so `/hooks` stays empty. See #334153 for the same `com.github.copilot` layout problem.
- **Discovery is not execution.** The harness reports a hook file as loaded, but nothing runs. There is no log or UI signal explaining why. See #302865, #302350 and #342022.
- **Plugin MCP servers and agents.** Plugin-owned MCP servers are not auto-started in Agent Host (#342860); custom agents are not picked up (#342085); `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` is not expanded for canonical schema plugins (#335006).
- **Plugin source mismatch.** The Copilot harness only reads installs under `~/.copilot/installed-plugins` (#342671), and plugin sync can fail on some setups (#341862).
- **Instructions.** How instructions and `applyTo` rules are loaded in the Copilot harness is unclear (#342595).

## Expected behavior

A plugin that installs correctly should expose the same hooks, MCP servers, instructions and agents in every client, or the docs should state exactly which manifest fields and hook formats each client supports.

## Requests

1. Document, per client (Local, Copilot harness / Agent Host, Copilot CLI, Desktop), which `plugin.json` fields are honored: `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `rules`, `paths`, `exclusive`, and the `com.github.copilot/` folder convention.
2. Accept both hook entry formats (`command` plus per-OS overrides, and `bash` / `powershell`) in every client, or log a clear warning when an entry is skipped.
3. When a hook is discovered but cannot run, surface the reason in the Hook Discovery Results view and in the output channel.
4. Make Copilot CLI `/hooks` list hooks contributed by installed plugins, including those declared through `plugin.json`.
5. Provide a single supported way to declare plugin MCP servers and instructions that all clients load.

## Related issues

microsoft/vscode: #342664, #342022, #302865, #302350, #334153, #342860, #342085, #335006, #342671, #342595, #341862
github/copilot-cli: #4629, #4520
"}

body: An Agent Plugin (OpenPlugin-style `plugin.json` that declares `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `rules` through `paths` + `exclusive`, with its content under a `com.github.copilot/` folder) works end to end in the **VS Code Local harness**: hooks run, MCP servers start, instructions load. The same installed plugin does **not** behave the same in:
1. VS Code **Copilot harness** (Copilot SDK / Agent Host)
Each surface seems to use its own plugin loader and its own hook format, so a plugin cannot be authored once and behave the same everywhere.
- VS Code 1.142.x, GitHub Copilot Chat extension, Windows 11
- Plugin installed from a marketplace into `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>`
| Capability | VS Code Local | Copilot harness (SDK / Agent Host) | Copilot CLI | Desktop / Agents window |
| Hooks discovered | yes | yes (Customizations > Hook Discovery Results lists every file as loaded) | `/hooks` shows nothing from the plugin | not verified |
| Plugin MCP servers | yes | not started automatically | not verified | not shown |
| Plugin instructions / rules | yes | not loaded | n/a | not verified |
| Custom hook path (`hooks.paths`, `exclusive`) | honored | unclear | appears ignored | unclear |
## Likely causes (partly from reading existing issues, not all verified)

- **Different hook schemas.** The Copilot harness appears to honor only Copilot-style entries (`bash` / `powershell`) and ignore VS Code-style entries (`command` with `windows` / `linux` / `osx`). See #342664.

- **Non-standard plugin layout.** The Copilot CLI documents plugin hooks as `hooks.json` or `hooks/hooks.json` inside the installed plugin directory. A hooks file reached only through `plugin.json` `hooks.paths` (for example under `com.github.copilot/`) is not found, so `/hooks` stays empty. See #334153 for the same `com.github.copilot` layout problem.
- **Discovery is not execution.** The harness reports a hook file as loaded, but nothing runs. There is no log or UI signal explaining why. See #302865, #302350 and #342022.

- **Plugin MCP servers and agents.** Plugin-owned MCP servers are not auto-started in Agent Host (#342860); custom agents are not picked up (#342085); `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` is not expanded for canonical schema plugins (#335006).
- **Plugin source mismatch.** The Copilot harness only reads installs under `~/.copilot/installed-plugins` (#342671), and plugin sync can fail on some setups (#341862).
- **Instructions.** How instructions and `applyTo` rules are loaded in the Copilot harness is unclear (#342595).

A plugin that installs correctly should expose the same hooks, MCP servers, instructions and agents in every client, or the docs should state exactly which manifest fields and hook formats each client supports.

1. Document, per client (Local, Copilot harness / Agent Host, Copilot CLI, Desktop), which `plugin.json` fields are honored: `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `rules`, `paths`, `exclusive`, and the `com.github.copilot/` folder convention.
2. Accept both hook entry formats (`command` plus per-OS overrides, and `bash` / `powershell`) in every client, or log a clear warning when an entry is skipped.
3. When a hook is discovered but cannot run, surface the reason in the Hook Discovery Results view and in the output channel.
4. Make Copilot CLI `/hooks` list hooks contributed by installed plugins, including those declared through `plugin.json`.
5. Provide a single supported way to declare plugin MCP servers and instructions that all clients load.

body: **Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider (20f16aa5, 2026-10-19), remote agent host over SSH, Copilot CLI provider. Client: macOS. Host: Linux.
When a remote agent-host session's customizations are listed, the remote host gets `resourceResolve` requests for the **client's** local plugin folders, and they fail:
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=29 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/agents
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=30 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/skills
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=31 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/commands
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=32 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/rules
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=33 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.copilot/installed-plugins/azure-exp/azure-exp/agents

On the client, the same requests appear as `[RemoteAgentHostProtocol] Request N failed: {"code":-32008,"message":"Resource not found: file:///Users/..."}`. Each run sends 4 folders × 2 client plugins, twice (16 requests). It repeats every time the customizations are refreshed.

Client-synced plugins (`customization.clientId !== undefined`) keep their original client-side URI (`file:///Users/...`). In `AgentCustomizationItemProvider.toRemoteUri` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentCustomizationItemProvider.ts`), only the synthetic synced bundle (`SYNCED_CUSTOMIZATION_SCHEME`) is left alone. Every other URI goes through `toAgentHostUri(original, connectionAuthority)`, including client-synced plugins:

`provideChatSessionCustomizations` then passes that URI to `AgentCustomizationContentExpander.expandPluginContents`. It assumes the URI is a remote root and resolves `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/` and `rules/` through the agent-host filesystem, which points at the remote machine. Those paths exist only on the client.

- The expansion fails quietly and returns `[]`, so the remote session's customization listing can't include those plugins' children. In this repro, `github-inbox` has 7 agents and 12 skills on the client and `azure-exp` has 4 skills, and none of them can be enumerated through the remote host.
- Each refresh sends useless round trips to the remote host, and both host and client log them as errors.

For client-synced customizations (`clientId` set), don't wrap with `toAgentHostUri`. Resolve them against the client's own filesystem, for example by keeping the original `file:` URI, or through whatever the synced-bundle path uses. The same applies to the other `toRemoteUri` call sites for client-owned items (`toItem`, children, `provideCustomAgents`).

{"body":"**Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider (20f16aa5, 2026-10-19), remote agent host over SSH, Copilot CLI provider. Client: macOS. Host: Linux.

### Symptom

When a remote agent-host session's customizations are listed, the remote host gets `resourceResolve` requests for the **client's** local plugin folders, and they fail:

```
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=29 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/agents
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=30 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/skills
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=31 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/commands
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=32 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/rules
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=33 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.copilot/installed-plugins/azure-exp/azure-exp/agents
...
```

On the client, the same requests appear as `[RemoteAgentHostProtocol] Request N failed: {"code":-32008,"message":"Resource not found: file:///Users/..."}`. Each run sends 4 folders × 2 client plugins, twice (16 requests). It repeats every time the customizations are refreshed.

### Cause

Client-synced plugins (`customization.clientId !== undefined`) keep their original client-side URI (`file:///Users/...`). In `AgentCustomizationItemProvider.toRemoteUri` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentCustomizationItemProvider.ts`), only the synthetic synced bundle (`SYNCED_CUSTOMIZATION_SCHEME`) is left alone. Every other URI goes through `toAgentHostUri(original, connectionAuthority)`, including client-synced plugins:

```ts
private toRemoteUri(customizationUri: string): URI {
	const original = URI.parse(customizationUri);
	if (original.scheme === SYNCED_CUSTOMIZATION_SCHEME) {
		return original;
	}
	return toAgentHostUri(original, this._connectionAuthority);
}
```

`provideChatSessionCustomizations` then passes that URI to `AgentCustomizationContentExpander.expandPluginContents`. It assumes the URI is a remote root and resolves `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/` and `rules/` through the agent-host filesystem, which points at the remote machine. Those paths exist only on the client.

### Impact

- The expansion fails quietly and returns `[]`, so the remote session's customization listing can't include those plugins' children. In this repro, `github-inbox` has 7 agents and 12 skills on the client and `azure-exp` has 4 skills, and none of them can be enumerated through the remote host.
- Each refresh sends useless round trips to the remote host, and both host and client log them as errors.

### Suggested fix

For client-synced customizations (`clientId` set), don't wrap with `toAgentHostUri`. Resolve them against the client's own filesystem, for example by keeping the original `file:` URI, or through whatever the synced-bundle path uses. The same applies to the other `toRemoteUri` call sites for client-owned items (`toItem`, children, `provideCustomAgents`).
"}

{"body":"**Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider, Copilot CLI agent host (local and remote)

### Problem

`CopilotAgentSession` logs this at **info** for every `assistant.message` event (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts`, in the `wrapper.onMessage` handler):

```ts
this._logService.info(`[Copilot:${sessionId}] Full message received: ${e.data.content.length} chars`);
```

Almost all of these lines say `0 chars`, because most model replies in an agent loop only call tools and contain no text. From a real overnight remote agent host log:

- `Full message received` made up **15,329 of 75,912 lines (20%)**.
- **14,528 (95%)** of those were `0 chars`.
- After a 0-char line, the next event for the same session is almost always `Tool started: …`. So the line adds nothing beyond the tool-start line that follows.

Costs:

- **Log retention**: the host log rotates by size. During that run, one rotated file covered only about 73 minutes, which made it hard to piece together an overnight incident afterwards.
- **It hides the case it should catch**: a truly empty reply (no text and no tool calls, i.e. the "no response" case) logs exactly the same as a normal tool-only reply.
- **The useful fields aren't logged**: `AssistantMessageData` already has `toolRequests`, `model`, `outputTokens`, `serviceRequestId` / `apiCallId`, and the event has `agentId` (main agent or subagent). None of these appear in the log, so you can't tell which agent replied or trace a bad reply on the service side.

### Suggested change

- Log tool-only replies (`content === ''` and `toolRequests?.length > 0`) at **trace**.
- Log other replies at **info** in one richer line, for example:
  `Model response: agent=<root|sub:agentId> model=<model> chars=<n> tools=<m> outTokens=<k> requestId=<serviceRequestId>`
- Make truly empty replies (no content, no `toolRequests`, last chunk) easy to find, for example `empty response` at info or warn. Chunked messages and model-less synthetic root messages, which the handler already detects, may need to be left out.
"}

After installing today’s VS Code updates, GitHub Copilot’s speech-to-text no longer works.

Expected result:
Spoken words should be transcribed into the Copilot Chat prompt.

Impact:
Voice input is unusable in GitHub Copilot Chat.
"}

{"body":"- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.70.0 (built-in, VS Code 1.142.0)
- VS Code Version: 1.142.0 (commit 6d62b1d5dace93a33b3a6d3eca1317bd5e15bcb1, 2026-10-15)
- OS Version: macOS <fill in> client, Remote-SSH to Linux (RHEL 9, kernel 5.14)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode, Copilot (Agent Host) harness
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Claude Opus 5.5
- Logs: `resource` context key included below

### Summary
This only happens with the **Copilot (Agent Host)** harness. In the same Remote-SSH window, with the same workspace and files, file links from a **Local harness** chat open the workspace file and reveal in the Explorer as expected. I have not tested other harnesses (Copilot CLI, Claude, Codex) or a non-remote window.

With the Copilot (Agent Host) harness, file links in a chat response open through a `vscode-agent-host://` URI. They never resolve to the workspace's `vscode-remote://` URI. The editor shows the file contents, but VS Code does not treat it as a workspace file:
- **Reveal in Explorer View** does nothing.
- The breadcrumb shows the full absolute path, not a path relative to the workspace folder.
- The tab is a separate resource from the copy opened via the Explorer. Language features from remote extensions (Go, Python) may not attach to it.

The Local harness writes workspace-relative links (e.g. `src/server/handler.go#L81-L92`), which resolve against the workspace folder.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Connect to an SSH host with Remote-SSH and open a folder, e.g. `/home/user/project`. The workspace folder URI is `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+my-host/home/user/project`.
2. Start a Copilot (Agent Host) chat and ask about a file, so the response contains a markdown link with an absolute path, e.g. `[handler.go](/home/user/project/src/server/handler.go)`.
3. Click the link. The file opens.
4. Right-click the editor tab and choose **Reveal in Explorer View**. Nothing happens.
5. Run **Developer: Toggle Developer Tools**, then **Developer: Inspect Context Keys**, and click in the editor. The console shows:

```
"resource": "vscode-agent-host://hex-7673636f64652d72656d6f74653a2f2f7373682d72656d6f74652b6d792d686f7374/home/user/project/src/server/handler.go?_ah%3DeyJzY2hlbWUiOiJmaWxlIn0",
"resourceScheme": "vscode-agent-host",
```

The hex authority decodes to `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+my-host`, and `_ah` decodes to `{"scheme":"file"}`. The Agent Host returns a `file:` URI from the remote side. That URI is then proxied through `vscode-agent-host:` instead of being mapped to the workspace's `vscode-remote:` URI. This happens both for a path that matches the workspace folder exactly and for a path that reaches the same directory through a symlink.

### Expected
The link opens `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+my-host/home/user/project/src/server/handler.go`, the same resource the Explorer uses, and **Reveal in Explorer View** selects the file.

### Other link forms tried (all fail in the Agent Host chat)
| Link written in the response | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Absolute path (`/home/user/project/...`) | Opens as `vscode-agent-host://...`; cannot be revealed in Explorer |
| Workspace-relative (`src/server/handler.go`) | Rendered as plain text, not a link |
| `vscode-remote://ssh-remote+my-host/<abs path>` (also with `%2B`) | Rendered as a link; clicking shows "Unable to open 'handler.go': The editor could not be opened because the file was not found." |

There is no link format the agent can write that opens the workspace resource.

### Suggested fix
When an Agent Host `file:` URI falls under a workspace folder served by the same remote authority, map it to that folder's `vscode-remote:` URI. Also resolve workspace-relative links against the workspace folder, as the Local harness does.

### Workaround
Open the file with **Go to File** (Cmd+P).

### Related
- #342378 (another issue with `vscode-agent-host` resources carrying `_ah` metadata)"}

{"body":"## Bug

With `workbench.browser.openLocalhostLinks` enabled, the Integrated Browser's localhost link opener is consulted before, and separately from, the external URI openers contributed by extensions. As a result, localhost links open in the Integrated Browser even when:

- the user configured another opener for the host in `workbench.externalUriOpeners`, or
- the caller explicitly requested an opener with `allowContributedOpeners: '<opener id>'`.

The Integrated Browser also never appears in the "How would you like to open" prompt.

## Expected

The Integrated Browser is an external URI opener like the others: preferred for localhost links when the setting is enabled, subject to the configured and requested opener, and chosen by the same selection rules.

This also lets one place decide which opener a link uses, which #342544 needs to list the available link handlers.

Part of #342050.
"}

{"body":"With CVE-2026-11194 / https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/ , we have to figure out a way to rotate certificates in all the packages.

The best posture would be for nixpkgs to have a single package / certificate list to update.

I wanted to check how many packages bundle the certificates and need to be patched manually. This list was generated using this scanner: https://github.com/zimbatm/nix-cacert-scan

My proposal:

Go trough this list of packages, and fix it so `cacerts` is passed as an argument.

## Tracking

The list is split into one issue per category. Tick entries and link PRs there. "Ticked" counts entries with a PR or with no change needed, as of 2026-10-20.

| Category | Packages | Ticked | Fix | Tracking |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Vendored PEM bundle | 95 | 5 | Symlink the file to `${cacert}/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt`, or point the program at it | #576541 |
| Bundle inside a wheel, jar or zip | 88 | 2 | Patch the bundle inside the archive at build time, or make the code use the system store | #576542 |
| Java keystore | 37 | 3 | Generate the keystore from `${cacert}` at build time (`jre-generate-cacerts`) | #576543 |
| Compiled into a binary | 663 | 5 | Make the program use the system store, or bump the embedded root list | #576544 |
| **Total** | **883** | **15** | | |
"}

{"body":"Tracking issue for security fixes for [eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/)

Partial mitigation while channels are getting fixes:
```
security.pki.caCertificateBlacklist = [
  # CVE-2026-111943
  "Comodo AAA Services root"
  # https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/projects/nss/rev/26d38a0c3fb81e7fb2acedbaf4c42dd21dce0517
  "emSign ECC Root CA - G3"
  # https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/projects/nss/rev/8159223c48ceeb1273a1915bca95a517294ab0e0
  "emSign Root CA - C1"
  "emSign ECC Root CA - C3"
];
```

This mitigation was also implemented in:
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/576390
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/576401

### Further reading
- https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/
- LWN overview: https://lwn.net/Articles/1101643/
- Mozilla Bug Report (includes report of preliminary investigation): https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2083449#c11
- Mozilla dev-security-policy Mailing List: https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/0R3XLJL6FuE
- Chrome Root Program: https://groups.google.com/a/mozilla.org/g/dev-security-policy/c/0R3XLJL6FuE/m/VAgSvefvAAAJ"}

{"body":"### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Upon switching Darktable from Nixpkgs Stable to Unstable, it fails to launch. It displays the splash screen for a second and then dumps the following to the console:

```
ERROR: something wrong with flag 'flagfile' in file '/build/source/src/gflags.cc'.  One possibility: file '/build/source/src/gflags.cc' is being linked both statically and dynamically into this executable.
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install darktable from Nixpkgs stable
2. Launch and notice no errors
3. Install Darktable from Nixpkgs unstable
4. Launch and notice the programme does not launch with the aforementioned error

### Minimal reproducer

```nix

```

### Expected behaviour

Darktable should launch correctly with no errors

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
ERROR: something wrong with flag 'flagfile' in file '/build/source/src/gflags.cc'.  One possibility: file '/build/source/src/gflags.cc' is being linked both statically and dynamically into this executable.
```

_No response_
